Do you who are sweet-flavoured and beatiful flow (at) our (sacrifice) for Bhaga, Vayu, Pushan, Mitra, and Varuna. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒च्चा ते॑ जा॒तमंध॑सो दि॒वि षद्भूम्या द॑दे ।  
> उ॒ग्रं शर्म॒ महि॒ श्रवः॑ ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उच्चा । ते । जातम् । अंधसः । दिवि । सत् । भूमिः । आ । ददे ।  
> उग्रम् । शर्म । महि । श्रवः ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम ते तव संबंधिनः अंधसः रसस्य उच्चा उपरि जातं जन्म अपि च दिवि द्युलोके सत् विद्यमानं स्वतस्तव संबंधि उग्रम उद्गूर्णं शर्म सुखं महि महत् श्रवः अन्नं च भूमिः आ ददे। भूम्या ददे इति पदत्रयमामनंति । विसर्जनीयलोपः सांहितिकः । भूमिर्भौमा जना मादृशाः । भूमिष्ठैरादीयत इत्यर्थः ॥ ॥ १९ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, the birth of your juice is on high. And, existing in the heavenly world, your own intense happiness and abundant food are taken by the earth, that is, by earth-dwelling people such as we; the meaning is that they are taken by those who live on the earth. One tradition recites the words as three, divided separately.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O divine Soma) ते (*te*)—your
- अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)—for the juice
- उच्चा (*uccā*)—the elevated region
- जातं (*jātaṃ*)—is the place of origin
- दिवि सत् (*divi sat*)—although you are in the heavenly world
- उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)—very great

### Printed p. 186
- शर्म (*śarma*)—happiness
- महि (*mahi*)—great
- श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)—food
- भूमिः (*bhūmiḥ*)—the people of the earth
- आ ददे (*ā dade*)—receive from you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, the elevated region is the place of origin of your juice. Although you are in the heavenly world, the people of the earth receive from you very great happiness and great food.

##### English translation
The birth of your juice is on high : the earth has received (your) intense happiness and abundant food, though (these) exist (naturally) in heaven.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒ना विश्वा॑न्य॒र्य आ द्यु॒म्नानि॒ मानु॑षाणाम् ।  
> सिषा॑संतो वनामहे ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एना । विश्वानि । अर्यः । आ । द्युम्नानि । मानुषाणाम् ।  
> सिसासंतः । वनामहे ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एना एनेनानेन सोमेन मानुषाणां मनुष्याणां विश्वा विश्वानि द्युम्नानि अन्नानि आ अर्यः अभिगच्छंतः सिषासंतः संभक्तुमिच्छंतश्च वयं वनामहे संभजामहे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By this Soma we, approaching all the splendours, the foods of men, and desiring to enjoy them, partake of them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एना (*enā*)—by the favour of this divine Soma
- मानुषाणां (*mānuṣāṇāṃ*)—pleasing to men
- द्युम्नानि (*dyumnāni*)—and shining
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all foods
- आ अर्यः (*ā aryaḥ*)—obtaining fully
- सिषासंतः (*siṣāsaṃtaḥ*)—enjoying them
- वनामहे (*vanāmahe*)—we attain satisfaction

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

By the favour of this divine Soma, we attain satisfaction, obtaining fully all the foods that are pleasing to men and shining, and enjoying them.

### Printed p. 187

##### English translation
By this (Soma) obtaining and desiring to enjoy all the good things that belong to men we enjoy them.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स न॒ इंद्रा॑य॒ यज्य॑वे॒ वरु॑णाय म॒रुद्भ्यः॑ ।  
> व॒रि॒वो॒वित्परि॑ स्रव ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । नः । इंद्राय । यज्यवे । वरुणाय । मरुत्ऽभ्यः ।  
> वरिवःऽवित् । परि । स्रव ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम वरिवोवित् धनस्य लंभकः पवमानस्त्वं नः अस्माकं यज्यवे यष्टव्याय इंद्राय वरुणाय च मरुद्भ्यः  च परि स्रव धारया क्षर ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, winner of wealth, being purified, flow in a stream for us, for the adorable Indra, for Varuṇa and for the Maruts.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O divine Soma) सः वरिवोवित् (*saḥ varivovit*)—you who are rich in wealth
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- यज्यवे (*yajyave*)—for the conduct of the sacrifice
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra
- वरुणाय (*varuṇāya*)—with Varuṇa as the aim
- मरुद्भ्यः (*marudbhyaḥ*)—for the satisfaction of the Maruts
- परि स्रव (*pari srava*)—flow in the form of a stream

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, you who are rich in wealth, flow in a stream for the conduct of our sacrifice, for the satisfaction of Indra, Varuṇa and the Maruts.

##### English translation
O you who are the possessor of wealth flow for us, for the adorable Indra, for Varuna. and the Maruts.

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उपो॒ षु जा॒तम॒प्तुरं॒ गोभि॑र्भं॒गं परि॑ष्कृतम् ।  
> इंदुं॑ दे॒वा अ॑यासिषुः ॥ १३ ॥

### Printed p. 188

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उपो इति । सु । जातम् । अप्ऽतुरम् । गोभिः । भंगम् । परिऽकृतम् ।  
> इंदुम् । देवाः । अयासिषुः ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सु जातं सम्यक्प्रादुर्भूतम् अप्तुरं वसतीवरीभिः प्रेरितं भंगं शत्रूणां भंजकं गोभिः गोविकारैः पयोभिः परिष्कृतम् अलंकृतं संस्कृतम् इंदुं सोमं देवाः इंद्रादयः उप अयासिषुः उपागच्छंति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains: "well born" means fully manifested; the word अप्तुरं (*apturaṃ*) means urged on by the waters called Vasatīvarī; भंगं (*bhaṃgaṃ*) means the breaker of enemies; "with cows" means adorned and refined with the products of the cow, that is, with milk. The gods, Indra and the rest, approach this Indu, Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सु जातं (*su jātaṃ*)—one of excellent origin
- अपुरं (*apuraṃ*)—one joined with the Vasatīvarī waters **NOTE**
- भंगं (*bhaṃgaṃ*)—the destroyer of enemies
- गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)—united with milk and the like
- परिष्कृतं (*pariṣkṛtaṃ*)—one who is refined
- इंदुं (*iṃduṃ*)—Soma, the divine
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods beginning with Indra
- उपो अयासिषुः (*upo ayāsiṣuḥ*)—approach

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The gods beginning with Indra approach the divine Soma, who is of excellent origin, joined with the Vasatīvarī waters, the destroyer of enemies, and refined and well prepared by union with milk and the like.

##### English translation
The gods approach Indu, ( who is ) completely generated, sent forth by the waters, the demolisher (of foes), adorned with milk and curds.

#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य इंद्र॑स्य हृदं॒सनिः॑ ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तम् । इत् । वर्धंतु । नः । गिरः । वत्सम् । संशिश्वरीःऽइव ।  
> यः । इंद्रस्य । हृदम्ऽसनिः ॥ १४ ॥

### Printed p. 189

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यः सोमः इंद्रस्य हृदंसनिः हृदयस्य संभक्ता भवति तमित् तमेव सोमं नः अस्माकं गिरः स्तुतिरूपा वाचः सं वर्धंतु सम्यग्वर्धयंतु । तत्र दृष्टांतः । वत्सं बालं शिश्वरीरिव । यथा शिश्वर्यो बद्धपयस्का मातरो वत्सं वर्धयंति तद्वदित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Soma who is the sharer of Indra's heart, that very Soma may our praises, which are words in the form of eulogy, cause to grow well. An illustration follows: as mothers whose milk is held back, being fond of their young, make the calf grow, so may our praises make Soma grow. This is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शिश्वरीः (*śiśvarīḥ*)—cows rich in milk
- वत्सं इव (*vatsaṃ iva*)—as they lick their calves lovingly and make them thrive
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Soma
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—of Indra
- हृदंसनिः (*hṛdaṃsaniḥ*)—brings satisfaction to the heart
- तमित् (*tamit*)—that very Soma
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—words of praise
- वर्धंतु (*vardhaṃtu*)—(well) let them increase

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As cows rich in milk lick their calves lovingly and make them thrive, so may our words of praise increase that very Soma who brings satisfaction to the heart of Indra.

##### English translation
May our praises foster him who wins the heart of Indra, as cows who have young ones (foster) their calf.

> वर्धा॑ समु॒द्रमु॒क्थ्य॑म् ॥ १५ ॥

> वर्ध । समुद्रम् । उक्थ्यम् ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, flow for our cow, that is, pour out comfort. Moreover, fill up and bring forth abundant, swollen food. And further, increase the water that is praiseworthy, the water.  **NOTE**

- सोम (*soma*)—O divine Soma
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- गवे (*gave*)—for the cows
- शं (*śaṃ*)—happiness
- अर्ष (*arṣa*)—provide

- इषं (*iṣaṃ*)—food

- वर्ध (*vardha*)—increase

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पवमान । रसः । तव । दक्षः । वि । राजति । द्युऽमान् ।  
> ज्योतिः । विश्वम् । स्वः । दृशे ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पवमान सोम तव त्वदीयः दक्षः वृद्धः द्युमान् दीप्तिमान् रसः वि राजति प्रकाशते । न केवलं स्वयमेव प्रकाशते किंतु विश्वं व्याप्तं स्वः सर्वं ज्योतिः तेजश्च दृशे द्रष्टुं करोतीति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Pavamāna Soma, your juice, grown strong and brilliant, shines forth. Not only does it shine of itself, but it also makes the whole pervading light, all radiance, to be seen; the verb "to make" is to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पवमान (*pavamāna*)—O divine Soma
- तव (*tava*)—your
- दक्षः (*dakṣaḥ*)—powerful
- म्यमान् (*myamān*)—radiant **NOTE**
- रसः (*rasaḥ*)—the juice
- वि राजति (*vi rājati*)—shines
- विश्वं (*viśvaṃ*)—all-pervading
- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—all
- ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)—light
- दृशे (*dṛśe*)—so as to be seen by all

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, your juice, which is powerful and radiant, shines forth. It also makes the all-pervading and all-embracing light to be seen by everyone.

##### English translation
Purified Soma, your juice as it increases shines bright; it (makes) a pervading universal light to be seen.

#### Ṛk 19

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यस्ते॒ मदो॒ वरे॑ण्य॒स्तेना॑ पव॒स्वांध॑सा ।  
> दे॒वा॒वीर॑घशंस॒हा ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । ते । मदः । वरेण्यः । तेन । पवस्व । अंधसा ।  
> देवऽअवीः । अघशंसऽहा ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम ते तव देवावीः देवकामः अघशंसहा राक्षसानां हंता वरेण्यः सर्वैर्वरणीयः मदः मदकरः यः रसो विद्यते तेन रसेन अंधसा अदनीयेन पवस्व क्षर ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, whatever juice of yours there is that is desirous of the gods, the slayer of the demons, to be chosen by all and exhilarating, with that juice, that food fit to be eaten, flow forth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ते (*te*)—your
- देवावीः (*devāvīḥ*)—that which desires the company of the gods
- अघशंसहा (*aghaśaṃsahā*)—that which destroys the sinful
- वरेण्यः (*vareṇyaḥ*)—most excellent
- मदः (*madaḥ*)—gladdening
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which juice there is
- तेन (*tena*)—with such
- अंधसा (*aṃdhasā*)—juice
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow in the form of a stream

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, with the juice which desires the company of the gods, destroys the sinful, is most excellent and gladdening, flow in the form of a stream.

##### English translation
Flow forth with that juice of yours which is exhilarating, the best gratifying the gods, the slayer of Rakshasas.

#### Ṛk 20

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> जघ्नि॑र्वृ॒त्रम॑मि॒त्रियं॒ सस्नि॒र्वाजं॑ दि॒वेदि॑वे ।  
> गो॒षा उ॑ अश्व॒सा अ॑सि ॥ २० ॥

> जघ्निः । वृत्रम् । अमित्रियम् । सस्निः । वाजम् । दिवेऽदिवे ।  
> गोऽसाः । ऊं इति । अश्वऽसाः । असि ॥ २० ॥

### Printed p. 194

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम त्वम् अमित्रियम् अमित्रभवं वृत्रं शत्रुं जघ्निः हंता असि भवसि । किंच दिवेदिवे प्रतिदिनं वाजं संग्रामं सस्निः संभक्तासि । किंच गोषाः गवां दातासि । अश्वसाः अश्वानां दाता चासि ॥ ॥ २१ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, you are the slayer of the enemy Vṛtra, the one born of hostility. Further, day by day you are the partaker of the battle. Further, you are the giver of cows and also the giver of horses.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अमित्रियं (*amitriyaṃ*)—who fosters enmity
- वृत्रं (*vṛtraṃ*)—the demon
- जघ्निः (*jaghniḥ*)—as the slayer
- असि (*asi*)—you are
- दिनेदिवे (*dinedive*)—every day **NOTE**
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—the battle
- सस्निः (*sasniḥ*)—you desire
- गोषाः (*goṣāḥ*)—the giver of cows
- अश्वसाः (*aśvasāḥ*)—the giver of horses

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, you destroy the demon who fosters enmity. You desire battle with him every day. You are the giver of cows and the giver of horses.

##### English translation
You are the slayer of the hostile Vritra, the enjoyer of battle day by day, the giver of cows and the giver of horses.

#### Ṛk 21

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सम्मि॑श्लो अरु॒षो भ॑व सूप॒स्थाभि॒र्न धे॒नुभिः॑ ।  
> सीदं॑छ्ये॒नो न योनि॒मा ॥ २१ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सम्ऽमिश्लः । अरुषः । भव । सुऽउपस्थाभिः । न । धेनुऽभिः ।  
> सीदन् । श्येनः । न । योनिम् । आ ॥ २१ ॥

### Printed p. 195

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम त्वं सूपस्थाभिः शोभनोपस्थानाभिः धेनुभिः गोभिः । गोविकारैः पयोभिरित्यर्थः । संमिश्लः संमिश्रितः श्येनो न यथा श्येनः शीघ्रमागत्य स्थानमासीदति तद्वत् योनिं स्वकीयं स्थानम् आ सीदन् । न संप्रत्यर्थे । इदानीम् अरुषः आरोचमानः भव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, mixed with the milch cows of good lap, that is, with the milk, the products of cows, like a falcon that quickly arrives and settles in its place, settle in your own place. Here न (*na*) is used in the sense of "now". Now become resplendent.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सूपस्थाभिः (*sūpasthābhiḥ*)—having an excellent place of refuge
- धेनुभिः (*dhenubhiḥ*)—with milk
- संमिश्लः (*saṃmiślaḥ*)—joined
- श्येनो न (*śyeno na*)—coming swiftly like a falcon
- योनिं (*yoniṃ*)—in your place of sacrifice
- आ सीदन् (*ā sīdan*)—sitting down
- न (*na*)—now
- अरुषः (*aruṣaḥ*)—shining
- भव (*bhava*)—be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, joined with the milk that has an excellent place of refuge, coming swiftly like a falcon and sitting down in your place of sacrifice, be now resplendent.

##### English translation
Be now resplendent, mixed with the supporting (products of the) milch cows, alighting like a falcon on your place.

#### Ṛk 22

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स प॑वस्व॒ य आवि॒थेंद्रं॑ वृ॒त्राय॒ हंत॑वे ।  
> व॒व्रि॒वांसं॑ म॒हीर॒पः ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । पवस्व । यः । आविथ । इंद्रम् । वृत्राय । हंतवे ।  
> वव्रिऽवांसम् । महीः । अपः ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम यः त्वं महीः महतीः अपः महांत्युदकानि वव्रिवांसं निरुंधानं वृत्राय वृत्रं हंतवे हंतुम् इंद्रम् आविथ अरक्षः सः त्वं पवस्व धारया क्षर । सोमं पीत्वा मत्त: सन्निंद्रो महांत्युदकानि निरुंधानं वृत्रं जघानेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, you who helped Indra to slay Vṛtra, who was holding back the great waters, such as you flow in a stream. The meaning is that Indra, having drunk Soma and being exhilarated, slew Vṛtra who was obstructing the great waters.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- महीः (*mahīḥ*)—great
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—waters
- वव्रिवांसं (*vavrivāṃsaṃ*)—who had held back

- आविथ (*āvitha*)—helped

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, you who helped Indra to destroy the demon Vṛtra, who had held back the great waters, such as you flow in the form of a stream.

#### Ṛk 23

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सु॒वीरा॑सो व॒यं धना॒ जये॑म सोम मीढ्वः ।  
> पु॒ना॒नो व॑र्ध नो॒ गिरः॑ ॥ २३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सुऽवीरासः । वयम् । धना । जयेम । सोम । मीढ्वः ।  
> पुनानः । वर्ध । नः । गिरः ॥ २३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुवीरासः सुवीराः कल्याणपुत्राः वयम् अमहीयव आंगिरसाः धना शत्रूणां धनानि जयेम । शत्रून् जित्वा तदीयानि धनानि स्वीकुर्यामेत्यर्थः । हे मीढ्वः सेक्तः सोम पुनानः पूयमानस्त्वं नः अस्माकं गिरः स्तुतिरूपा वाचश्च वर्ध वर्धय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We, the अमहीयव आंगिरसाः (*amahīyava āṃgirasāḥ*), having good sons, would conquer the wealth of our enemies; the meaning is that, having conquered the enemies, we would take possession of their wealth. O Soma, the sprinkler, being purified, increase our words of praise, our speech in the form of eulogy.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मीढ्वः (*mīḍhvaḥ*)—O bestower of desires
- सोम (*soma*)—O divine Soma
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- सुवीरासः (*suvīrāsaḥ*)—accompanied by excellent heroic sons
- धना (*dhanā*)—the wealth of enemies
- जयेम (*jayema*)—may we conquer
- पुनासः (*punāsaḥ*)—you, the purifier **NOTE**
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—words of praise
- वर्ध (*vardha*)—make thrive

### Printed p. 197

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, bestower of desires, may we, accompanied by excellent heroic sons, conquer the wealth of enemies. You, the purifier, make our words of praise thrive.

##### English translation
May we, possessed of excellent male offspring, conquer the wealth (of our enemies), O Soma, the sprinkler; being purified, accept our praises.

#### Ṛk 24

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वोता॑स॒स्तवाव॑सा॒ स्याम॑ व॒न्वंत॑ आ॒मुरः॑ ।  
> सोम॑ व्र॒तेषु॑ जागृहि ॥ २४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वाऽऊतासः । तव । अवसा । स्याम । वन्वंतः । आऽमुरः ।  
> सोम । व्रतेषु । जागृहि ॥ २४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम तव त्वदीयेन अवसा रक्षणेन त्वोतासः त्वया रक्षिताः संतः वन्वंतः शत्रून् भजमानाः आमुरः तेषामभिमारकाः स्याम भवेम । व्रतेषु अस्माकं कर्मसु जागृहि प्रबुद्धो भव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, protected by you, through your protection, may we become those who वन्वंतः (*vanvaṃtaḥ*), that is, who attend upon the enemies, and आमुरः (*āmuraḥ*), their destroyers. Be awake in our rites, be watchful. **NOTE**

- सोम (*soma*)—O divine Soma
- तव (*tava*)—your
- अवसा (*avasā*)—by the protection
- त्वोतासः (*tvotāsaḥ*)—we who are protected
- वन्वंतः (*vanvaṃtaḥ*)—enjoying the wealth of enemies
- आमुरः (*āmuraḥ*)—and their destroyers
- स्याम (*syāma*)—may we become
- व्रतेषु (*vrateṣu*)—in our sacrificial rites
- जागृहि (*jāgṛhi*)—be watchful

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, protected by your protection, may we become enjoyers of the wealth of enemies and their destroyers. Be watchful in our sacrificial rites.

##### English translation
Protected by you, through your protection may we be victorious, slaying (our enemies); be vigilant, Soma, at our sacrificees.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम राधः धनम् आ दित्संतम् आदातुमिच्छंतं त्वा त्वां शतं चन बहवोऽपि ह्रुतः हिंसकाः शत्रवः न मिनन् न हिंसंति । कदेत्यत्राह । यत् यदा पुनानः पूयमानस्त्वं मखस्यसे अस्मभ्यं धनं दातुमिच्छसि । ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, even a hundred violent enemies do not injure you, who wish to give wealth. When is that? When, being purified, you wish to give us wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुनानः (*punānaḥ*)—you, the purifier
- मखस्यसे (*makhasyase*)—you wish to give us wealth, then
- राधः (*rādhaḥ*)—wealth
- आ दित्संतं (*ā ditsaṃtaṃ*)—wishing to give
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- शतंचन ह्रुतः (*śataṃcana hrutaḥ*)—even enemies of many hundreds
- न मिनन् (*na minan*)—cannot injure

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, when you, the purifier, wish to give us wealth, then not even enemies in great numbers can injure you, who wish to give wealth.

##### English translation
A hundred fces harm you not, purposing to give wealth when being purified you are benevolently iuclined. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 28

> पव॑स्वेंदो॒ वृषा॑ सु॒तः कृ॒धी नो॑ य॒शसो॒ जने॑ ।  
> विश्वा॒ अप॒ द्विषो॑ जहि ॥ २८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विश्वाः । अप । द्विषः । जहि ॥ २८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंदो सोम सुतः अभिषुतः वृषा सेक्ता त्वं पवस्व धारया क्षर। जने जनपदेषु नः अस्मान् यशसः यशस्विनः कृधि कुरु । विश्वाः सर्वान् द्विषः द्वेष्टॄन् शत्रून् अप जहि मारय च ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indu, Soma, pressed and a showerer, flow in a stream. Among the people and the lands make us renowned. And slay all the hating enemies.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O divine Soma
- सुतः (*sutaḥ*)—you who are pressed
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—and a showerer of desires
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow in the form of a stream
- जने (*jane*)—among the people of our group
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- यशसः (*yaśasaḥ*)—as renowned
- कृधि (*kṛdhi*)—make

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

You, Indu. when effused, the showerer (of benefits). make us celebrated amongst men : slay all our enemies.

#### Ṛk 29

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अस्य॑ ते स॒ख्ये व॒यं तवें॑दो द्यु॒म्न उ॑त्त॒मे ।  
> सा॒स॒ह्याम॑ पृतन्य॒तः ॥ २९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अस्य । ते । सख्ये । वयम् । तव । इंदो इति । द्युम्ने । उत्ऽतमे ।  
> ससह्याम । पृतन्यतः ॥ २९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंदो सोम अस्य अस्मिन् यागे वर्तमानस्य ते तव सख्ये सखित्वे सति वयम् अमहीयव आंगिरसा: तव त्वदीये उतमे श्रेष्ठे द्युम्ने अन्ने तृप्तिं प्राप्ता: । तथा च यास्कः-- द्युम्नं द्योततेर्यशो वान्नं वा ' ( निरु, ५. ५) इति । पृतन्यतः युद्धमिच्छतः शत्रून् ससह्याम अभिभवेम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indu, Soma, while we, the अमहीयव आंगिरसा (*amahīyava āṃgirasā*), are in the friendship of you who are present in this sacrifice, we have attained satisfaction in your excellent splendour, that is, food. Accordingly Yāska says: द्युम्नं द्योततेर्यशो वान्नं वा (*dyumnaṃ dyotateryaśo vānnaṃ vā*) (Ni. 5. 5). May we overcome the enemies who desire battle.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O divine Soma
- अस्य (*asya*)—who are present in this sacrifice
- ते (*te*)—your
- सख्ये (*sakhye*)—having attained friendship
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- तव (*tava*)—favoured by you

### Printed p. 202

- उत्तमे (*uttame*)—extremely excellent
- द्युम्ने (*dyumne*)—and shining, by the food, having attained satisfaction
- पृतन्यवः (*pṛtanyavaḥ*)—our enemy armies **NOTE**
- ससह्याम (*sasahyāma*)—may we conquer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, we who have attained the friendship of you who are present in this sacrifice, having been satisfied with food that is favoured by you, extremely excellent and shining, may we conquer our enemy armies.

##### English translation
(Enjoying) the friendship of you here and your excellent food, Indu may we overcome our assailants.

- ते (*te*)—your

## Sūkta 62 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘एते असृग्रम्' इति त्रिंशदृचं द्वितीयं सूक्तं भार्गवस्य जमदग्नेरार्षं गायत्रं पवमानसोमदेवताकम् । तथा चानुक्रांतम्-- एते असृग्रं जमदग्निः' इति । गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The second sūkta, एते असृग्रम् (*ete asṛgram*), of thirty ṛks, has as seer Jamadagni of the Bhārgava line, is in the Gāyatra metre, and has Pavamāna Soma as deity. So the Anukramaṇī says: एते असृग्रं जमदग्निः (*ete asṛgraṃ jamadagniḥ*). The ritual application has been stated already.

The sūkta एते असृग्रं (*ete asṛgraṃ*) is the second sūkta in the third anuvāka. It has thirty ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Jamadagni, the son of Bhṛgu; the deity is Pavamāna Soma; the metre is Gāyatrī. The Anukramaṇī says एते असृग्रं जमदग्निः (*ete asṛgraṃ jamadagniḥ*); the application has been stated before. **NOTE**

Sūkta 62. Maṇḍala 9; Anuvāka 3; Sūkta 62. Aṣṭaka 7; Adhyāya 1; Vargas 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 30. Seer: Jamadagni. Deity: Pavamāna Soma. Metre: Gāyatrī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒ते अ॑सृग्र॒मिंद॑वस्ति॒रः प॒वित्र॑मा॒शवः॑ ।  
> विश्वा॑न्य॒भि सौभ॑गा ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एते । असृग्रम् । इंदवः । तिरः । पवित्रम् । आशवः ।  
> विश्वानि । अभि । सौभगा ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आशवः शीघ्राः एते पवमानाः इंदवः सोमाः विश्वानि सर्वाणि सौभगा सौभगानि धनान्यभिलक्ष्य पवित्रं तिरः असृग्रम् ऋत्विग्भिः सृज्यंते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

These swift Soma juices, as they flow, have been released across the filter by the priests, aiming at all good fortunes, that is, riches.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आशवः (*āśavaḥ*)—swift-moving
- एते इंदवः (*ete iṃdavaḥ*)—these Soma juices
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all
- सौभगा अभि (*saubhagā abhi*)—to procure blessings
- पवित्रं तिरः (*pavitraṃ tiraḥ*)—toward the ten-fold filter
- अस्यग्रं (*asyagraṃ*)—have been made to turn **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

These swift-moving Soma juices have been made to flow by the priests toward the ten-fold filter, to procure all prosperity.

##### English translation

> तना॑ कृ॒ण्वंतो॒ अर्व॑ते ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विऽघ्नंतः । दुःऽइता । पुरु । सुऽगा । तोकाय । वाजिनः ।  
> तना । कृण्वंतः । अर्वते ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वाजिनः बलवंतः सोमाः पुरु बहूनि दुरिता दुरितानि विघ्नंतः विशेषेण नाशयंतः तोकाय अस्माकं पुत्राय अर्वते अश्वाय च सुगा सुखानि तना धनानि च कृण्वंतः कुर्वंतः तिरः पवित्रं सृज्यंत इति संबंधः ॥

- पुरु (*puru*)—many

- कृण्वंतः (*kṛṇvaṃtaḥ*)—producing (they go and join toward the ten-fold filter)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> असावि । अंशुः । मदाय । अप्ऽसु । दक्षः । गिरिऽस्थाः ।  
> श्येनः । न । योनिम् । आ । असदत् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> गिरिष्ठाः पर्वते जातः अंशुः सोमः मदाय मदार्थम् असावि अभिषुतः । अप्सु वसतीवरीषु दक्षः प्रवृद्धश्च भवति । किंच श्येनो न यथा श्येनो वेगेनागत्य स्थानमासीदति तद्वदयं सोमो योनिं स्वकीयं स्थानम् आसदत् आसीदति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Soma plant, born on the mountain, has been pressed for exhilaration. It becomes strong and swollen when it mingles with the waters, the वसतीवरीषु (*vasatīvarīṣu*) (Vasatīvarī waters). Like a falcon that comes with speed and settles in its place, this Soma settles in its own place.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गिरिष्ठाः (*giriṣṭhāḥ*)—born in the mountain region
- अंशुः (*aṃśuḥ*)—the Soma
- मदाय (*madāya*)—for gladness
- असावि (*asāvi*)—has been pressed
- अप्पु (*appu*)—joined with the Vasatīvarī and other waters **NOTE**
- वक्षः (*vakṣaḥ*)—becomes powerful **NOTE**
- श्येनो न (*śyeno na*)—coming swiftly like a falcon
- योनिं (*yoniṃ*)—in his own place of sacrifice
- आसदत् (*āsadat*)—sits down

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

From the Soma plant that is born in the mountain region the Soma juice is pressed for gladness. It becomes powerful by mingling with the Vasatīvarī and other waters. Coming swiftly like a falcon, it sits down in its own place of sacrifice.

##### English translation
The mountain-born Soma flows for exhilaration, mighty in the (Vasativari) waters : he alights like a falcon on his own place

### Printed p. 207

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शुभ्रम् । अंधः । देवऽवातम् । अप्ऽसु । धूतः । नृऽभिः । सुतः ।  
> स्वदंति । गावः । पयःऽभिः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यत् देववातं देवैः प्रार्थितं शुभ्रं शोभनम् अंधः अन्नं गावः पशवः पयोभिः आशिरैः स्वदंति स्वादयंति सोऽयं सोमः नृभिः नेतृभिर्ऋत्विग्भिः सुतः अभिषुतः सन् अप्सु वसतीवरीषु धूतः शोधितो भवति ॥ ॥ २४ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The cattle make sweet with their milk, the आशिरैः (*āśiraiḥ*) (admixtures), the bright and beautiful food that the gods desire. This Soma, pressed by the priests, the leaders, is purified in the Vasatīvarī waters.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देववातं (*devavātaṃ*)—that which is desired by the gods
- शुभ्रं (*śubhraṃ*)—and that which is shining
- अंधः (*aṃdhaḥ*)—the Soma
- गावः (*gāvaḥ*)—the cows
- पयोभिः (*payobhiḥ*)—mixing with their milk
- स्वदंति (*svadaṃti*)—make it pleasant to the taste
- नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)—by the priests
- सुतः (*sutaḥ*)—the pressed Soma juice
- अप्पु (*appu*)—in the Vasatīvarī and other waters **NOTE**
- धूतः (*dhūtaḥ*)—is purified

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Soma that is desired by the gods and shining, the cows make pleasant to the taste by mixing it with their milk. The Soma pressed by the priests is purified in the Vasatīvarī and other waters.

##### English translation
The cattle sweeten with their milk the beautiful food that is asked for by the gods; the Soma when effused by the priests is cleansed in the water.
#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आदी॒मश्वं॒ न हेता॒रोऽशू॑शुभन्न॒मृता॑य ।  
> मध्वो॒ रसं॑ सध॒मादे॑ ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आत् । ईम् । अश्वम् । न । हेतारः । अशूशुभन् । अमृताय ।  
> मध्वः । रसम् । सधऽमादे ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 208

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आत् अनंतरं हेतारः प्रेरका ऋत्विजः सधमादे यज्ञे ईम् एनं मध्वः मदकरस्य सोमस्य रसम् अमृताय अमरणाय अश्वं न अश्वमिव अशूशुभन् शोभयंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Thereupon the priests, the impellers, at the sacrifice adorn this juice of the intoxicating Soma, as one adorns a horse, for the sake of immortality.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आत् (*āt*)—immediately
- होतारः (*hotāraḥ*)—the Hotṛ priests **NOTE**
- सधमादे (*sadhamāde*)—at the sacrifice
- मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)—of the sweet Soma
- ईं रसं (*īṃ rasaṃ*)—this juice
- अमृताय (*amṛtāya*)—to gain immortality
- अश्वं न (*aśvaṃ na*)—as one decorates a horse
- अशूशुभन् (*aśūśubhan*)—they adorn

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As soon as the Soma juice has been pressed and purified, the Hotṛ priests adorn this sweet juice at the place of sacrifice, as one decorates a horse, to gain immortality.

##### English translation
Then the ministering priests in the assembly beautify the juice of the exhilarating (Soma) like a horse, for the sake of immortality
#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यास्ते॒ धारा॑ मधु॒श्चुतोऽसृ॑ग्रमिंद ऊ॒तये॑ ।  
> ताभिः॑ प॒वित्र॒मास॑दः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> याः । ते । धाराः । मधुऽश्चुतः । असृग्रम् । इंदो इति । ऊतये ।  
> ताभिः । पवित्रम् । आ । असदः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंदो सोम ते तव मधुश्चुतः मधुररसस्य श्चोतयित्र्यः याः धाराः ऊतये रक्षणाय असृग्रं सृज्यंते ताभिः धाराभिस्त्वं पवित्रम् आसदः आसीद ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indu, Soma, the streams of yours that drip sweet juice and are sent forth for protection: with those streams sit down upon the filter.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma-deva
- ते (*te*)—your
- मधुश्चुतः (*madhuścutaḥ*)—that shed sweet juice
- याः धाराः (*yāḥ dhārāḥ*)—which streams of Soma
- ऊतये (*ūtaye*)—for protection
- असृग्रं (*asṛgraṃ*)—are produced
- ताभिः (*tābhiḥ*)—with those streams
- पवित्रं (*pavitraṃ*)—on the Daśāpavitra filter
- असदः (*asadaḥ*)—come and sit down **NOTE**
### Printed p. 209

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, with those streams of yours that shed sweet juice and are produced for protection, come and sit down on the Daśāpavitra filter.

##### English translation
Sit down, Indu, on the filter with those streams the shedders of (juice) which are let fall for our protection.
#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सो अ॒र्षेंद्रा॑य पी॒तये॑ ति॒रो रोमा॑ण्य॒व्यया॑ ।  
> सीद॒न्योना॒ वने॒ष्वा ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । अर्ष । इंद्राय । पीतये । तिरः । रोमाणि । अव्यया ।  
> सीदन् । योना । वनेषु । आ ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम सः अभिषुतस्त्वम् अव्यया अव्ययानि अविमयानि रोमाणि वालानि तिरः तिरस्कुर्वन् वनेषु पात्रेषु योना योनौ स्थाने आ सीदन् इंद्राय इंद्रस्य पीतये पानाय अर्ष क्षर ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, pressed as you are, pass through the woollen hairs, the अव्यया (*avyayā*) of the filter, and settle in the place in the vessels, and flow for Indra's drinking.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Soma-deva) सः (*saḥ*)—you who have been pressed
- अव्यया (*avyayā*)—of the Daśāpavitra made of wool
- रोमाणि (*romāṇi*)—the fibres
- तिरः (*tiraḥ*)—crossing over
- वनेषु (*vaneṣu*)—in the vessels
- योना (*yonā*)—in the excellent place
- आसीदन् (*āsīdan*)—sitting down **NOTE**
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra
- वीतये (*vītaye*)—for drinking **NOTE**
- अर्ष (*arṣa*)—flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, pressed as you are, pass across the fibres of the Daśāpavitra made of wool, sit in the excellent place in the vessels, and flow for Indra's drinking.

##### English translation
Passing obliquely through the sheeps' hairs, hasten for Indra's drinking, sitting in your place in the wooden vessels.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वमिं॑दो॒ परि॑ स्रव॒ स्वादि॑ष्ठो॒ अंगि॑रोभ्यः ।  
> व॒रि॒वो॒विद्घृ॒तं पयः॑ ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वम् । इंदो इति । परि । स्रव । स्वादिष्ठः । अंगिरःऽभ्यः ।  
> वरिवःऽवित् । घृतम् । पयः ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंदो सोम स्वादिष्टः स्वादुतमः वरिवोवित् अस्मदभिलषितस्य धनस्य लंभकश्च त्वम् अंगिरोभ्यः अंगिरसामर्थाय घृतम् आज्यं पयः च परि स्रव परिक्षर ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indu, Soma, you are the sweetest and the obtainer of the wealth we desire. Flow around for the Aṅgirases, for their sake, with ghee and milk.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma-deva
- स्वादिष्टः (*svādiṣṭaḥ*)—the most delicious
- वरिवोवित् (*varivovit*)—the bringer of wealth
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- अंगिरोभ्यः (*aṃgirobhyaḥ*)—to us, who are called Aṅgirases
- धृतं (*dhṛtaṃ*)—ghee **NOTE**
- पयः (*payaḥ*)—milk
- परि स्रव (*pari srava*)—cause to flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you who are the most delicious and the bringer of wealth, make ghee and milk flow for us, who are called Aṅgirases.

##### English translation
Indu, who are most sweet-flavoured, the bestower of riches, drop for the Angirasas butter and milk.
#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यं विच॑र्षणिर्हि॒तः पव॑मानः॒ स चे॑तति ।  
> हि॒न्वा॒न आप्यं॑ बृ॒हत् ॥ १० ॥

### Printed p. 211

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयम् । विऽचर्षणिः । हितः । पवमानः । सः । चेतति ।  
> हिन्वानः । आप्यम् । बृहत् ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विचर्षणिः विद्रष्टा हितः पात्रेषु निहितः पवमानः अयं सोमः आप्यम् अप्सु भवं बृहत् महदन्नं हिन्वानः प्रेरयन् चेतति सर्वैः ज्ञायते ॥ ॥ २५ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Soma, the all-seeing, placed in the vessels, and purifying, sends forth the great food that is born in the waters, and is known to all.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विचर्षणिः (*vicarṣaṇiḥ*)—who can see everything minutely
- हितः (*hitaḥ*)—who is placed in the vessels
- पवमानः (*pavamānaḥ*)—and who is the purifier
- अयं सः (*ayaṃ saḥ*)—this Soma-deva
- आप्यं (*āpyaṃ*)—that dwells in the water
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—great food
- हिन्वानः (*hinvānaḥ*)—sending forth
- चेतति (*cetati*)—becomes visible to all

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This Soma-deva, who can see everything minutely, is placed in the vessels, and is the purifier, becomes visible to all, sending forth the great food that dwells in the water.

##### English translation
This all-seeing Pavamana Soma deposited (in the vessels), sending forth abundant (food), the product of the waters, is known (by all).
#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒ष वृषा॒ वृष॑व्रतः॒ पव॑मानो अशस्ति॒हा ।  
> कर॒द्वसू॑नि दा॒शुषे॑ ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एषः । वृषा । वृषऽव्रतः । पवमानः । अशस्तिऽहा ।  
> करत् । वसूनि । दाशुषे ॥ ११ ॥

### Printed p. 212

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वृषा कामानां सेक्ता वृषव्रतः वृषकर्मा अशस्तिहा राक्षसानां हंता पवमानः एषः सोमः दाशुषे हविषां दात्रे यजमानाय वसूनि धनानि करत् करोति । प्रयच्छतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Soma, the showerer of desires, whose work is showering, the slayer of the Rākṣasas, purifying himself, bestows riches on the sacrificer who gives oblations; the meaning is that he gives them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—the showerer of desires
- वृषव्रतः (*vṛṣavrataḥ*)—whose work is the pouring of rain
- अशस्तिहा (*aśastihā*)—the destroyer of the wicked Rākṣasas
- एषः पवमानः (*eṣaḥ pavamānaḥ*)—this Soma-deva
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to the sacrificer who offers the oblation
- वसूनि (*vasūni*)—riches
- करत् (*karat*)—provides

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This Soma-deva, who showers desires, whose work is the pouring of rain, and who destroys the wicked Rākṣasas, provides riches to the sacrificer who offers the oblation.

##### English translation
This Pavamana Soma, the sprinkler ( of benefits ), engaged in sprinkling, the destroyer of the Rakshasas, bestows riches upon the donor (of the oblation).
#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ प॑वस्व सह॒स्रिणं॑ र॒यिं गोमं॑तम॒श्विन॑म् ।  
> पु॒रु॒श्चं॒द्रं पु॑रु॒स्पृह॑म् ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । पवस्व । सहस्रिणम् । रयिम् । गोऽमंतम् । अश्विनम् ।  
> पुरुऽचंद्रम् । पुरुऽस्पृहम् ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम त्वं सहस्रिणं बहुसंख्याकं गोमंतं गोभिरुपेतम् अश्विनम् अश्ववंतं पुरुश्चंद्रं बहूनां हर्षकं पुरुस्पृहं बहुस्पृहणीयं रयिं धनम् आ पवस्व परिक्षर ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, flow towards us the wealth that is thousandfold, rich in cows, rich in horses, delighting many and desired by many.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Soma-deva) सहस्रिणं (*sahasriṇaṃ*)—that which is thousandfold
- गोमंतं (*gomaṃtaṃ*)—that which is joined with cows
- अश्विनं (*aśvinaṃ*)—that which is joined with horses
- पुरुश्चंद्रं (*puruścaṃdraṃ*)—that which gives delight to many
- पुरुस्पृहं (*puruspṛhaṃ*)—that which is desired by many
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- आ पवस्व (*ā pavasva*)—pour out for us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, pour out for us wealth that is thousandfold, joined with cows, joined with horses, delighting many and desired by many.

##### English translation
Pour forth thousand-fold wealth, together with cattle and horses, delighting many, desired by many.
#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒ष स्य परि॑ षिच्यते मर्मृ॒ज्यमा॑न आ॒युभिः॑ ।  
> उ॒रु॒गा॒यः क॒विक्र॑तुः ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एषः । स्यः । परि । सिच्यते । मर्मृज्यमानः । आयुऽभिः ।  
> उरुऽगायः । कविऽक्रतुः ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उरुगायः बहुस्तुतिः कविक्रतुः क्रांतप्रज्ञः क्रांतकर्मा वा स्थः सः एषः अयं सोमः आयुभिः मनुष्यैः मर्मृज्यमानः शोध्यमानः परि षिच्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Soma, much praised, of wise purpose or of surpassing deeds, is purified by men and sprinkled all around. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उरुगायः (*urugāyaḥ*)—that which is praised by many
- कविक्रतुः (*kavikratuḥ*)—that which has work endowed with wisdom
- स्यः (*syaḥ*)—and that which is renowned
- एषः (*eṣaḥ*)—this Soma
- आयुभिः (*āyubhiḥ*)—by the priests and others
- मर्म्मृज्यमानः (*marmmṛjyamānaḥ*)—being purified **NOTE**
- परिषिच्यते (*pariṣicyate*)—is poured out
### Printed p. 214

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This Soma, which is praised by many, has work endowed with wisdom and is renowned, is purified by the priests and others and poured out.

##### English translation
This (Soma) the many-hymned, having wise designs, being cleansed by the priests, is sprinkled forth.
#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒हस्रो॑तिः श॒ताम॑घो वि॒मानो॒ रज॑सः क॒विः ।  
> इंद्रा॑य पवते॒ मदः॑ ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सहस्रऽऊतिः । शतऽमघः । विऽमानः । रजसः । कविः ।  
> इंद्राय । पवते । मदः ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सहस्रोतिः अपरिमितरक्षणः शतमघः बहुधनः रजसः लोकस्य विमानः निर्माता कविः क्रांतकर्मा मदः मदकरः सोमः इंद्राय इंद्रार्थं पवते धारया क्षरति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The intoxicating Soma, of unmeasured protection, of abundant wealth, the maker of the world, the sage whose works are surpassing, flows in a stream for Indra.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सहस्रोतिः (*sahasrotiḥ*)—who has protection of many kinds
- शतमघः (*śatamaghaḥ*)—who has wealth of various kinds
- रजसः (*rajasaḥ*)—for the worlds
- विमानः (*vimānaḥ*)—the maker
- कविः (*kaviḥ*)—who has work endowed with wisdom
- मदः (*madaḥ*)—the Soma-deva who gives gladness
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for the satisfaction of Indra
- पवते (*pavate*)—runs in the form of a stream

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Soma-deva, who has protection of many kinds, wealth of various kinds, is the maker of the worlds, has work endowed with wisdom and gives gladness, runs in the form of a stream for the satisfaction of Indra.
### Printed p. 215

##### English translation
Offering thonsand-fold protection, having hundred-fold wealth, the measurer of the world, the sage, the exilarating (Soma) flows for Indra.

> विः । योना । वसतौऽइव ॥ १५ ॥

Indu, the Soma, who has appeared and been praised by song, is placed at this sacrifice in his own place for Indra, as a bird in its dwelling.

- गिरा (*girā*)—by praises

- योना (*yonā*)—in his excellent place
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra

- धीयते (*dhīyate*)—is placed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Soma-deva, who has been born and extolled with praises, is placed at this sacrifice in his own excellent place for Indra, as a bird is in its own nest.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> त्रिपृष्ठे त्रिषवणपृष्ठे त्रिवंधुरे त्रिवेदवंधुरे ऋषीणां रथे यज्ञरथे तं सोमं सप्त सप्तभिः धीतिभिः छंदोभिः यातवे देवान् प्रति गंतुं युंजंति ऋत्विजो योजयंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The priests yoke that Soma, with the seven metres, to the sacrificial chariot of the sages, which is three-backed (resting on the three pressings) and three-benched (resting on the three Vedas), so that he may go to the gods.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्रिपृष्ठे (*tripṛṣṭhe*)—that which has three kinds of support
- त्रिवंधुरे (*trivaṃdhure*)—and that which has a support of three forms
- ऋषीणां (*ṛṣīṇāṃ*)—of the sages
- रथे (*rathe*)—in the chariot that is the sacrifice
- तं (*taṃ*)—that Soma-deva
- सप्त (*sapta*)—seven in number
- धीतिभिः (*dhītibhiḥ*)—having prepared with the metres
- यातने (*yātane*)—to go to the gods **NOTE**
- युंजंति (*yuṃjaṃti*)—the priests yoke

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In the chariot of the sages that is the sacrifice, which has three kinds of support and a support of three forms, the priests prepare that Soma-deva with the seven metres and yoke him, so that he may go to the gods.

##### English translation
The attach him by seven ceremonies to the three-backed three-benched chariot of the Rishis to go to the gods. **NOTE**
#### Ṛk 18

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तं सो॑तारो धन॒स्पृत॑मा॒शुं वाजा॑य॒ यात॑वे ।  
> हरिं॑ हिनोत वा॒जिन॑म् ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तम् । सोतारः । धनऽस्पृतम् । आशुम् । वाजाय । यातवे ।  
> हरिम् । हिनोत । वाजिनम् ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोतारः अभिषवकर्तार ऋत्विजः धनस्पृतं धनानां स्प्रष्टारं वाजिनं बलिनम् आशुं वेगवंतं तं सोमात्मकं हरिम् अश्वं वाजाय यज्ञाख्यं संग्रामं यातवे गंतंं हिनोत प्रेरयत । यथा योद्धारो युद्धं गंतुं बलिनं वेगवंतमश्वं प्रेरयंति तद्वत् यज्ञमभिगंतुं बलवंतं सोमं प्रेरयतेति भावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O pressers, priests who perform the pressing, urge on that Soma, the horse, the seizer of wealth, strong and swift, to go to the battle that is the sacrifice. As warriors urge a strong, swift horse to go to battle, so urge the strong Soma to go to the sacrifice; that is the sense.

- स्तोतारः (*stotāraḥ*)—O praisers **NOTE**
- धनस्पृतं (*dhanaspṛtaṃ*)—that which bestows wealth
- वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*)—and that which is full of strength
- आशुं (*āśuṃ*)—and that which goes swiftly
- तं (*taṃ*)—that which has the form of Soma
- हरिं (*hariṃ*)—the horse
- वाजाय (*vājāya*)—for the battle that is the sacrifice
- यातने (*yātane*)—to go **NOTE**
- हिनोत (*hinota*)—urge and send forth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O praisers, urge and send forth the horse that bestows wealth, is full of strength, goes swiftly and has the form of Soma, to go to the battle that is the sacrifice.

##### English translation
Effusers of the Soma, urge forward that wealth-bestowing rapid vigorous steed to go to the battle.

- तिष्ठति (*tiṣṭhati*)—stands

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम पुनानः पूयमानो यस्त्वं वीतये भक्षणाय गव्यानि गोसंबंधीनि नृम्णा नृम्णानि धनानि क्षीरादीनि अभि अर्षसि अभिगच्छसि स त्वं सनद्वाजः दीयमानान्नः सन् परि स्रव परिक्षर ॥

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you who have been purified, go and join the milk and the like that are connected with cows, to become fit for consumption. Being the giver of food, flow all around.

##### English translation
Being purified you hasten to the treasures of the cows to enjoy (them); flow forth you who grant food.

> गृ॒णा॒नो ज॒मद॑ग्निना ॥ २४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> गृणानः । जमत्ऽअग्निना ॥ २४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उत अपि च हे सोम जमदग्निना जमदग्निनाम्ना ऋषिणा मया गृणानः स्तूयमानस्त्वं नः अस्माकं गोमतीः गोभिर्युक्तानि परिष्टुभः परितः स्तोतव्यानि विश्वाः सर्वाणि इषः अन्नानि अर्ष गच्छ। अस्मभ्यमेवंविधान्यन्नानि देहीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Moreover, O Soma, praised by me, the seer named Jamadagni, go to us with all foods that are rich in cattle and everywhere to be praised; that is, give us foods of this kind.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, who make everything tremble, you who are chief, urging on the praising words, cause the waters of the atmosphere to flow (by way of rain).

> हे कवे क्रांतकर्मन् सोम तुभ्य तुभ्यं तव महिम्ने इमा इमानि भुवना भुवनानि तस्थिरे तिष्ठंति । त्वामेव पुरस्कुर्वंतीत्यर्थः। अपि च सिंधवः नद्यः तुभ्यम् एव अर्षंति गच्छंति । त्वदाज्ञामेवानुपालयंतीत्यर्थः ॥

- अर्षंति (*arṣaṃti*)—flow on

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you whose action is full of wisdom, to make your greatness shine all these worlds stand, each established in its own place. The rivers too flow on by that same greatness of yours.

##### English translation

## Sūkta 63 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘आ पवस्व' इति त्रिंशदृचं तृतीयं सूक्तं काश्यपस्य निध्रुवेरार्षं गायत्रं पवमानसोमदेवताकम् । तथा चानुक्रांतम्- आ पवस्व निध्रुविः काश्यपः' इति । गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning आ पवस्व (*ā pavasva*) has thirty Ṛks and is the third sūkta. Its seer is Nidhruvi of the Kāśyapa line, its metre is Gāyatra, and its deity is Pavamāna Soma. Sāyaṇa cites the Anukramaṇī: आ पवस्व निध्रुविः काश्यपः (*ā pavasva nidhruviḥ kāśyapaḥ*). The ritual application has already been stated.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, beginning आ पवस्व (*ā pavasva*), is the third sūkta in the third anuvāka. It has thirty Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Nidhruvi Kāśyapa; the deity is Pavamāna Soma; the metre is Gāyatrī. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: आ पवस्व निध्रुविः काश्यपः (*ā pavasva nidhruviḥ kāśyapaḥ*). The ritual application has been stated earlier.

##### Particulars

- Sūkta 63
- Maṇḍala 9, Anuvāka 3, Sūkta 63
- Aṣṭaka 7, Adhyāya 1, Vargas 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, 35
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 30
- Seer: Nidhruvi Kāśyapa
- Deity: Pavamāna Soma
- Metre: Gāyatrī

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ प॑वस्व सह॒स्रिणं॑ र॒यिं सो॑म सु॒वीर्य॑म् ।  
> अ॒स्मे श्रवां॑सि धारय ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 229

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । पवस्व । सहस्रिणम् । रयिम् । सोम । सुऽवीर्यम् ।  
> अस्मे इति । श्रवांसि । धारय ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम त्वं सहस्रिणं बहुसंख्याकं सुवीर्यं शोभनवीर्यं रयिं धनम् आ पवस्व आभिमुख्येन क्षर । अपि च अस्मे अस्मासु श्रवांसि अन्नानि धारय स्थापय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, flow towards us a wealth that is thousandfold, abundant and of good heroic power; flow it with a facing movement. Moreover, establish in us foods.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- सहस्रिणं (*sahasriṇaṃ*)—that which is of a thousand kinds
- सुवीर्यं (*suvīryaṃ*)—that which has excellent power
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- आ पवस्व (*ā pavasva*)—provide on all sides
- अस्मे (*asme*)—in us
- श्रवांसि (*śravāṃsi*)—foods
- धारय (*dhāraya*)—establish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, provide us fully with wealth that is of a thousand kinds and has excellent power. Fill us with foods.

##### English translation
Pour (upon us), Soma, thousand fold wealth, with excellent male progeny, secure to us ample food.

> च॒मूष्वा नि षी॑दसि ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इषम् । ऊर्जम् । च । पिन्वसे । इंद्राय । मत्सरिन्ऽतमः ।  
> चमूषु । आ । नि । सीदसि ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 230

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम मत्सरिंतमः अतिशयेन मदयितृतमस्त्वम् इंद्राय इंद्रार्थम् इषम् अन्नम् ऊर्जं रसं च पिन्वसे क्षरसि । अपि च चमूषु चमसेषु आ नि षीदसि तिष्ठसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, you who most exhilarate, flow food and sap for Indra, that is, for Indra's sake. Moreover, you settle and stay in the ladles.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मत्सरिंतमः (*matsariṃtamaḥ*)—you who are the most exceedingly gladdening (O Soma-deva)
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra's sake
- इषं (*iṣaṃ*)—food
- ऊर्जं च (*ūrjaṃ ca*)—and sap
- पिन्वसे (*pinvase*)—you make flow
- चमूषु (*camūṣu*)—in the ladle vessels
- आ नि षीदसि (*ā ni ṣīdasi*)—you sit

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you who are the most exceedingly gladdening, cause food and sap to flow for Indra's sake. You sit also in the ladle vessels.

##### English translation
You who are most exhilarating effuse food and drink for Indra; you sit on the ladles.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सु॒त इंद्रा॑य॒ विष्ण॑वे॒ सोमः॑ क॒लशे॑ अक्षरत् ।  
> मधु॑माँ अस्तु वा॒यवे॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सुतः । इंद्राय । विष्णवे । सोमः । कलशे । अक्षरत् ।  
> मधुऽमान् । अस्तु । वायवे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्राय इंद्रार्थं विष्णवे विष्ण्वर्थं च वायवे वाय्वर्थं च सुतः अभिषुतः यः सोमः कलशे द्रोणकलशे अक्षरत् क्षरति सोऽयं सोमः मधुमान् मधुररसवान् अस्तु भवतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Soma that is pressed for Indra, for Viṣṇu and for Vāyu, and that flows in the Droṇa vessel, may that Soma be full of sweet flavour.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra's sake
- विष्णवे (*viṣṇave*)—for Viṣṇu
- वायवे (*vāyave*)—for Vāyu
- सुतः (*sutaḥ*)—pressed
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—which Soma
- कलशे (*kalaśe*)—in the Droṇa vessel
- अक्षरत् (*akṣarat*)—flows, that Soma
- मधुमान् (*madhumān*)—most delicious
- अस्तु (*astu*)—may it be

### Printed p. 231

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May that Soma, pressed for Indra, for Viṣṇu and for Vāyu, which flows in the Droṇa vessel, be most delicious.

##### English translation
Soma effused for Indra and Vishnu and Vayu drops into the pitcher ; may he be sweet-flavonred. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒ते अ॑सृग्रमा॒शवोऽति॒ ह्वरां॑सि ब॒भ्रवः॑ ।  
> सोमा॑ ऋ॒तस्य॒ धार॑या ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एते । असृग्रम् । आशवः । अति । ह्वरांसि । बभ्रवः ।  
> सोमाः । ऋतस्य । धारया ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> बभ्रवः बभ्रुवर्णाः आशवः शीघ्राः एते इमे सोमाः ऋतस्य उदकस्य धारया असृग्रं सृज्यंते । ह्वरांसि रक्षांस्यभिगच्छंति च ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

These tawny and swift Somas are let loose with the stream of water, and they go towards the Rākṣasas.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- बभ्रवः (*babhravaḥ*)—those of golden-brown colour
- आशवः (*āśavaḥ*)—and swift-going
- एते सोमाः (*ete somāḥ*)—these Soma-juices
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—with water
- धारया (*dhārayā*)—joined in the form of a stream
- ह्वरांसि (*hvarāṃsi*)—towards the Rākṣasas
- असृग्रं (*asṛgraṃ*)—have been let loose

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

These Soma-juices, golden-brown and swift-going, joined with water in the form of a stream, have been let loose to rush towards the Rākṣasas.

##### English translation
These swift-flowing tawny-coloured Soma-juices, with a stream of water are let loose upon the Rakshasas.

### Printed p. 232

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रं॒ वर्धं॑तो अ॒प्तुरः॑ कृ॒ण्वंतो॒ विश्व॒मार्य॑म् ।  
> अ॒प॒घ्नंतो॒ अरा॑व्णः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रम् । वर्धंतः । अप्ऽतुरः । कृण्वंतः । विश्वम् । आर्यम् ।  
> अपऽघ्नंतः । अराव्णः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्रं वर्धंतः वर्धयंतः अप्तुरः उदकस्य प्रेरकाः विश्वं सोममस्मदीयकर्मार्थम् आर्यं भद्रं कृण्वंतः कुर्वंतः अराव्णः अदातॄन अपघ्नंतः विनाशयंतः । अभ्यर्षंतीत्युत्तरया संबंधः ॥ ॥ ३० ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Increasing Indra, impelling the waters, making everything auspicious for our rites **NOTE**, and destroying the non-givers, the Somas flow. Sāyaṇa connects this with the verb अभ्यर्षंति (*abhyarṣaṃti*) of the next Ṛk.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- वर्धंतः (*vardhaṃtaḥ*)—increasing
- अपुरः (*apuraḥ*)—as impellers of the water **NOTE**
- विश्वं (*viśvaṃ*)—all
- आर्यं (*āryaṃ*)—auspiciousness
- कृण्वंतः (*kṛṇvaṃtaḥ*)—bringing about
- अराष्ट्रः (*arāṣṭraḥ*)—the misers who give no gifts **NOTE**
- अपघ्नंतः (*apaghnaṃtaḥ*)—destroying (the Soma-juices go and join their own place)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Fortifying Indra, impelling the water, bringing about all auspiciousness, and destroying the misers who give no gifts, the Soma-juices go and join their own place.

##### English translation
Augmenting Indra, urging thc waters. making all our acts prosperous, destroying the withholders (of oblations). **NOTE**

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सु॒ता अनु॒ स्वमा रजो॒ऽभ्य॑र्षंति ब॒भ्रवः॑ ।  
> इंद्रं॒ गच्छं॑त॒ इंद॑वः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सुताः । अनु । स्वम् । आ । रजः । अभि । अर्षंति । बभ्रवः ।  
> इंद्रम् । गच्छंतः । इंदवः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> बभ्रवः बभ्रुवर्णाः सुताः अभिषुताः इंदवः सोमाः इंद्रम् आ गच्छंतः आभिमुख्येन प्राप्नुवंतः स्वं स्वकीयं रजः स्थानम् अनु प्रति अभ्यर्षंति अभिगच्छंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The tawny pressed Indus, that is the Somas, going to Indra, that is, reaching towards him, flow towards their own place, their own region.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- बभ्रवः (*babhravaḥ*)—those of golden-brown colour
- सुताः (*sutāḥ*)—and pressed
- इंदवः (*iṃdavaḥ*)—Soma-juices
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—towards Indra
- आ गच्छंतः (*ā gacchaṃtaḥ*)—coming swiftly
- स्वं (*svaṃ*)—their own
- रजः अनु (*rajaḥ anu*)—towards their own place
- अभ्यर्षंति (*abhyarṣaṃti*)—come running

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Soma-juices, golden-brown and pressed, come swiftly towards Indra. They come running towards their own place.

##### English translation
The effused tawny-coloured Soma-juices going to Indra hasten to their own place.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒या प॑वस्व॒ धार॑या॒ यया॒ सूर्य॒मरो॑चयः ।  
> हि॒न्वा॒नो मानु॑षीर॒पः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अया । पवस्व । धारया । यया । सूर्यम् । अरोचयः ।  
> हिन्वानः । मानुषीः । अपः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम मानुषीः मनुष्याणां हितानि अपः उदकानि हिन्वानः प्रेरयंस्त्वं यया धारया सूर्यमरोचयः प्राकाशयः तया अया अनया धारया पवस्व क्षर ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, urging on the waters that are beneficial to men, flow with that very stream with which you made the sun shine.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मानुषीः (*mānuṣīḥ*)—beneficial to men (O Soma-deva)
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the waters
- हिन्वानः (*hinvānaḥ*)—urging on
- यया (*yayā*)—by which stream of yours
- सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—the sun
- अरोचयः (*arocayaḥ*)—you made shine
- आया धारया (*āyā dhārayā*)—by that same stream
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow (in the form of a stream)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, urging on the waters that are beneficial to men, flow with that very stream of yours with which you made the sun shine.

Flow with that stream with which you, Soma, light up the sun, urging on the waters beneficial to man.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अयु॑क्त॒ सूर॒ एत॑शं॒ पव॑मानो म॒नावधि॑ ।  
> अं॒तरि॑क्षेण॒ यात॑वे ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयुक्त । सूरः । एतशम् । पवमानः । मनौ । अधि ।  
> अंतरिक्षेण । यातवे ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पवमानः पूयमानः सोमः मनावधि। मनुर्मनुष्यः । तस्मिन् मनुष्य इत्यर्थः । अंतरिक्षेण यातवे गंतुं सूरः सूर्यस्य एतशम् अश्वम् । ‘एतग्वः एतशः' इत्यश्वनामसु पाठात् । अयुक्त युंक्ते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The purifying Soma harnesses the horse of the sun to go through the atmosphere to Manu, that is, to man. Sāyaṇa says that the word for the horse is एतशं (*etaśaṃ*), since एतग्वः एतशः (*etagvaḥ etaśaḥ*) is read among the names of horses.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पवमानः (*pavamānaḥ*)—Soma-deva who is in the state of being purified
- अंतरिक्षेण (*aṃtarikṣeṇa*)—through the atmosphere
- मनावधि (*manāvadhi*)—to man
- यातने (*yātane*)—to go **NOTE**
- सूरः (*sūraḥ*)—of the sun
- एतशं (*etaśaṃ*)—the horse
- आयुंक्त (*āyuṃkta*)—harnesses **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The purified Soma-deva harnesses the sun's horse to go through the atmosphere to man.

##### English translation

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒त त्या ह॒रितो॒ दश॒ सूरो॑ अयुक्त॒ यात॑वे ।

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

- इंदुः (*iṃduḥ*)—Soma-deva

- आयुंक्त (*āyuṃkta*)—harnesses

Soma-deva, uttering the name "Indra", harnesses the sun's horse to travel in the well-known ten directions.

O praisers, the Soma that is pressed for Vāyu and for Indra, and that gladdens, pour out from this place of pressing into the meshes of the ten-fold filter made of wool.

##### English translation
Purified Soma, grant us wealth unassailable (by our foes), and which cannot be destroyed by the enemy.

> अ॒भि वाज॑मु॒त श्रवः॑ ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अभि । वाजम् । उत । श्रवः ॥ १२ ॥

> हे सोम त्वं सहस्रिणं बहुसंख्याकं गोमंतं गोभिर्युक्तम् अश्विनम् अश्ववंतं रयिं धनम् अभ्यर्ष अस्मानभिगमय । उत अपि च वाजं बलं श्रवः अन्नं चास्मान् अभि गमय ।

O Soma, bring to us wealth that is thousandfold, with cattle and with horses. Moreover, bring to us strength and food.

- गोमंतं (*gomaṃtaṃ*)—that which is joined with cattle
- अश्विनं (*aśvinaṃ*)—and that which is joined with horses
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- अभ्यर्ष (*abhyarṣa*)—provide for us
- उत (*uta*)—and
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—strength
- श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)—and food
- अभि (*abhi*)—provide for us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, provide us with wealth that is of a thousand kinds, joined with cattle and joined with horses; and provide us with strength and food.

##### English translation
Bring to us thousand-fold wealth with cattle and horses; bring vigour and food.

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सोमो॑ दे॒वो न सूर्योऽद्रि॑भिः पवते सु॒तः ।

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दधानः । कलशे । रसम् ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

Soma, shining like a god, like the sun, pressed by the stones, bearing the juice in the Droṇa vessel, flows in a stream.

- सूर्यः न (*sūryaḥ na*)—radiant like the sun

- सुतः (*sutaḥ*)—having been pressed
- कलशे (*kalaśe*)—in the Droṇa vessel
- रसं (*rasaṃ*)—the juice
- दधानः (*dadhānaḥ*)—holding
- पवते (*pavate*)—flows in the form of a stream

### Printed p. 239

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma-deva, who is of the nature of a god and radiant like the sun, pressed by the pressing stones, takes on the form of juice in the Droṇa vessel and flows on.

##### English translation
Soma, like the radiant sun, when effused flows forth, depositing its juice in the pitcher.

#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एते अभिषुताः इमे शुक्राः दीप्ताः सोमाः आर्या आर्याणां श्रेष्ठानां यजमानानां धामानि गृहान् प्रति गोमंतं गोभिर्युक्तं वाजम् अन्नम् ऋतस्य उदकस्य धारया अक्षरन् क्षरंति ॥

- एते (*ete*)—pressed
- शुक्राः (*śukrāḥ*)—and shining Soma-juices
- आर्या (*āryā*)—of excellent sacrificers
- धामानि (*dhāmāni*)—in the houses
- गोमंतं (*gomaṃtaṃ*)—joined with cattle
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—food
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of water
- धारया (*dhārayā*)—in the form of a stream
- अक्षरन् (*akṣaran*)—they pour down

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The pressed and shining Soma-juices pour down, in the houses of excellent sacrificers, food joined with cattle in the form of a stream of water.

These brilliant Soma-juices (flowing) towards thc dwellings of respectable (worshippers), effuse food and cattle in a stream of water. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 15

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सु॒ता इंद्रा॑य व॒ज्रिणे॒ सोमा॑सो॒ दध्या॑शिरः ।  
> प॒वित्र॒मत्य॑क्षरन् ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सुताः । इंद्राय । वज्रिणे । सोमासः । दधिऽआशिरः ।  
> पवित्रम् । अति । अक्षरन् ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वज्रिणे वज्रवते इंद्राय इंद्रार्थं सुताः अभिषुताः दध्याशिरः । दधि आशीराश्रयणद्रव्यं येषां ते दध्याशिरः । दधिसंस्कृताः सोमासः सोमाः पवित्रमति अतिक्रम्य अक्षरन् धारया क्षरंति ॥ ॥ ३२ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

For Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the pressed Somas called दध्याशिरः (*dadhyāśiraḥ*), those whose binding material is curds, that is, Somas prepared with curds, flow across the filter in a stream.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वज्रिणे (*vajriṇe*)—bearing the thunderbolt weapon
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra's sake
- सुताः (*sutāḥ*)—pressed
- दध्याशिरः (*dadhyāśiraḥ*)—and prepared mixed with curds
- सोमासः (*somāsaḥ*)—Soma-juices
- पवित्रमति (*pavitramati*)—crossing the ten-fold filter
- अक्षरन् (*akṣaran*)—flow on

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Soma-juices, pressed for the sake of Indra who bears the thunderbolt weapon and prepared mixed with curds and other binding substances, flow on across the ten-fold filter.

##### English translation
The Soma-juices mixed with curds effused for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, flow through the filter.

Soma, pour into the filter to bring us wealth (your joice), which is most sweet-flavoured, exhilarating, and most desired by the gods. **NOTE**

- वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*)—endowed with strength

- इंदुं (*iṃduṃ*)—Soma
- आयवः (*āyavaḥ*)—the priests
- नदीषु (*nadīṣu*)—in the waters called Vasatīvarī
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for the sake of Indra
- मृजंति (*mṛjaṃti*)—they cleanse

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The priests cleanse this well-known Soma, green-hued, strong and intoxicating, in the waters called Vasatīvarī, for the sake of Indra.

The priests cleanse in the (Vasativari) waters the green-tinted powerful exhilarating Indu for Indra.

### Printed p. 243

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम त्वं हिरण्यवत् सुवर्णोपेतम् अश्ववत् अश्वयुक्तं च वीरवत् पुत्राद्युपेतं च धनम् आ पवस्व अस्मान् प्रति क्षर । अपि च गोमंतं पशुभिरुपेतं वाजम् अन्नम् आ भर अस्मभ्यमाहर ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, flow (pavasva) towards us, that is, pour down upon us, wealth that is possessed of gold, possessed of horses and possessed of heroes, that is, endowed with sons and the like. Further, bring (bhara) to us, that is, fetch for us, food (vāja) endowed with cattle.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- हिरण्यवत् (*hiraṇyavat*)—endowed with gold
- अश्ववत् (*aśvavat*)—endowed with horses
- वीरवत् (*vīravat*)—accompanied by heroic sons, such wealth
- आ पवस्व (*ā pavasva*)—cause to flow to us
- गोमंतं (*gomaṃtaṃ*)—endowed with cattle
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—food
- आ भर (*ā bhara*)—provide for us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, cause to flow towards us wealth that is endowed with gold, endowed with horses and accompanied by heroic sons. Provide us with food endowed with cattle.

##### English translation
Soma, pour forth wealth of gold, horses. and male offspring ; bring us food and cattle.

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This same Soma, the showerer (vṛṣan), flows (arṣati) in a stream, making a sound (kanikrat). The section number 33 is printed at the end of the block.

- धीभिः (*dhībhiḥ*)—with their fingers
- मर्ज्यं (*marjyaṃ*)—fit to be purified
- कविं (*kaviṃ*)—Soma-deva, whose action is full of wisdom
- मृजंति (*mṛjaṃti*)—they purify
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—Soma, the showerer of desires
- कनिक्रत् (*kanikrat*)—making a sound
- अर्षति (*arṣati*)—flows in the form of a stream

The priests, who desire protection and are wise, purify with their fingers Soma-deva, who is fit to be purified and whose action is full of wisdom. Soma-deva, the showerer of desires, flows in the form of a stream, making a sound.

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वृषणम् । धीभिः । अप्ऽतुरम् । सोमम् । ऋतस्य । धारया ।  
> मती । विप्राः । सम् । अस्वरन् ॥ २१ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विप्राः मेधाविन ऋत्विजः वृषणं कामानां वर्षकम् अप्तुरम् अपां प्रेरकं सोमं धीभिः अंगुलीभिः मती मत्या स्तुत्या च ऋतस्य उदकस्य धारया समस्वरन् प्रेरयंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The wise priests (vipra) bring together (samasvaran), that is, set in motion, Soma, the showerer of desires (vṛṣan) and impeller of the waters (aptur), with their fingers (dhībhiḥ), with thought (matī), that is, with praise, and with the stream of water (ṛtasya dhārayā).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विप्राः (*viprāḥ*)—the wise priests
- वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*)—the showerer of desires
- अप्तूरं (*aptūraṃ*)—one who pours out water, such
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—Soma
- धीभिः (*dhībhiḥ*)—with the fingers
- मती (*matī*)—and with praise
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of water
- धारया (*dhārayā*)—with the stream
- समस्वरन् (*samasvaran*)—they cause to unite

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The wise priests cause Soma, the showerer of desires and the one who pours out water, to unite with the stream of water, both with their fingers and with praise.

### Printed p. 246

##### English translation
The wise (priests) in a stream of water send forth with their fingers and with praise the sprinkler (of benefits), the shedder of water.

#### Ṛk 22

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पव॑स्व देवायु॒षगिंद्रं॑ गच्छतु ते॒ मदः॑ ।  
> वा॒युमा रो॑ह॒ धर्म॑णा ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पवस्व । देव । आयुषक् । इंद्रम् । गच्छतु । ते । मदः ।  
> वायुम् । आ । रोह । धर्मणा ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे देव द्योतमान सोम पवस्व धारया क्षर । अपि च ते तव मदः मदकरो रसः आयुषक् अनुषक्तम् इंद्रं प्रति गच्छतु । अपि च त्वं वायुं धर्मणा धारकेण रसेन आ रोह प्राप्नुहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O shining (deva) Soma, flow (pavasva), that is, pour in a stream. Further, may your intoxicating juice (madaḥ) go continuously (āyuṣak, explained as anuṣaktam) towards Indra. And you, rise upon (ā roha), that is, reach, Vāyu with your supporting (dharmaṇā) juice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देव (*deva*)—O shining Soma-deva
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow in the form of a stream
- तेनिन्न (*teninna*)—your **NOTE**
- मदः (*madaḥ*)—the gladdening juice
- आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*)—always **NOTE**
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—towards Indra
- गच्छतु (*gacchatu*)—may it flow
- धर्मणा (*dharmaṇā*)—with the juice that supports the world
- वायुं (*vāyuṃ*)—Vāyu-deva **NOTE**
- आ रोह (*ā roha*)—approach and join

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O shining Soma-deva, flow in the form of a stream. May your gladdening juice always flow towards Indra. With your juice that supports the world, approach Vāyu-deva and join him.

##### English translation
Flow, brilliant (Soma), let your exhilarating juice proceed in continuous order to Indra, rise with your supporting (juice) to Vayu.

#### Ṛk 23

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पव॑मान॒ नि तो॑शसे र॒यिं सो॑म श्र॒वाय्य॑म् ।  
> प्रि॒यः स॑मु॒द्रमा वि॑श ॥ २३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पवमान । नि । तोशसे । रयिम् । सोम । श्रवाय्यम् ।  
> प्रियः । समुद्रम् । आ । विश ॥ २३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पवमान सोम यस्त्वं श्रवाय्यं श्रवणीयं रयिं शत्रूणां धनं नि तोशसे नितरां पीडयसि स त्वं प्रियः सन् समुद्रं द्रोणकलशम् आ विश प्रविश ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O purifying (pavamāna) Soma, you who press down hard (ni tośase), that is, afflict greatly, the famous (śravāyya, that is, "worth hearing of") wealth (rayi) of enemies, being dear (priya), enter (ā viśa), that is, go into, the ocean (samudra), the Droṇa-kalaśa vessel.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पवमान (*pavamāna*)—O purifier
- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- श्रवाय्यं (*śravāyyaṃ*)—the famous
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—the wealth of enemies
- नि तोशसे (*ni tośase*)—you carry off
- प्रियः (*priyaḥ*)—being one who does what is dear to all of us
- समुद्रं (*samudraṃ*)—the Droṇa-kalaśa
- आ विश (*ā viśa*)—enter

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, the purifier, you carry off all the famous wealth of enemies. Being one who does what is dear to all of us, enter the Droṇa-kalaśa.

##### English translation
Purified Soma, you squeeze forth the celebrated riches (of the enemy) ; do you who are beloved enter the ocean.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒प॒घ्नन्प॑वसे॒ मृधः॑ क्रतु॒वित्सो॑म मत्स॒रः ।  
> नु॒दस्वादे॑वयुं॒ जन॑म् ॥ २४ ॥

### Printed p. 248

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अपऽघ्नन् । पवसे । मृधः । क्रतुऽवित् । सोम । मत्सरः ।  
> नुदस्व । अदेवऽयुम् । जनम् ॥ २४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम मत्सरः मदकरो यस्त्वं मृधः हिंसकान् शत्रून् अपघ्नन् मारयन् क्रतुवित् अस्मभ्यं प्रज्ञां प्रयच्छन् पवसे क्षरसि स त्वम् अदेवयुम् अदेवकामं जनं राक्षसवर्गं नुदस्व प्रेरय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, you who are intoxicating (matsara), slaying (apaghnan) the harmful (mṛdhaḥ) enemies and bestowing wisdom (kratuvit, explained as "giving us understanding") upon us, flow (pavase), that is, stream. Such as you are, drive away (nudasva), that is, impel, the people who do not desire the gods (adevayu), the class of Rākṣasas.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- मत्सरः (*matsaraḥ*)—you who gladden
- मृधः (*mṛdhaḥ*)—the harmful enemies
- अपघ्नन् (*apaghnan*)—destroying
- क्रतुवित् (*kratuvit*)—desiring to produce wisdom in us
- पवसे (*pavase*)—you flow
- अदेवयुं (*adevayuṃ*)—who is not a worshipper of the gods
- जनं (*janaṃ*)—the unbeliever
- नुदस्व (*nudasva*)—strike down

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you who gladden, flow, destroying the harmful enemies and desiring to produce wisdom in us. Strike down the unbeliever who does not worship the gods.

##### English translation
Soma, you who are exhilarating, flow defeating the enemies, bestowing knowledge (on us); drive off the people who love not the gods.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> शुक्रासः उज्ज्वलाः इंदवः दीप्ताः पवमानाः क्षरंतः सोमाः विश्वानि काव्या काव्यानि स्तोत्राणि अभि असृक्षत सृज्यंत ऋत्विग्भिः ॥ ॥ ३४ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The bright (śukrāsaḥ) and shining (indavaḥ) Soma-juices, flowing and purifying (pavamānāḥ), are produced (asṛkṣata, explained as "are created") by the priests as all songs of praise (viśvāni kāvyā, explained as "praises"). The section number 34 is printed at the end of the block.

- शुक्रासः (*śukrāsaḥ*)—radiant
- इंदवः (*iṃdavaḥ*)—flowing
- पवमानाः (*pavamānāḥ*)—and purifying
- सोमाः (*somāḥ*)—the Soma-juices
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all
- काव्या (*kāvyā*)—the songs of praise
- अभ्यसृक्षत (*abhyasṛkṣata*)—they cause to be produced by the priests

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Soma-juices, radiant, flowing and purifying, cause all the songs of praise to be produced by the priests.

##### English translation
The brilliant purified Soma-juices are let fall amidst all praises.

> घ्नंतो॒ विश्वा॒ अप॒ द्विषः॑ ॥ २६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> घ्नंतः । विश्वाः । अप । द्विषः ॥ २६ ॥

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आशवः (*āśavaḥ*)—swift-moving
- शुभ्राः (*śubhrāḥ*)—shining
- पवमानासः (*pavamānāsaḥ*)—and flowing
- इंदवः (*iṃdavaḥ*)—the Soma-juices
- विश्वाः (*viśvāḥ*)—all
- द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)—enemies
- अप घ्नंतः (*apa ghnaṃtaḥ*)—destroying
- अस्यग्रं (*asyagraṃ*)—they are produced **NOTE**

### Printed p. 250

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Soma-juices, swift-flowing, shining and purifying, are produced, destroying all enemies.

The purified Soma-juices flow swift and bright, destroying enemies.

#### Ṛk 27

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पव॑माना दि॒वस्पर्यं॒तरि॑क्षादसृक्षत ।  
> पृ॒थि॒व्या अधि॒ सान॑वि ॥ २७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पवमानाः । दिवः । परि । अंतरिक्षात् । असृक्षत ।  
> पृथिव्याः । अधि । सानवि ॥ २७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पवमानाः सोमाः दिवः द्युलोकात् अंतरिक्षात् च पृथिव्याः भूम्याः अधि सानवि समुच्छ्रिते देशे देवयजने परि असृक्षत सृज्यंते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The purifying (pavamānāḥ) Soma-juices are produced (asṛkṣata) from heaven (divaḥ), that is, from the world of heaven, and from the atmosphere, upon the earth (pṛthivyāḥ adhi), at the high (sānavi) place, that is, the place of the sacrifice to the gods.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पवमानाः (*pavamānāḥ*)—the purifying Soma-juices
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—from the world of heaven
- अंतरिक्षात् (*aṃtarikṣāt*)—and from the atmosphere
- पृथिव्याः अधि (*pṛthivyāḥ adhi*)—upon the earth
- सानवि (*sānavi*)—in the very high place of sacrifice
- पर्यसृक्षत (*paryasṛkṣata*)—they are produced and poured

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The purifying Soma-juices are produced and poured upon the earth, in the very high place of sacrifice, both from the world of heaven and from the atmosphere.

##### English translation
The purified (juices) are poured forth from heaven aad from the firmament upon the summit of the ground. **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O radiant Soma-deva, performer of excellent action, you who bring about purification with your stream, destroy all the enemies and the Rākṣasas.

Brilliani Soma, do you, purified in a stream, achieving great acts, destroy all foes and the Rakshasas. **NOTE**

- रक्षसः (*rakṣasaḥ*)—the Rākṣasas
- अपघ्नन् (*apaghnan*)—destroying
- कनिक्रदत् (*kanikradat*)—and making a sound
- द्युमंतं (*dyumaṃtaṃ*)—radiant
- उत्तमं (*uttamaṃ*)—and excellent
- शुष्मं (*śuṣmaṃ*)—strength
- अभ्यर्ष (*abhyarṣa*)—cause to come to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, destroying the Rākṣasas and making a sound, cause radiant and excellent strength to come to us.

##### English translation
Destroying the Rakshasas, pour forth, Soma, with a noise, brilliant and excellent vigour.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंदो दीप्त सोम दिव्यानि दिवि भवानि पार्थिवा पार्थिवानि पृथिव्यां जातानि च विश्वानि सर्वाणि वार्या वार्याणि वरणीयानि वसूनि अस्मे अस्मासु धारय प्रक्षिप ॥ ॥ ३५ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O shining (indo) Soma, place (dhāraya), that is, put, in us (asme) all (viśvāni) desirable (vāryā) treasures (vasūni), those that belong to heaven (divyāni) and those born on earth (pārthivā). The section number 35 is printed at the end of the block.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O radiant
- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- दिव्यानि (*divyāni*)—those born in the world of heaven
- पार्थिवौ (*pārthivau*)—those born on the earth **NOTE**
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all
- वार्या (*vāryā*)—and desired
- वसूनि (*vasūni*)—treasures
- अस्मे (*asme*)—to us
- धारय (*dhāraya*)—bring and provide

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O radiant Soma-deva, cause all the treasures, those born in the world of heaven and those born on the earth, and fully desired, to come to us.

##### English translation
Bestow upon us, Soma, celestial and terrestrial treasnres : (bestow), Indu, all desirable things. **NOTE**

## Sūkta 64 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘वृषा सोम' इति त्रिंशदृचं चतुर्थं सूक्तं मारीचस्य कश्यपस्यार्षं गायत्रं पवमानसौम्यम् । तथा चानुक्रांतं- वृषा सोम कश्यपः' इति । उक्तो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta "vṛṣā soma" is the fourth sūkta of the thirty-verse set; its seer is Kaśyapa, son of Marīci; the metre is Gāyatrī; the deity is Pavamāna Soma. He cites the Anukramaṇī, "vṛṣā soma kaśyapaḥ". The ritual use has been stated.

Anuvāda: This sūkta, "vṛṣā soma", is the fourth sūkta in the third Anuvāka. It has thirty Ṛks. Its seer is Mārīca Kāśyapa; its deity is Pavamāna Soma; its metre is Gāyatrī. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said "vṛṣā somaḥ kaśyapaḥ". The ritual use was stated earlier.

Sūkta 64.

Maṇḍala 9; Anuvāka 3; Sūkta 64.

Aṣṭaka 7; Adhyāya 1; Vargas 36, 37, 38, 39, 40, 41.

Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 30.

Seer: Kaśyapa.

Deity: Pavamāna Soma.

Metre: Gāyatrī. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वृषा॑ सोम द्यु॒माँ अ॑सि॒ वृषा॑ देव॒ वृष॑व्रतः ।  
> वृषा॒ धर्मा॑णि दधिषे ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वृषा । सोम । द्युऽमान् । असि । वृषा । देव । वृषऽव्रतः ।  
> वृषा । धर्माणि । दधिषे ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम वृषा वर्षकस्त्वं द्युमान् दीप्तिमान् असि । अपि च हे देव द्योतमान सोम वृषा त्वं वृषव्रतः वर्षणशीलकर्मासि । किंच हे सोम वृषा त्वं धर्माणि देवानां मनुष्याणां च हितानि कर्माणि दधिषे धारयसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, you, the showerer (vṛṣā), are bright (dyumān). Further, O shining (deva) Soma, you, the showerer, are one whose ordinary course of action is showering (vṛṣavrataḥ). Further, O Soma, you, the showerer, bear (dadhiṣe), that is, uphold, the rites (dharmāṇi), meaning the actions that are beneficial to gods and men.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—you, the bestower of what is wished for
- द्युमान् (*dyumān*)—radiant
- असि (*asi*)—you are
- देव (*deva*)—O Soma, of the nature of a deity
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—you, the showerer of desires
- वृषव्रतः (*vṛṣavrataḥ*)—you have an action that bestows what is wished for
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—you, the showerer of desires
- धर्माणि (*dharmāṇi*)—the actions that support all
- दधिषे (*dadhiṣe*)—you possess

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you, the bestower of what is wished for, are radiant. O Soma, of the nature of a deity, you, the showerer of desires, have an action that bestows what is wished for. You, the showerer of desires, possess the actions that support all.

##### English translation
You, Soma, are the bright sprinkler; you shining (Soma) are the sprinkler whose occupation is sprinkling ; you, the sprinkler, sustain the rites (of men and gods).

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वृष्ण॑स्ते॒ वृष्ण्यं॒ शवो॒ वृषा॒ वनं॒ वृषा॒ मदः॑ ।  
> स॒त्यं वृ॑ष॒न्वृषेद॑सि ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वृष्णः । ते । वृष्ण्यम् । शवः । वृषा । वनम् । वृषा । मदः ।  
> सत्यम् । वृषन् । वृषा । इत् । असि ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वृषन् कामानां वर्षक सोम वृष्णः वर्षितुः ते तव शवः बलं वृष्ण्यं वर्षणशीलं भवति । वनं तव भजनमपि वृषा वर्षणशीलम् । मदः तव रसोऽपि वृषा वर्षणशीलः । सत्यं सत्यमेव त्वं वृषेत् वर्षणशील एव असि भवसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O showerer (vṛṣan) of desires, Soma, your strength (śavaḥ) as the showerer (vṛṣṇaḥ) is showering in nature (vṛṣṇyam). Your worship (vanam) too is showering in nature. Your juice (madaḥ) too is showering in nature. Truly (satyam) you are indeed (vṛṣed) showering in nature.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृषन् (*vṛṣan*)—O Soma-deva, the showerer of desires
- वृष्णः (*vṛṣṇaḥ*)—you who bestow what is wished for
- ते (*te*)—your
- शवः (*śavaḥ*)—strength
- वृष्णं (*vṛṣṇaṃ*)—is such as gives what is desired **NOTE**
- वनं (*vanaṃ*)—your drinking too
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—is such as bestows what is wished for
- मदः (*madaḥ*)—your gladdening juice too
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—is a showerer of desires
- सत्यं (*satyaṃ*)—certainly
- वृषेत् (*vṛṣet*)—you indeed, the bestower of what is wished for
- असि (*asi*)—you are

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, showerer of desires, your strength, you who bestow what is wished for, is such as gives what is desired. Your drinking too is such as bestows what is wished for. Your gladdening juice too is a showerer of desires. Certainly you are indeed a bestower of what is wished for.

##### English translation
O sprinkler, the strength of you the sprinkler consists in sprinkling, your worship consists in sprinkling your juice consists in sprinkling; you truly are always. the sprinkler.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वि नो॑ रा॒ये दुरो॑ वृधि ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 256

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अश्वः । न । चक्रदः । वृषा । सम् । गाः । इंदो इति । सम् । अर्वतः ।  
> वि । नः । राये । दुरः । वृधि ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंदो सोम वृषा त्वम् अश्वो न अश्व इव सं चक्रदः संक्रंदसे । अपि च गाः पशून् अर्वतः अश्वांश्चास्मभ्यं सं प्रयच्छसीति शेषः। किंच नः अस्माकं राये धनाय दुरः द्वाराणि वि वृधि विवृतानि कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O shining Soma, you, the showerer, bellow (saṃ cakradaḥ) like a horse. Further, the verb "you give (saṃ prayacchasi)" is to be supplied: you give us cattle (gāḥ) and horses (arvataḥ). Further, open wide (vi vṛdhi), that is, make open, the doors (duraḥ) for our wealth (rāye).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma-deva
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—you, the bestower of what is wished for
- अश्वो न (*aśvo na*)—like a horse
- सं चक्रदः (*saṃ cakradaḥ*)—you make a sound
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—cattle
- अर्वतः (*arvataḥ*)—and horses
- सं (*saṃ*)—give
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- राये (*rāye*)—for the attainment of wealth
- दुरः (*duraḥ*)—the doors
- वि वृधि (*vi vṛdhi*)—open fully

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you, the bestower of what is wished for, make a sound like a horse. Open fully the doors that lead to the attainment of our wealth.

##### English translation
Indu, the sprinkler, you neigh like a horse; you give us cattle, you give us horses; open the doors for our wealth.
