#### Ṛk 16

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> राजा॑ मे॒धाभि॑रीयते॒ पव॑मानो म॒नावधि॑ ।  
> अं॒तरि॑क्षेण॒ यात॑वे ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> राजा । मेधाभिः । ईयते । पवमानः । मनौ । अधि ।  
> अंतरिक्षेण । यातवे ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मनौ मनुष्ये यागं कुर्वाणे सति । यद्वा । मनावधि । मनुर्मंतव्यो यज्ञः । तस्मिन् पवमानः पूयमानः पुनानो वा राजा । राजशब्देन सोमोऽभिधीयते । सोमं राजानमक्रीणन् ' (ऐ. ब्रा. १.२७) इत्यादिषु दृष्टत्वात् । स राजा मेधाभिः स्तुतिभिः सह ईयते गच्छति । किमर्थम् । अंतरिक्षेण आकाशमार्गेण द्रोणकलशं प्रति यातवे यातुम् । द्रोणाभिगमनकाले हि स्तोतृभिः स्तूयते खलु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

मनौ (*manau*): when man is performing the sacrifice. Or else, मनावधि (*manāvadhi*): मनुर्मंतव्यो (*manurmaṃtavyo*): Manu is the sacrifice, which is to be thought of; in it Pavamāna, being purified or purifying, is राजा (*rājā*), the king: by the word king Soma is meant, as is seen in such passages as सोमं राजानमक्रीणन् (*somaṃ rājānamakrīṇan*) (Ai. Brā. 1.27). That king goes together with मेधाभिः (*medhābhiḥ*), praises. For what? यातवे (*yātave*), to go to the Droṇa-kalaśa by the path of the sky, the atmosphere; for at the time of going to the Droṇa he is praised by the singers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मनौ अधि (*manau adhi*)—at the time of the sacrifice
- पवमानः (*pavamānaḥ*)—the purifier
- राजा (*rājā*)—the lord
- अंतरिक्षेण (*aṃtarikṣeṇa*)—by the path of the atmosphere
- यातने (*yātane*)**NOTE**—to go and join the Droṇa-kalaśa
- मेधाभिः (*medhābhiḥ*)—with praises
- ईयते (*īyate*)—flows

### Printed p. 296

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma, the purifier and the lord, travels at the time of the sacrifice by the path of the atmosphere, with praises, to go and join the Droṇa-kalaśa.

##### English translation
The king (Soma) purified at the sacrifice is urged by the priests to pass through the firmament.

#### Ṛk 17

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ न॑ इंदो शत॒ग्विनं॒ गवां॒ पोषं॒ स्वश्व्य॑म् ।  
> वहा॒ भग॑त्तिमू॒तये॑ ॥ १७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । नः । इंदो इति । शतऽग्विनम् । गवाम् । पोषम् । सुऽअश्व्यम् ।  
> वह । भगत्तिम् । ऊतये ॥ १७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंदो पात्रेषु क्षरणशील दीपनशील वा हे सोम शतग्विनं शतसहस्रसंख्याभिर्गोभिर्युक्तं गवां पोषं गवादीनां पुष्टिवर्धनं स्वश्व्यं शोभनाश्वसंगसहितं भगत्तिं भगदत्तिं भजनीयधनदानं च ऊतये रक्षणाय नः अस्माकम् आ वह प्रापय । गवादींश्च तेषां च वृद्धिं प्रयच्छेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indu, flowing in the vessels or shining; O Soma, bring to us, for protection, शतग्विनं (*śatagvinaṃ*), endowed with hundreds of thousands of cows; गवां पोषं (*gavāṃ poṣaṃ*), the increase of nourishment of cows and the like; स्वश्व्यं (*svaśvyaṃ*), accompanied by good horses; and भगत्तिं (*bhagattiṃ*), the gift of Bhaga, the bestowal of wealth that is to be shared. आ वह (*ā vaha*), cause to reach us. The meaning is: give cows and the like, and their increase.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma-deva
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- ऊतये (*ūtaye*)—for protection
- शतग्विनं (*śatagvinaṃ*)—accompanied by many cows
- गवां (*gavāṃ*)—for cows
- पोषं (*poṣaṃ*)—nourishing
- स्वश्वं (*svaśvaṃ*)**NOTE**—accompanied by excellent horses
- भगत्तिं (*bhagattiṃ*)—venerable wealth
- आ वह (*ā vaha*)—provide to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, for our protection, provide for us wealth accompanied by many cows, nourishing for cows, and accompanied by excellent horses.

### Printed p. 297

##### English translation
Bring to us, Indu, for our protection increase of cows with hundreds of cattle and a gift of fortune with beautiful horses.

#### Ṛk 18

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ नः॑ सोम॒ सहो॒ जुवो॑ रू॒पं न वर्च॑से भर ।  
> सु॒ष्वा॒णो दे॒ववी॑तये ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । नः । सोम । सहः । जुवः । रूपम् । न । वर्चसे । भर ।  
> सुस्वानः । देवऽवीतये ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम देववीतये देवपानाय देवानां कामाय वा सुष्वाणः अभिषूयमाणोऽभिषुतो भव त्वम् । सहः शत्र्वभिभवनसमर्थं बलं जुवः । जु इति गत्यर्थः। शत्रून् प्रति शीघ्रगमनं च । यद्वा । सर्वतो गमनशीलं बलं च । न इति चार्थे । वर्चसे ।  वर्च दीप्तौ । दीप्त्यै सर्वत्र प्रकाशनाय रूपं च नः अस्मभ्यम् आ भर आहर प्रयच्छ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, you are to be pressed for the drinking of the gods, or for the desire of the gods (देववीतये (*devavītaye*)). Bring (आ भर (*ā bhara*): fetch, bestow) to us सहः (*sahaḥ*), strength able to overcome enemies; जुवः (*juvaḥ*), from the root जु (*ju*) meaning going, swift going against the enemies, or alternatively strength that moves in every direction; न (*na*) is used in the sense of "and"; and for वर्चसे (*varcase*), from the root वर्च (*varca*) meaning shining, for brilliance, for shining everywhere, a form.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- देवनीतये (*devanītaye*)**NOTE**—for the drinking of the gods
- सुष्वाणः (*suṣvāṇaḥ*)—become one who is pressed
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- सहः (*sahaḥ*)—strength that destroys enemies
- जुवः (*juvaḥ*)—speed of going
- वर्चसे (*varcase*)—for brilliance
- रूपं (*rūpaṃ*)—a form
- आ भर (*ā bhara*)—provide

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, become pressed for the drinking of the gods. Provide for us strength that destroys enemies, speed that moves everywhere, and an excellent form that is a means of brilliance.

##### English translation
(Be) expressed for the banquet of the gods: bestow on us, Soma, strength, speed and a form for brilliance.

### Printed p. 298

#### Ṛk 19

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अर्षा॑ सोम द्यु॒मत्त॑मो॒ऽभि द्रोणा॑नि॒ रोरु॑वत् ।  
> सीदं॑छ्ये॒नो न योनि॒मा ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अर्ष । सोम । द्युमत्ऽतमः । अभि । द्रोणानि । रोरुवत् ।  
> सीदन् । श्येनः । न । योनिम् । आ ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम अभिषूयमाण पवमान द्युमत्तमः अतिशयेन दीप्तिमांस्त्वं द्रोणानि । प्रयोगबाहुल्यापेक्षमेतद्बहुवचनम् । द्रोणान् अभि लक्षीकृत्य रोरुवत् पुनःपुनर्भृशं वा शब्दं कुर्वन् अर्ष तानागच्छ। दशापवित्रमध्यान्निर्गतः सोमोऽविच्छिन्नधारया द्रोणकलशे पतन् शब्दं करोति खलु। तत्र दृष्टांतः । श्येनो न यथा आ सीदन् सर्वतो गच्छन् श्येनः शंसनीयगतिः पक्षी योनिं स्वस्थानं कुलायं प्रति भृशं शब्दायमानः सन्नागच्छति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, being pressed and purifying, you who are most radiant, roaring again and again, or loudly, toward the Droṇa vessels, flow to them. The plural द्रोणानि (*droṇāni*) is used with regard to the frequency of use. Soma, issuing from the middle of the ten-fold filter with an unbroken stream and falling into the Droṇa vessel, indeed makes a sound. The example: just as a hawk (श्येनः (*śyenaḥ*)), a bird of praiseworthy flight, coming from all sides, makes a loud noise and comes to its own place, its nest, so does Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- योनिं (*yoniṃ*)—to reach his own nest
- आ सीदन् (*ā sīdan*)—of praiseworthy flight
- श्येनो न (*śyeno na*)—as the hawk goes swiftly and making sound
- द्युमत्तमः (*dyumattamaḥ*)—you who are of exceeding radiance
- द्रोणानि अभि (*droṇāni abhi*)—facing the Droṇa vessels
- रोरुवत् (*roruvat*)—making sound
- अर्ष (*arṣa*)—move

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, as a hawk of praiseworthy flight goes swiftly and with noise when reaching its nest, so you, of exceeding radiance, move toward the Droṇa vessels making sound.

##### English translation
Hasten, Soma, who are most radiant, with a roar to the wooden vessels; as a hawk flying to its nest.

### Printed p. 299

#### Ṛk 20

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒प्सा इंद्रा॑य वा॒यवे॒ वरु॑णाय म॒रुद्भ्यः॑ ।  
> सोमो॑ अर्षति॒ विष्ण॑वे ॥ २० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अप्साः । इंद्राय । वायवे । वरुणाय । मरुत्ऽभ्यः ।  
> सोमः । अर्षति । विष्णवे ॥ २० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अप्साः वसतीवरीनामधेयानामपां संभक्ता । ‘षण संभक्तौ । जनसन ' इति विट् । आत्वं ‘ विड्वनोः' इति । तादृशः सोमः अर्षति द्रोणकलशमागच्छति । किमर्थम्। इंद्राय । सर्वदेवानां प्रथम एवेंद्रः सोमं पिबति तस्मात्पूर्वमेवाभिहितः । तस्मै वायवे तत्सहायाय च । ऐंद्रवायवे हींद्रस्यानंतरं वायुः सोमं पिबति तस्मात्तदनु वायुरुक्तः । तस्मै च वरुणाय मरुद्भ्यः  मितं शब्दं कुर्वद्भ्य एतन्नामकेभ्यो देवेभ्यः विष्णवे सर्वजगद्व्यापिने विष्णवे च । एतेषां पातुं सोमः स्रवतीत्यर्थः ॥ ॥ ४ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

अप्साः (*apsāḥ*) is the one who shares the waters called Vasatīvarī. Such a Soma flows to, reaches, the Droṇa vessel. For what purpose? For Indra: among all the gods Indra drinks Soma first, therefore he is named first. For Vāyu, his companion: in the Aindravāya (cup) Vāyu drinks Soma after Indra, therefore Vāyu is mentioned next. For Varuṇa, for the Maruts, the gods of that name who make a measured sound, and for Viṣṇu, who pervades the whole world. The meaning is that Soma flows for these to drink.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अप्साः (*apsāḥ*)—mingling with the water called Vasatīvarī
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra
- वायवे (*vāyave*)—for Vāyu
- वरुणाय (*varuṇāya*)—for Varuṇa
- मरुद्भ्यः (*marudbhyaḥ*)—for the Maruts
- विष्णवे (*viṣṇave*)—for Viṣṇu, to become fit for drinking
- अर्षति (*arṣati*)—goes to the Droṇa vessel and joins it

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma, who mingles with the water called Vasatīvarī, goes to the Droṇa vessel and joins it, to become fit for the drinking of the gods Indra, Vāyu, the Maruts, Varuṇa and Viṣṇu.

##### English translation
Soma, the enjoyer of the water, hasten (to the vessels) for Indra, Vayu, Varuna, the Maruts, and Vishnu.

### Printed p. 300

#### Ṛk 21

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इषं॑ तो॒काय॑ नो॒ दध॑द॒स्मभ्यं॑ सोम वि॒श्वतः॑ ।  
> आ प॑वस्व सह॒स्रिण॑म् ॥ २१ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इषम् । तोकाय । नः । दधत् । अस्मभ्यम् । सोम । विश्वतः ।  
> आ । पवस्व । सहस्रिणम् ॥ २१ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम त्वं नः अस्माकं तोकाय पुत्राय इषम् अन्नं दधत् विदधत् प्रयच्छन् सहस्रिणं सहस्रसंख्याकं धनं विश्वतः सर्वतो दिक्षु अस्मभ्यं च आ पवस्व आप्रापय । अस्मभ्यं पुत्राय च अन्नधनादिकं प्रयच्छेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, bestowing (दधत् (*dadhat*): giving) food (इषं (*iṣaṃ*)) upon our son, flow to (आ पवस्व (*ā pavasva*): bring to) us from all sides, in all directions, wealth in thousands (सहस्रिणं (*sahasriṇaṃ*)). The meaning is: give food, wealth and the like to us and to our son.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- नः-नम्म (*naḥ-namma*)—our
- तोकाय-पुत्ररिगॆ (*tokāya-putrarigè*)—to sons
- इषं-अन्न (*iṣaṃ-anna*)—food
- दधत्-कॊडुत्त (*dadhat-kòḍutta*)—giving
- अस्मभ्यं-नमगॆ (*asmabhyaṃ-namagè*)—to us
- विश्वतः-ऎल्ला (*viśvataḥ-èllā*)—from all sides
- सहस्रिणंसहस्र (*sahasriṇaṃsahasra*)—wealth of thousandfold number
- आ पवस्व-तुंबुवंतॆ (*ā pavasva-tuṃbuvaṃtè*)—cause to fill

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, giving food to our sons, provide us from all sides with wealth of a thousandfold number.

##### English translation
Bestowing food upon our offspring, Soma, pour from all quarters thousand-fold (wealth).

#### Ṛk 22

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ये सोमा॑सः परा॒वति॒ ये अ॑र्वा॒वति॑ सुन्वि॒रे ।  
> ये वा॒दः श॑र्य॒णाव॑ति ॥ २२ ॥

### Printed p. 301

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ये । सोमासः । पराऽवति । ये । अर्वाऽवति । सुन्विरे ।  
> ये । वा । अदः । शर्यणाऽवति ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एतदादिभ्यामृग्भ्यामिंद्रार्थं सर्वत्र सोमाभिषवोऽस्तीत्याह । ये सोमासः सोमाः परावति विप्रकृष्टेऽतिदूरे देशे ये वा अर्वावति अंतिके देश इंद्रार्थं सुन्विरे अभिषूयंते अभ्यषूयंत ये वा शर्यणावति । कुरुक्षेत्रस्य जघनार्धे शर्यणावत्संज्ञकं मधुररसयुक्तं सोमवत्सरोऽस्ति । अदः अस्मिन् सरसि सुरसा ये सोमाः इंद्रायाभिषूयंते तेऽस्माकमभिमतफलं प्रयच्छंत्विति वक्ष्यमाणेन संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By this Ṛk and those that follow, Sāyaṇa says that Soma is pressed everywhere for Indra. The Soma juices that are pressed for Indra in a distant, very remote place, or those in a near place, or those at Śaryaṇāvat: in the rear half of Kurukṣetra there is a lake called Śaryaṇāvat, endowed with sweet juice. Those well-flavoured Soma juices that are pressed for Indra in this lake: let them grant us the desired fruit, so it connects with what is to be said next.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ये सोमासः (*ye somāsaḥ*)—which Soma-juices
- परावति (*parāvati*)—in a very distant place
- ये (*ye*)—which
- अर्वावति (*arvāvati*)—in a very near region
- सुन्वीरॆ (*sunvīrè*)**NOTE**—are pressed
- ये (*ye*)—which
- ना (*nā*)**NOTE**—which
- शरणावति (*śaraṇāvati*)**NOTE**—called Śaraṇāvat
- अदः (*adaḥ*)—in this lake they are obtained; may all of them be fulfillers of our desired ends

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May those Soma-juices that are pressed for Indra in a very distant place, those in a very near place, and those obtained in this lake called Śaryaṇāvat, all be bestowers of our desired ends.

##### English translation
May those Soma-juices which are effused at a distance or nigh or on this Sharyanavat (lake).—

#### Ṛk 23

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य आ॑र्जी॒केषु॒ कृत्व॑सु॒ ये मध्ये॑ प॒स्त्या॑नाम् ।  
> ये वा॒ जने॑षु पं॒चसु॑ ॥ २३ ॥

### Printed p. 302

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ये । आर्जीकेषु । कृत्वऽसु । ये । मध्ये । पस्त्यानाम् ।  
> ये । वा । जनेषु । पंचऽसु ॥ २३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ये वा सोमाः आर्जीकेषु । ऋजीकानामदूरभवा आर्जीका देशाः । तेषु तथा कृत्वसु । कृत्वान इति देशाभिधानम् । तेषु कर्मवत्सु देशेषु च किंच पस्त्यानां सरस्वत्यादीनां नदीनां मध्ये समीपे च ये सोमा अभिषूयंते । ऋषयो वै सरस्वत्यां सत्रमासत' (ऐ. ब्रा. २.१९) इत्यादिषु नदीतीरे यज्ञकरणस्य श्रवणात् । किंच जनेषु पंचसु । निषादपंचमाश्चत्वारो वर्णाः पंच जनाः । तेषु च ये वा सोमा अभिषुताः ते सोमा अस्माकमभिमतं प्रयच्छंत्वित्युत्तरेण संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Or those Soma juices (pressed) among the Ārjīkas: the Ārjīka countries are those not far from the Ṛjīka; likewise among the Kṛtvas, a name of countries, that is, in lands of ritual action. Further, in the middle, that is, near, the rivers (पस्त्यानां (*pastyānāṃ*)) such as the Sarasvatī, the Soma juices that are pressed; for the performance of sacrifice on river banks is heard of in passages such as ऋषयो वै सरस्वत्यां सत्रमासत (*ṛṣayo vai sarasvatyāṃ satramāsata*) (Ai. Brā. 2.19). Further, among the five peoples: the four castes with the Niṣāda as the fifth are the five peoples; and the Soma juices pressed among them: let those Soma juices grant us what we desire, so it connects with the following Ṛk.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ये (*ye*)—which Soma-juices
- आर्जिकेषु (*ārjikeṣu*)—in the Ārjika countries
- कृत्वसु (*kṛtvasu*)—in the Kṛtva countries, places of ritual action, are obtained
- ये (*ye*)—which juices
- पस्त्यानां (*pastyānāṃ*)—of rivers such as the Sarasvatī
- मध्यॆ (*madhyè*)—are obtained near
- ये वा (*ye vā*)—which juices
- पंचसु जनेषु (*paṃcasu janeṣu*)—among people of five classes beginning with the Niṣādas, are pressed for Indra; let those Soma-juices be bestowers of our desired ends

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May those Soma-juices that are obtained in the Arjīka countries and in the Kṛtva countries, places of ritual action, those juices that are obtained near rivers such as the Sarasvatī, and those juices that are pressed for Indra among people of the five classes beginning with the Niṣādas, be bestowers of our desired ends.

##### English translation
Or amongst the Rijikas, or the Kritwas, or in ihe neighbourhood of the rivers Sarasvati, etc., or in the five castes.—

#### Ṛk 24

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ते नो॑ वृ॒ष्टिं दि॒वस्परि॒ पवं॑ता॒मा सु॒वीर्य॑म् ।  
> सु॒वा॒ना दे॒वास॒ इंद॑वः ॥ २४ ॥

### Printed p. 303

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ते । नः । वृष्टिम् । दिवः । परि । पवंताम् । आ । सुऽवीर्यम् ।  
> सुवानाः । देवासः । इंदवः ॥ २४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुवानाः तत्र चात्र चाभिषूयमाणा देवा दीपनशीलाः स्तुत्या वा इंदवः ग्रहेषु चमसेषु च क्षरंतः ते सोमाः नः अस्माकं दिवस्परि। परिशब्दः पंचमीद्योतकः। अंतरिक्षादादित्याद्वा वृष्टिम् । अग्नौ प्रास्ताहुतिः सम्यगादित्यमुपतिष्ठते । आदित्याज्जायते वृष्टिः' इति वृष्टिकारणत्वात् । किंच सुवीर्यं शोभनवीर्योपेतं पुत्रं च धनादिकं वा आ पवंतां प्रापयंतु । यजमानः सोमेन अभिमतफलानि प्राप्नोति खलु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those Soma juices (इंदवः (*iṃdavaḥ*)), being pressed (सुवानाः (*suvānāḥ*)) there and here, bright or praiseworthy, flowing into the cups and the ladles, let them, for us (नः (*naḥ*)), pour (आ पवंतां (*ā pavaṃtāṃ*): bring) from heaven (दिवस्परि (*divaspari*): the word परि (*pari*) indicates the ablative), from the atmosphere or from the sun, rain (वृष्टिम् (*vṛṣṭim*)), since the sun is the cause of rain: अग्नौ प्रास्ताहुतिः सम्यगादित्यमुपतिष्ठते । आदित्याज्जायते वृष्टिः' (*agnau prāstāhutiḥ samyagādityamupatiṣṭhate | ādityājjāyate vṛṣṭiḥ '*) **GLOSS**. Further, let them bring (सुवीर्यं (*suvīryaṃ*)) a son endowed with good valour, or wealth and the like. The sacrificer indeed obtains the desired fruits through Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—those that are brilliant
- सुवानाः (*suvānāḥ*)—those that are pressed for Indra
- इंदवः (*iṃdavaḥ*)—those that are of the nature of a stream
- ते (*te*)—those Soma-juices
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- दिवस्परि (*divaspari*)—from the atmosphere
- वृष्टिं (*vṛṣṭiṃ*)—rain
- सुवीर‍्यं (*suvīryaṃ*)—wealth possessed of excellent valour
- आ पवंतां (*ā pavaṃtāṃ*)—let them cause to flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the Soma-juices, which are brilliant, pressed for Indra, and of the nature of a stream, cause rain from the atmosphere and wealth possessed of excellent valour to come to us.

##### English translation
May those brilliant Soma-juices when expressed, pour down upon us from heaven, rain with male progeny.

#### Ṛk 25

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पव॑ते हर्य॒तो हरि॑र्गृणा॒नो ज॒मद॑ग्निना ।  
> हि॒न्वा॒नो गोरधि॑ त्व॒चि ॥ २५ ॥

### Printed p. 304

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पवते । हर्यतः । हरिः । गृणानः । जमत्ऽअग्निना ।  
> हिन्वानः । गोः । अधि । त्वचि ॥ २५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हर्यतः देवान् कामयमानः हरिः हरितवर्णः किंच गोः त्वचि अधि आनडुहे चर्मणि हिन्वानः प्रेर्यमाणः स सोमः जमदग्निना मंत्रद्रष्ट्रर्षिणा गृणानः स्तूयमानः सन् पवते दशापवित्रेण पूतो भवति । यद्वा । पात्राण्यभिगच्छति ॥ ॥ ५ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

हर्यतः (*haryataḥ*) is one who desires the gods; हरिः (*hariḥ*) is of green colour. Further, that Soma, urged (हिन्वानः (*hinvānaḥ*)) upon (अधि (*adhi*)) the hide (त्वचि (*tvaci*)) of the cow, that is, the bull's hide, being praised (गृणानः (*gṛṇānaḥ*)) by Jamadagni, the seer of the mantra, flows (पवते (*pavate*)), that is, becomes purified by the ten-fold filter. Or else: he goes to the vessels.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हर्यतः (*haryataḥ*)—one who desires the gods
- हरिः (*hariḥ*)—one who is of green colour
- गोः त्वचिअधि (*goḥ tvaciadhi*)—upon the cow-hide
- हिन्वानः (*hinvānaḥ*)—one who is poured out, Soma
- जमदग्निना (*jamadagninā*)—by the seer Jamadagni
- गृणानः (*gṛṇānaḥ*)—having been praised
- पवते (*pavate*)—flows toward the ten-fold filter

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma, who desires the gods, is of green colour, and is poured upon the cow-hide, having been praised by the seer Jamadagni, flows toward the ten-fold filter.

##### English translation
The delightful green-tinted Soma, praised by Jamadagni, urged on the cow-hide flows (to the vessels.)

#### Ṛk 26

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र शु॒क्रासो॑ वयो॒जुवो॑ हिन्वा॒नासो॒ न सप्त॑यः ।  
> श्री॒णा॒ना अ॒प्सु मृं॑जत ॥ २६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । शुक्रासः । वयःऽजुवः । हिन्वानासः । न । सप्तयः ।  
> श्रीणानाः । अप्ऽसु । मृंजत ॥ २६ ॥

### Printed p. 305

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> शुक्रासः शुक्रा दीप्यमानाः वयोजुवः अन्नं प्रेरयंतः । यद्यदपेक्ष्य देवेभ्यः सोमं प्रयच्छंति तत्तदपेक्षितं सोमो ददाति । ते सोमाः श्रीणानाः दधिक्षीरादिभिः श्रीयमाणाः संतः अप्सु वसतीवरीष्वेकधनासु च मृंजत ऋत्विग्भिः प्रमृज्यंते शोध्यंते । तत्र दृष्टांतः । हिन्वानासो न सप्तयः । अश्वनामैतत् । यथाश्वा हिन्वानासो हिन्वानाः सादिभिः प्रेर्यमाणाः संतोऽप्सु तैरेव प्रशोधिता भवंति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

शुक्रासः (*śukrāsaḥ*) are bright, shining; वयोजुवः (*vayojuvaḥ*) send forth food: whatever they desire when they give Soma to the gods, Soma gives that very thing. Those Soma juices, being mixed (श्रीणानाः (*śrīṇānāḥ*)) with curds, milk and the like, are cleansed, wiped, by the priests in the waters (अप्सु (*apsu*)), the Vasatīvarī waters, and in the Ekadhanā waters. The example: हिन्वानासो न सप्तयः (*hinvānāso na saptayaḥ*); सप्तयः (*saptayaḥ*) is a name of horses. As horses, urged (हिन्वानाः (*hinvānāḥ*)) by their riders, are purified in the waters by those very riders, so are the Soma juices.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शुक्रासः (*śukrāsaḥ*)—those that are shining
- वयोजुवः (*vayojuvaḥ*)—those that are impellers of food, the Soma-juices
- श्रीणानाः (*śrīṇānāḥ*)—mixing with the admixture substances
- अप्पु (*appu*)**NOTE**—in the waters such as Vasatīvarī
- हिन्वानासः (*hinvānāsaḥ*)—urged by the charioteer
- सप्तयः न (*saptayaḥ na*)—like horses
- प्र मृंजत (*pra mṛṃjata*)—attain purification

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As horses urged by charioteers are washed and cleansed with water, so the Soma-juices, which are shining and impellers of food, mixing with the admixture substances, attain purification in the waters such as Vasatīvarī.

##### English translation
The bright Soma-juices, the dispensers of food, being mixed with the curds and milk, are cleansed in the waters like horses urged (by the charioteers).

#### Ṛk 27

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तं त्वा॑ सु॒तेष्वा॒भुवो॑ हिन्वि॒रे दे॒वता॑तये ।  
> स प॑वस्वा॒नया॑ रु॒चा ॥ २७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तम् । त्वा । सुतेषु । आऽभुवः । हिन्विरे । देवऽतातये ।  
> सः । पवस्व । अनया । रुचा ॥ २७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

### Printed p. 306

> अथ प्रत्यक्षकृतः । हे सोम आभुवः । कर्मकरणार्थं समंताद्भवंतीत्याभुव ऋत्विजः । ते सुतेषु । सुतोऽभिषुतः सोमः । तद्वत्सु यज्ञेषु देवतातये । ‘ सर्वदेवात्तातिल्' इति स्वार्थिकस्तातिल् । इंद्रादिदेवेभ्यः तं तादृशं प्रसिद्धं त्वा त्वां हिन्विरे ग्रावभिः प्रेरयंति । अभिषुण्वंतीत्यर्थः । ततः सः अभिषुतः स त्वम् अनया रुचा दीप्यमानया धारया द्रोणकलशं प्रति पवस्व आगच्छ । पवतिर्गतिकर्मा । यद्वा । अनया मदीयया रुचा स्तुत्या सह कलशमागच्छ । कलशाभिगमनकाले हि सोमं स्तुवंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Now addressing him directly: O Soma, the आभुवः (*ābhuvaḥ*) are the priests, who come about on all sides for the performance of the rite. In the pressings (सुतेषु (*suteṣu*)), that is, in sacrifices where Soma is pressed, for the gods (देवतातये (*devatātaye*)), for Indra and the other gods, they send you forth (हिन्विरे (*hinvire*)) with the pressing stones, that is, they press you, the renowned one. Then you, thus pressed, flow (पवस्व (*pavasva*)), come toward the Droṇa vessel with this (अनया (*anayā*)) shining (रुचा (*rucā*)) stream; the root पव (*pava*) means going. Or else: come to the vessel with this praise (रुचा (*rucā*)) of mine; for Soma is praised at the time of approach to the vessel.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आभुवः (*ābhuvaḥ*)—(O Soma-deva) the priests engaged in the rite
- सुतेषु (*suteṣu*)—at the time of your pressing
- देवतातये (*devatātaye*)—for the sacrifice for the worship of the gods
- तं (*taṃ*)—the renowned
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you
- हिन्विरे (*hinvire*)—press with stones
- सः (*saḥ*)—you, thus pressed
- अनया रुचा (*anayā rucā*)—with this shining praise
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow toward the Droṇa vessel

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, the priests engaged in the rite press you, the renowned, with stones at the time of your pressing, for the sacrifice for the worship of the gods. Thus pressed, flow toward the Droṇa vessel with this shining praise.

##### English translation
The priests who are present send you forth at the rites at which you are effused for the whole of the gods; do you flow with this splendour.

#### Ṛk 28

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ ते॒ दक्षं॑ मयो॒भुवं॒ वह्नि॑म॒द्या वृ॑णीमहे ।  
> पांत॒मा पु॑रु॒स्पृह॑म् ॥ २८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । ते । दक्षम् । मयःऽभुवम् । वह्निम् । अद्य । वृणीमहे ।  
> पांतम् । आ । पुरुऽस्पृहम् ॥ २८ ॥

### Printed p. 307

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम यष्टारो वयं ते तव स्वभूतं दक्षं बलम् अद्य अस्मिन् यागदिने आभिमुख्येन आ वृणीमहे संभजामहे। कीदृशम्। मयोभुवं सुखस्य भावकं वह्निं धनादीनां प्रापकं पांतं शत्रुभ्यो रक्षकं पुरुस्पृहं बहुभिः स्पृहणीयं काम्यमानं बलमिति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, we sacrificers today, on this day of the sacrifice, choose (आ वृणीमहे (*ā vṛṇīmahe*): take up, partake of) your (ते (*te*)) own strength (दक्षं (*dakṣaṃ*)), facing it. Of what kind? मयोभुवं (*mayobhuvaṃ*), the producer of happiness; वह्निं (*vahniṃ*), the bringer of wealth and the like; पांतं (*pāṃtaṃ*), the protector from enemies; पुरुस्पृहं (*puruspṛhaṃ*), desired by many, the strength that is wished for.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मयोभुवं (*mayobhuvaṃ*)—(O Soma-deva) that which gives happiness
- वह्निं (*vahniṃ*)—that which brings wealth
- पांतं (*pāṃtaṃ*)—that which protects
- पुरुस्पृहं (*puruspṛhaṃ*)—that which is desired by many
- ते दक्षं (*te dakṣaṃ*)—your extraordinary strength
- अद्य (*adya*)—at this time of the sacrifice
- आ वृणीमहे (*ā vṛṇīmahe*)—we worship (we take refuge in)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, your extraordinary strength, which gives happiness, brings wealth, protects and is desired by many, we worship and take refuge in at this time of the sacrifice.

##### English translation
We have recourse to-day to your strength, the source of happiness, the bearer (of good things), the defender (against foes), the desired of many—

#### Ṛk 29

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ मं॒द्रमा वरे॑ण्य॒मा विप्र॒मा म॑नी॒षिण॑म् ।  
> पांत॒मा पु॑रु॒स्पृह॑म् ॥ २९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । मंद्रम् । आ । वरेण्यम् । आ । विप्रम् । आ । मनीषिणम् ।  
> पांतम् । आ । पुरुऽस्पृहम् ॥ २९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम मंद्रं मदकरं स्तुत्यं वा त्वाम् आ वृणीमहे । वरेण्यं सर्वैर्वरणीयं संभजनीयं च । किंच विप्रं मेधाविनं त्वाम् । तथा मनीषिणम् । मनस ईषा मनीषा। तद्वंतं स्तुतिमंतं वा त्वाम् आ वृणीमहे । प्रत्येकविशेषणापेक्षया आ इत्युपसर्गः कृतः । किंच पांतं सर्वेषां रक्षकं पुरुस्पृहं बहुभिः स्पृहणीयं च त्वां संभजामहे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, we choose you, who are exhilarating (मंद्रं (*maṃdraṃ*)), causing exhilaration, or praiseworthy. वरेण्यं (*vareṇyaṃ*): to be chosen by all and to be shared in. Further, you, the wise (विप्रं (*vipraṃ*)); and likewise मनीषिणम् (*manīṣiṇam*): मनीषा (*manīṣā*) is the impulse of the mind, and one who has it, or one who has praise: you we choose. The prefix आ (*ā*) is repeated with regard to each separate epithet. Further, we partake of you, the protector (पांतं (*pāṃtaṃ*)) of all and desired (पुरुस्पृहं (*puruspṛhaṃ*)) by many.

### Printed p. 308

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मंद्रं (*maṃdraṃ*)—(O Soma-deva) the delightful
- वरेण्यं (*vareṇyaṃ*)—the most venerable one, you
- आ (*ā*)—we worship
- विप्रं (*vipraṃ*)—the wise
- मनीषिणं (*manīṣiṇaṃ*)—the praise-endowed, you
- आ (*ā*)—we worship
- पांतं (*pāṃtaṃ*)—the protector
- पुरुस्पृहं (*puruspṛhaṃ*)—the desired of many, you
- आ (*ā*)—we worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you, the delightful and most venerable, we worship. You, the wise and endowed with praise, we worship. You, the protector, desired by many, we worship.

##### English translation
The exhilarating, the desirable, the wise, the intelligent, the defender (of all), the desired of many.

#### Ṛk 30

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ र॒यिमा सु॑चे॒तुन॒मा सु॑क्रतो त॒नूष्वा ।  
> पांत॒मा पु॑रु॒स्पृह॑म् ॥ ३० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । रयिम् । आ । सुऽचेतुनम् । आ । सुक्रतो इति सुऽक्रतो । तनूषु । आ ।  
> पांतम् । आ । पुरुऽस्पृहम् ॥ ३० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सुक्रतो शोभनप्रज्ञ सोम त्वदीयं रयिं धनं वयम् आ वृणीमहे । किंच सुचेतुनम् । ‘ चिती संज्ञाने'। भाव औणादिक उनन्प्रत्ययः । सुज्ञानं च। तनूषु अस्मत्पुत्रेषु च धनं सुज्ञानं च त्वम् आ विधेहि । यद्वा पुत्रार्थं वयमावृणीमहे । तथा पांतं सर्वस्य रक्षकं पुरुस्पृहं बहुभिर्यष्टृभिः काम्यमानं त्वां संभजामहे ॥ ॥ ६ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma of good insight (सुक्रतो (*sukrato*)), we choose your wealth (रयिं (*rayiṃ*)). Further, सुचेतुनम् (*sucetunam*) is good knowledge. In our sons (तनूषु (*tanūṣu*)) too, do you bestow wealth and good knowledge. Or else: we choose it for the sake of sons. Likewise we partake of you, the protector (पांतं (*pāṃtaṃ*)) of all and desired (पुरुस्पृहं (*puruspṛhaṃ*)) by many sacrificers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुक्रतो (*sukrato*)—O Soma-deva, of excellent insight
- सुचेतुनं (*sucetunaṃ*)—excellent, bestowing strength
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—your wealth
- आ (वृणीमहे) (*ā (vṛṇīmahe)*)—we worship and desire
- तनूषु (*tanūṣu*)—in our sons and the like
- आ (विधेहि) (*ā (vidhehi)*)—provide that wealth
- पांतं (*pāṃtaṃ*)—the protector of all
- पुरुस्पृहं (*puruspṛhaṃ*)—the one desired by many, you
- आ (*ā*)—we worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, of excellent insight, your wealth, which is excellent and bestows strength, we worship and desire. Fill our sons and the like with that wealth. You, the protector of all and desired by many, we worship.

##### English translation
(We have recourse) to your wealth and intelligence for our prosterity**NOTE** O you to whom fair sacrifices are offered, and to you the defender (of all), the desired of many.

## Sūkta 66 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘पवस्व' इति त्रिंशदृचं षष्ठं सूक्तम् । अत्रानुक्रम्यते- पवस्व शतं वैखानसा अष्टादश्यनुष्टुप्परास्तिस्र आग्नेय्यः' इति । शतसंख्याका वैखानसाख्याः संहता ऋषयः । ‘ त्वं सोम सूरः ' इत्येषानुष्टुप् । शिष्टा गायत्र्यः । ‘ अग्न आयूंषि' इत्याद्यास्तिस्रः पवमानविशिष्टाग्निदेवताकाः । अन्यासां पवमानः सोमो देवता । गतः सूक्तविनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sixth sūkta, पवस्व (*pavasva*), has thirty Ṛks. The Anukramaṇī says of it: अत्रानुक्रम्यते- पवस्व शतं वैखानसा अष्टादश्यनुष्टुप्परास्तिस्र आग्नेय्यः' (*atrānukramyate- pavasva śataṃ vaikhānasā aṣṭādaśyanuṣṭupparāstisra āgneyyaḥ '*). The seers are a hundred together, the Vaikhānasas. The eighteenth Ṛk, त्वं सोम सूरः (*tvaṃ soma sūraḥ*), is in the Anuṣṭubh metre; the rest are Gāyatrī. The three beginning अग्न आयूंषि (*agna āyūṃṣi*) have as deity Agni qualified as Pavamāna; for the others the deity is Pavamāna Soma. The application of the sūkta has been given.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, पवस्व (*pavasva*), is the sixth sūkta in the third anuvāka. It has thirty Ṛks. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: पवस्व शतं वैखानसा अष्टादश्यनुष्टुप्परा स्तिस्र आग्नेय्यः (*pavasva śataṃ vaikhānasā aṣṭādaśyanuṣṭupparā stisra āgneyyaḥ*). The seers of this sūkta are, collectively, the hundred seers called Vaikhānasas. The eighteenth Ṛk of this sūkta, त्वं सोम सूरः (*tvaṃ soma sūraḥ*), is in the Anuṣṭubh metre; the remaining Ṛks are in the Gāyatrī metre. The three Ṛks beginning अग्न आयूंषि (*agna āyūṃṣi*) (Ṛks 19–21) have as deity Agni qualified as Pavamāna. For the other Ṛks the deity is Pavamāna Soma. The application of the sūkta has been stated before.

##### Particulars

Sūkta 66. Maṇḍala 9. Anuvāka 3. Sūkta 66. Aṣṭaka 7. Adhyāya 2. Vargas 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 30. Seer: Śataṃ Vaikhānasāḥ. Deity: 1–18, 22–30 Pavamāna Soma; 19–21 Agni. Metre: 1–17, 19–30 Gāyatrī; 18 Anuṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पव॑स्व विश्वचर्षणे॒ऽभि विश्वा॑नि॒ काव्या॑ ।  
> सखा॒ सखि॑भ्य॒ ईड्यः॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पवस्व । विश्वऽचर्षणे । अभि । विश्वानि । काव्या ।  
> सखा । सखिऽभ्यः । ईड्यः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे विश्वचर्षणे सर्वव्यापित्वेन सर्वस्य द्रष्टर्हे सोम सखा स्तुत्यस्तोतृयष्टृयष्टव्यलक्षणेन संबंधेन सखिभूतस्त्वम् ईड्यः स्तोतव्यः सन् सखिभ्यः हविष्प्रदानेनोपकारकत्वात् मित्रभूतेभ्योऽस्मभ्यं विश्वानि सर्वाणि काव्या । कवेः कर्माणि काव्यानि । ब्राह्मणादित्वात् ष्यञ्। सर्वाणि स्तोत्राणि अभि लक्षीकृत्य पवस्व आगच्छ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, all-seeing (विश्वचर्षणे (*viśvacarṣaṇe*)), that is, seeing everything through your all-pervasiveness, you are a friend (सखा (*sakhā*)) by the relation of the praised, the praiser, the sacrificer and the one sacrificed to. Being worthy of praise (ईड्यः (*īḍyaḥ*)), flow (पवस्व (*pavasva*)), come, toward all (विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)) the hymns (काव्या (*kāvyā*): works of the poet), to us, your friends (सखिभ्यः (*sakhibhyaḥ*)), who are like friends because we help you by the offering of oblations.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्वचर्षणे (*viśvacarṣaṇe*)—O Soma, able to see everything
- सखा (*sakhā*)—you, who are a friend to us
- ईड्यः (*īḍyaḥ*)—being worthy of praise
- सखिभ्यः (*sakhibhyaḥ*)—of us, your friends
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all
- काव्या अभि (*kāvyā abhi*)—with regard to the acts of praise
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow hither

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, able to see everything, you who are a friend to us, being worthy of our praise, flow hither with regard to all the acts of praise of us, your friends.

### Printed p. 311

##### English translation
All-seeing (Soma), who are the adorable friend (of the worshippers), flow for (us your) friends towards all (our) hymns of praise.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ताभ्यां॒ विश्व॑स्य राजसि॒ ये प॑वमान॒ धाम॑नी ।  
> प्र॒ती॒ची सो॑म त॒स्थतुः॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ताभ्याम् । विश्वस्य । राजसि । ये इति । पवमान । धामनी इति ।  
> प्रतीची इति । सोम । तस्थतुः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पवमान दशापवित्रेण पूयमान पुनान वा हे सोम ये धामनी पूर्वपक्षापरपक्षयोर्लतारूपस्य सोमस्य तवैकैकपर्णवृद्धिहासाभ्यां तव स्वभूतौ पूर्वादिपक्षौ । यद्वा ये धामनी नामनी अंशुसोमात्मके अपि प्रतीची त्वदभिमुखं गच्छंतौ गच्छती वा पक्षौ नामनी वा तस्थतुः उपजग्मतुः ताभ्यां त्वं विश्वस्य सर्वस्य लोकस्य राजसि स्वामी भवसि । पूर्वादिपक्षाभ्यां सर्वलोकस्योपनायकत्वात्तस्य स्वामी भवसि । पृथिव्यामंशुनाम्ना मनुष्याणां सर्वेषामभीप्सितदानेन तस्य लोकस्य द्युलोके देवेभ्यः स्वसुधामयकलादानेन तेषां प्रीणयिता भवसि । देवाः खलु सोमस्यैकैकवृद्धिहासाभ्यां कलाः पिबंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Pavamāna, purified by the ten-fold filter, O Soma: the two abodes (धामनी (*dhāmanī*)) are the two fortnights, the earlier and the later, which are your own through the increase and decrease, leaf by leaf, of you who are of the form of the creeper Soma. Or else the two abodes are two names, those of the plant Soma and of the pressed Soma, which stand facing you, or the two fortnights or names that have come to you. By these two you are lord (राजसि (*rājasi*)) of the whole world: through the fortnights you lead the whole world, and on earth, under the name of the plant, by granting the desires of all men, and in heaven, by giving the gods the digits made of his nectar, you become the one who pleases them. For the gods indeed drink the digits of Soma through his increase and decrease, one by one.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पवमान (*pavamāna*)—O purifying one
- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- ये (*ye*)—which
- धामनी (*dhāmanī*)—the two faces (powers) called the earlier and the later fortnight
- प्रतीची (*pratīcī*)—toward you
- तस्थतुः (*tasthatuḥ*)—stand established (or move)
- ताभ्यां (*tābhyāṃ*)—with those
- विश्वस्य (*viśvasya*)—of the whole world
- राजसि (*rājasi*)—you are lord

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, purifier, with those two faces, called the earlier and the later fortnight, which stand established and move facing you, you are lord of the whole world.

### Printed p. 312

##### English translation
You, purified Soma, rule the universe by those two halves (of the lunar month) which stand facing you.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> परि॒ धामा॑नि॒ यानि॑ ते॒ त्वं सो॑मासि वि॒श्वतः॑ ।  
> पव॑मान ऋ॒तुभिः॑ कवे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परि । धामानि । यानि । ते । त्वम् । सोम । असि । विश्वतः ।  
> पवमान । ऋतुऽभिः । कवे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम यस्मात् ते त्वदीयानि धामानि त्वदधीना अहोरात्ररूपाः कालविशेषाः परि भवंति सर्वत्र व्याप्तास्तिष्ठंति । यद्वा त्वदीयानि धामानि तेजांसि परि वर्तंते अत एव हे पवमान पूयमान हे कवे क्रांतकर्मन हे सोम त्वम् ऋतुभिः वसंतादिकालविशेषैः सह विश्वतः सर्वतः असि भवसि । अहोरात्रौ यत्र यत्र व्याप्तौ तत्र तत्र वसंतादिकालोपाधिकः सोमस्तिष्ठति । तयोस्तधीनत्वादित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, since your abodes (धामानि (*dhāmāni*)), the particular times in the form of day and night, which depend on you, extend (परि (*pari*)) everywhere, or since your splendours go round, therefore, O Pavamāna, being purified, O sage (कवे (*kave*): of far-reaching action), you are (असि (*asi*)) everywhere (विश्वतः (*viśvataḥ*)) together with the seasons (ऋतुभिः (*ṛtubhiḥ*)), the particular times such as spring. Wherever day and night extend, there Soma, conditioned by seasons such as spring, abides, since these depend on him. This is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पवमान (*pavamāna*)—O purifier
- कवे (*kave*)—one of far-reaching action
- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- ते (*te*)—your
- यानि धामानि (*yāni dhāmāni*)—which (powers), particular times in the form of day and night
- परि (*pari*)—extend everywhere; such
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- ऋतुभिः (*ṛtubhiḥ*)—with the divisions of the seasons such as spring
- विश्वतः (*viśvataḥ*)—everywhere
- असि (*asi*)—you pervade

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, purifier and one of far-reaching action, because those particular times of yours in the form of day and night extend everywhere, therefore you pervade everywhere together with the divisions of the seasons such as spring.

##### English translation
Since your splendours abound, you purified sage, Soma, are everywhere (associated) with the seasons.

### Printed p. 313

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पव॑स्व ज॒नय॒न्निषो॒ऽभि विश्वा॑नि॒ वार्या॑ ।  
> सखा॒ सखि॑भ्य ऊ॒तये॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पवस्व । जनयन् । इषः । अभि । विश्वानि । वार्या ।  
> सखा । सखिऽभ्यः । ऊतये ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम सखा सखिभूतस्त्वं विश्वानि सर्वाणि वार्या वरणीयान्यस्मत्कृतानि स्तोत्राणि अभि लक्षीकृत्य सखिभ्यः अस्मभ्यम् ऊतये रक्षणाय जीवनाय इषः अन्नानि जनयन् प्रयच्छन् पवस्व आगच्छ । पवतिर्गतिकर्मा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, being a friend, toward all (विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)) the desirable (वार्या (*vāryā*)) hymns made by us, to us your friends (सखिभ्यः (*sakhibhyaḥ*)), for protection (ऊतये (*ūtaye*)), for life, generating (जनयन् (*janayan*)), that is, giving, foods (इषः (*iṣaḥ*)), flow (पवस्व (*pavasva*)), come. The root पव (*pava*) means going.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सखा (*sakhā*)—you, who are a friend (O Soma-deva)
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all
- वार्या अभि (*vāryā abhi*)—toward our hymns that are desired by you
- सखिभ्यः (*sakhibhyaḥ*)—of us, your friends
- ऊतये (*ūtaye*)—for protection
- इषः (*iṣaḥ*)—foods
- जनयन् (*janayan*)—producing
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—come flowing

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you who are a friend, facing all our hymns that are desired by you, for the protection of us, your friends, come flowing, producing foods.

##### English translation
Soma, who are a friend, do you for the sake of all our desirable (praises) approach generating food for (us your) friends for our support

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तव॑ शु॒क्रासो॑ अ॒र्चयो॑ दि॒वस्पृ॒ष्ठे वि त॑न्वते ।  
> प॒वित्रं॑ सोम॒ धाम॑भिः ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 314

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तव । शुक्रासः । अर्चयः । दिवः । पृष्ठे । वि । तन्वते ।  
> पवित्रम् । सोम । धामऽभिः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम शुक्रासः सर्वत्र ज्वलनशीलाः धामभिः तेजोभिः सहितस्य तव स्वभूताः अर्चयः अर्चनीया रश्मयः दिवः द्योतमानस्यादित्यस्य द्युलोकस्य वा पृष्ठे अधरभागे। पृथिव्यामित्यर्थः। पवित्रं पवनसाधनमुदकं वि तन्वते विशेषेण तन्वंति विस्तारयंति । सर्वत्र कुर्वंतीत्यर्थः ॥ ॥ ७ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, the bright (शुक्रासः (*śukrāsaḥ*)), that is, everywhere blazing, rays (अर्चयः (*arcayaḥ*)), to be worshipped, which are your own, accompanied by splendours (धामभिः (*dhāmabhiḥ*)), spread out (वि तन्वते (*vi tanvate*)), extend widely the filter (पवित्रं (*pavitraṃ*)), the water that is the means of purifying, on the back (पृष्ठे (*pṛṣṭhe*)) of heaven (दिवः (*divaḥ*)), that is, of the shining sun or of the heavenly world, in its lower part, that is, on the earth. The meaning is that they do so everywhere.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- धामभिः (*dhāmabhiḥ*)—accompanied by splendours
- तव (*tava*)—your
- शुक्रासः (*śukrāsaḥ*)—shining
- अर्चयः (*arcayaḥ*)—rays
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the atmosphere
- पृष्ठे (*pṛṣṭhe*)—on the earth, the lower region
- पवित्रः (*pavitraḥ*)—the water, the means of purification
- वि तन्नते (*vi tannate*)**NOTE**—cause to spread

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, your shining rays, accompanied by splendours, spread out the water, the means of purification, on the earth, which lies below the atmosphere.

##### English translation
Soma, the shinning rays of you who are accompanied by brilliance, spread the purifying (water) over the surface of heaven.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तवे॒मे स॒प्त सिंध॑वः प्र॒शिषं॑ सोम सिस्रते ।  
> तुभ्यं॑ धावंति धे॒नवः॑ ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तव । इमे । सप्त । सिंधवः । प्रऽशिषम् । सोम । सिस्रते ।  
> तुभ्यम् । धावंति । धेनवः ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 315

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सृष्टिकर्तृत्वप्रसंगादाह । हे सोम इमे इमाः त्वया सृष्टाः सप्त सप्तसंख्याकाः सिंधवः स्यंदमाना गंगाद्या नद्यः । यद्वा सप्त सर्पणशीला नद्यः तव प्रशिषं प्रशासनमाज्ञामभि सिस्रते अनुसरंति । त्वदाज्ञामनुसृत्य समुद्रं गच्छंतीत्यर्थः । किंच धेनवः नवप्रसूतिका देवानां हविष्प्रदानेन प्रीणयित्र्यो गावः तुभ्यं त्वदर्थमेवाशिरं प्रयच्छाम इति धावंति आगच्छंति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Because the creation of things has come up, Sāyaṇa says: O Soma, these seven rivers, Gaṅgā and the others, created by you and flowing, follow your command (or else: the seven gliding rivers go after your order). Obeying your command they go to the ocean. Further, the milch cows, newly calved, who please the gods by the gift of oblations, run to you, thinking: we shall give you the milk-mixture for your sake.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- इमे (*ime*)—created by you
- सप्त (*sapta*)—seven in number
- सिंधवः (*siṃdhavaḥ*)—the rivers, Gaṅgā and others
- तव (*tava*)—your
- प्रशिषं (*praśiṣaṃ*)—obedient to command
- सिस्रते (*sisrate*)—flow
- धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*)—the milk-giving cows
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—to you, to provide the milk-mixture
- धावंति (*dhāvaṃti*)—come quickly

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, these Gaṅgā and other rivers, seven in number, created by you, flow obedient to your command. The milk-giving cows come quickly to provide you the milk-mixture.

##### English translation
These your seven rivers flow, Soma, at your command : the milch cows hasten to you.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र सो॑म याहि॒ धार॑या सु॒त इंद्रा॑य मत्स॒रः ।  
> दधा॑नो॒ अक्षि॑ति॒ श्रवः॑ ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । सोम । याहि । धारया । सुतः । इंद्राय । मत्सरः ।  
> दधानः । अक्षिति । श्रवः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम अभिषूयमाण देव मत्सरः इंद्रस्य मदकरस्वं सुतः अस्माभिरभिषुतः सन् इंद्राय इंद्रार्थं दशापवित्रान्निर्गतया संततया त्वदीयया धारया द्रोणकलशं प्र याहि प्रकर्षेण प्राप्नुहि । यद्वा । हे सोम सुतोऽभिषुतस्त्वमिंद्राय मत्सरो मादयितृतमः सन् धारयाग्नौ स्वाहाकारेण पात्रात् पतंत्या धारया सह त्वमिंद्रमुपयाहि । कीदृशः । अक्षिति अक्षीणं श्रवः। श्रव इत्यन्ननाम । दधानः अस्मभ्यं प्रयच्छन् प्र याहीति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, god who is pressed, exhilarating (delighter) of Indra, being pressed by us, go forth for Indra with your stream, which flows continuously from the ten-fold filter, to the Droṇa-vessel; reach it forcefully. Or else: O pressed Soma, most intoxicating for Indra, go to Indra together with the stream that falls from the vessel into the fire with the call svāhā. How are you? Bestowing on us inexhaustible food, for śravas is a name for food.

### Printed p. 316

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- मत्सरः (*matsaraḥ*)—you who give delight to Indra
- सुतः (*sutaḥ*)—pressed
- अक्षिति (*akṣiti*)—imperishable
- श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)—food
- दधानः (*dadhānaḥ*)—giving to us
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for the sake of Indra
- धारया (*dhārayā*)—in the form of a stream
- प्रे याहि (*pre yāhi*)**NOTE**—flow towards the Droṇa-vessel

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you who give delight to Indra, as soon as you are pressed, giving us imperishable food, flow in the form of a stream, for the sake of Indra, towards the Droṇa-vessel.

##### English translation
Proceed, Soma, in a stream when effused, giving exhilaration to Indra, bestowing (upon us) inexhaustible food.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> समु॑ त्वा धी॒भिर॑स्वरन्हिन्व॒तीः स॒प्त जा॒मयः॑ ।  
> विप्र॑मा॒जा वि॒वस्व॑तः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सम् । ऊं इति । त्वा । धीभिः । अस्वरन् । हिन्वतीः । सप्त । जामयः ।  
> विप्रम् । आजा । विवस्वतः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम हिन्वतीः । लिंगव्यत्ययः । हिन्वंतः स्तुतीः प्रेरयंतः सप्त सप्तसंख्याकाः जामयः एकस्मिन् यज्ञे कर्मकरणेन परस्परं बंधुभूता होतृप्रभृतयः सप्त होत्रकाः विवस्वतः देवानां हविष्प्रदानेन परिचरणवतो यजमानस्य आजा आजौ । अजंति गच्छंति ऋत्विजोऽत्रेत्याजिर्यज्ञः । तस्मिन् विप्रं मेधाविनं पवमानं त्वा त्वामेव धीभिः धीतिभिः स्तुतिभिः सम् अस्वरन् अशब्दयन् अस्तुवन् । यद्वा । हिन्वतीर्गच्छंत्यः सप्त जामयो गंगाद्याः सप्त नद्यो धीभिः । वर्णलोपश्छांदसः । धीतिभिः अंगुलीभिर्विप्रं त्वां समस्वरन् प्रेरयंति । वसतीवरीभिरेकधनाभिश्च परिशोधनार्थं प्रेरयंतीति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, the seven kinsmen (jāmi), the Hotṛ and the other priests, who are related to one another by performing the rites in one sacrifice, urging on (the verb hinvatīḥ, with a change of gender) their praises, the seven officiants of the sacrifice of the worshipper, who serves the gods with the gift of oblations, praised you, the wise one who purifies himself, in the sacrifice (āji, the place where the priests go), with their hymns. Or else: the seven flowing sisters, the seven rivers Gaṅgā and the others, with the fingers (dhītibhiḥ, a letter being dropped in the Vedic idiom) urge you, the wise one, on; they urge you for purification, with the vasatīvarī and the ekadhanā waters.

### Printed p. 317

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- हिन्वतीः (*hinvatīḥ*)—those who offer praises
- सप्त (*sapta*)—seven in number
- जामयः (*jāmayaḥ*)—the Hotṛs, who are kinsmen in one sacrifice and engaged in the rite
- विवस्वतः (*vivasvataḥ*)—of the sacrificer
- आजा (*ājā*)—in the sacrifice
- विप्रं (*vipraṃ*)—wise
- त्वा उ (*tvā u*)—you indeed
- धीभिः (*dhībhiḥ*)—with praises
- समस्वरन् (*samasvaran*)—praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, these seven Hotṛs, who offer praises and who help one another in the same sacrifice, praise you, the wise one, with praises in the sacrifice of the sacrificer.

##### English translation
The seven kindred (priests) uttering (praises) and worshipping (the gods with oblations) invoked you the sage at the sacrifice with hymns.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मृ॒जंति॑ त्वा॒ सम॒ग्रुवोऽव्ये॑ जी॒रावधि॒ ष्वणि॑ ।  
> रे॒भो यद॒ज्यसे॒ वने॑ ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मृजंति । त्वा । सम् । अग्रुवः । अव्ये । जीरौ । अधि । स्वनि ।  
> रेभः । यत् । अज्यसे । वने ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम अग्रुवः । अंगुलिनामैतत् । अजंति प्रक्षिपंति हवींष्यग्नाविति । यद्वा अगेर्गत्यर्थस्य । कर्मकरणार्थमितस्ततो गच्छंतीति । अग्रुवोऽंगुलयोऽस्मदीयाः जीरौ पापानामभिभावुके क्षिप्रं कृते वा स्वनि अधि अधिकं शब्दायमाने अव्ये अविवालेन कृते पवित्रे त्वा त्वां तदा सं मृजंति सम्यक् शोधयंति । यत् यदा रेभः । ‘ रेभृ शब्दे । उदकमध्ये प्रक्षेपेण शब्दायमानस्त्वं वने वननीये वसतीवर्याख्य उदके अज्यसे अक्तः सिक्तो भवसि । तदा मृजंतीत्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, agruvaḥ is a name of the fingers: they throw the oblations into the fire; or else, from the root of motion, they go hither and thither for the performance of the rite. Our fingers then cleanse you thoroughly in the pavitra (filter) made of sheep's wool, which quickly overcomes sins (jīra), makes a loud sound, when you, making a noise, are put into the water, and are sprinkled in the water called vasatīvarī, the vananīya water. This is the construction: they cleanse you then. The word rebha is derived from the root meaning to sound: it means you who make a noise when thrown into the water.

### Printed p. 318

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)(O Soma-deva)—when
- रेभः (*rebhaḥ*)—you who sound in the midst of the water
- वने (*vane*)—in the venerable water
- अज्यसे (*ajyase*)—you are mixed, then
- अग्रुवः (*agruvaḥ*)—the fingers
- जीरौ (*jīrau*)—quickly
- स्वनि अधि (*svani adhi*)—loud-sounding, to a great degree
- अव्ये (*avye*)—in the ten-fold filter
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- सं मृजंति (*saṃ mṛjaṃti*)—purify

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, when you, who make a noise in the midst of the water, are mixed in the venerable water, then the ten fingers purify you in the ten-fold filter, which is quickly made and makes a loud sound.

##### English translation
The fingers cleanse you in the quickly-made loud-sounding (woollen) filter, when with a noise you are sprinkled with the water.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पव॑मानस्य ते कवे॒ वाजि॒न् त्सर्गा॑ असृक्षत ।  
> अर्वं॑तो॒ न श्र॑व॒स्यवः॑ ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पवमानस्य । ते । कवे । वाजिन् । सर्गाः । असृक्षत ।  
> अर्वंतः । न । श्रवस्यवः ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मार्जनप्रसंगमाह । हे कवे क्रांतप्रज्ञ हे वाजिन् अन्नवन् सोम पवमानस्य दशापवित्रेण पूयमानस्य ते तव सर्गाः । सृज्यंत इति सर्गा धाराः । कीदृशाः । श्रवस्यवः । छंदसि परेच्छायां क्यच् । यष्टॄणामन्नं कामयमानास्त्वदीया धाराः असृक्षत सृजंति । निर्गच्छंतीत्यर्थः । तत्र दृष्टांतः । अर्वंतो न । यथाश्वा मंदुरातो निर्गच्छंति तद्वत् पवित्रान्निःसरंतीत्यर्थः । प्रयोगापेक्षं चात्र धाराबाहुल्यम् ॥ ॥ ८ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues on the subject of purification. O sage (kavi, of far-reaching wisdom), O possessor of food, O Soma, who are being purified by the ten-fold filter, your streams (sargāḥ, that are poured forth) desiring food (śravasyavaḥ, desiring the food of the worshippers, with the suffix kyac in the Veda in the sense of desire for another) are let loose, that is, they flow out. An example: just as horses go out from the stable, so they come forth from the filter. The abundance of streams is relative to the use in the rite.

### Printed p. 319

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कवे (*kave*)—you of far-reaching wisdom
- वाजिन् (*vājin*)—you who possess food, O Soma-deva
- पवमानस्य (*pavamānasya*)—purified in the ten-fold filter
- ते (*te*)—your
- श्रवस्यवः (*śravasyavaḥ*)—desiring oblation
- सर्गाः (*sargāḥ*)—streams
- अर्वंतो न (*arvaṃto na*)—like swiftly running horses
- असृक्षत (*asṛkṣata*)—flow quickly

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you of far-reaching wisdom and possessor of food, your streams, which desire the oblation and are purified in the ten-fold filter, flow quickly like swiftly running horses.

##### English translation
Sage Soma, possessor of food, your food-desiring streams when you are filtered are let loose like horses.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अच्छा॒ कोशं॑ मधु॒श्चुत॒मसृ॑ग्रं॒ वारे॑ अ॒व्यये॑ ।  
> अवा॑वशंत धी॒तयः॑ ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अच्छ । कोशम् । मधुऽश्चुतम् । असृग्रम् । वारे । अव्यये ।  
> अवावशंत । धीतयः ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> धारानिर्गमनप्रसंगादभिधीयते । मधुश्चुतं मधुररसस्य च्यावयितारं क्षारयितारं कोशं द्रोणकलशम् अच्छ अभिलक्ष्य अव्यये अविमये अविस्वभूते वा वारे वाले दशापवित्रे असृग्रं सोमा ऋत्विग्भिः सृज्यंते । सृजेः कर्मणि तिङां तिङो भवंति' इति झो रमादेशः। किंच धीतयः । अंगुलिनामैतत् । धयंति पिबंत्याभिरिति । अस्मदीया अंगुलयः अवावशंत तान् सोमान् पुनःपुनर्मार्जनार्थं कामयंते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Because the flowing out of the streams has been mentioned, this is said. The Somas are poured by the priests towards the Droṇa-vessel, which makes the sweet juice flow (madhuścut), upon the vāra (hair), the ten-fold filter, made of wool, avyaya (not of sheep's own, or else not belonging to oneself). Further, dhītayaḥ is a name of the fingers, by which one drinks. Our fingers desire those Somas again and again for purification.

### Printed p. 320

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मधुश्चुतं (*madhuścutaṃ*)—that which makes the sweet juice flow
- कोशं अच्छ (*kośaṃ accha*)—towards the ten-fold filter
- अव्यये (*avyaye*)—made of wool
- वारे (*vāre*)—on the fibres
- असृग्रं (*asṛgraṃ*)—the Soma juices are poured out
- धीतयः (*dhītayaḥ*)—the fingers
- अवावशंत (*avāvaśaṃta*)—are eager to purify them

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Towards the ten-fold filter that makes the sweet juice flow, upon the fibres made of wool, the Soma juices are poured out. The fingers are eager to purify them.

##### English translation
They are let loose in the woollen filter (to go) towards the honey-dropping vessel; our fingers have desired them.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अच्छा॑ समु॒द्रमिंद॒वोऽस्तं॒ गावो॒ न धे॒नवः॑ ।  
> अग्म॑न्नृ॒तस्य॒ योनि॒मा ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अच्छ । समुद्रम् । इंदवः । अस्तम् । गावः । न । धेनवः ।  
> अग्मन् । ऋतस्य । योनिम् । आ ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंदवः क्षरंतः सोमाः समुद्रं सोमानामेकत्रैव संगमनस्थानं द्रोणकलशम् अच्छ अभि गच्छंति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । धेनवः पयःप्रदानेन जनानां प्रीणयित्र्यो नवप्रसूतिकाः गावः अस्तं गृहं यथाभिगच्छंति तद्वत् । किंच ते सोमाः ऋतस्य सत्यभूतस्य यज्ञस्य योनिं स्थानम् आ अग्मन् आभिमुख्येन गच्छंति । गमेर्लुङि सिचो लुक्युपधालोपः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The flowing Somas (indavaḥ) go towards the ocean, the one place where the Somas meet together, the Droṇa-vessel. An example: just as the milch cows (dhenavaḥ, who please people by giving milk, newly calved) go towards their home (astam). Further, those Somas come towards the place (yoni) of the sacrifice (ṛta, which is truthful).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*)—the milk-giving
- गावः (*gāvaḥ*)—cows
- अस्तं न (*astaṃ na*)—as they go towards home
- इंदवः (*iṃdavaḥ*)—the flowing Somas
- समुद्रं अच्छ (*samudraṃ accha*)—where all the juices gather together**NOTE**

### Printed p. 321

go and join, facing the Droṇa-vessel. (And)

- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of the sacrifice
- योनिं (*yoniṃ*)—to the place
- आ अग्मन् (*ā agman*)—go and join

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As milk-giving cows go eagerly towards their home, so the flowing Somas go and join, facing the Droṇa-vessel where all the juices gather together. And from there they go and join the place of the sacrifice.

##### English translation
The Soma-juices go to the ocean, as milch cows to their stall ; they go to the place of sacrifice.

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र ण॑ इंदो म॒हे रण॒ आपो॑ अर्षंति॒ सिंध॑वः ।  
> यद्गोभि॑र्वासयि॒ष्यसे॑ ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । नः । इंदो इति । महे । रणे । आपः । अर्षंति । सिंधवः ।  
> यत् । गोभिः । वासयिष्यसे ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंदो क्षरन् सोम नः अस्माकं स्वभूताय रणे रणाय । रणंति स्तुवंति देवानत्रेति रणो यज्ञः । अधिकरणे अप् । ङेर्यः' (पा. सू. ७.१.१३) इति न भवति सर्वविधीनां छंदसि विकल्पितत्वात् । महे महते रणाय यज्ञाय तदर्थं सिंधवः स्यंदमानाः आपः वसतीवर्याख्याः सोमसेकार्थं तदा अर्षंति प्रगच्छंति । यत् यदा त्वं गोभिः गव्यैर्दधिक्षीरादिभिः वासयिष्यसे आच्छाद्यसे मिश्रितो भवसि तदापो गच्छंतीति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indu, O flowing Soma, for our great rite (raṇa, the sacrifice, where they praise the gods) the flowing waters, called vasatīvarī, go forth then for the sprinkling of Soma; that is, when you are covered and mixed with the products of cows, curds, milk and the like, then the waters go.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma-deva
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)—with the milk-mixtures, milk and the rest
- वासयिष्यसे (*vāsayiṣyase*)—you join (then)
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- महे (*mahe*)—great

### Printed p. 322

- रणे (*raṇe*)—for the sacrifice
- सिंधवः (*siṃdhavaḥ*)—in the form of streams
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the waters, the vasatīvarī and others
- प्र अर्षंति (*pra arṣaṃti*)—flow forth and come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, when you join the milk and other mixtures, then for our great sacrifice the waters, the vasatīvarī and others, in the form of streams, flow forth and come.

##### English translation
Indu, the flowing waters hasten to our great sacrifices when you are mixed with the curds and milk.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंदो पवमान इयक्षंतः यष्टुमिच्छंतः पूजयितुमिच्छंतो वा अस्य प्रसिद्धस्य ते तव सख्ये सखिकर्मणि स्थिताः वयं त्वोतयः त्वदायत्तरक्षणाः संतः सखित्वं सखिभावमेव उश्मसि उश्मः कामयामहे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indu, O purifying Soma, we, desiring to sacrifice or to worship, standing in the friendship of you, the well known, dependent on you for our protection, desire (uśmasi, we long for) only friendship with you.

- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- त्वोतॆयः (*tvotèyaḥ*)**NOTE**—wishing for your protection
- सखित्वं (*sakhitvaṃ*)—your friendship
- उश्मसि (*uśmasi*)—we desire

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, we who wish to perform the sacrifice and who have your well-known friendship, wishing for your protection, desire your friendship.

Indu, we abiding in your friendship, desiring to sacrifice, depending on your protection, desire your friendship.

#### Ṛk 15

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ प॑वस्व॒ गवि॑ष्टये म॒हे सो॑म नृ॒चक्ष॑से ।  
> एंद्र॑स्य ज॒ठरे॑ विश ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । पवस्व । गोऽइष्टये । महे । सोम । नृऽचक्षसे ।  
> आ । इंद्रस्य । जठरे । विश ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम पवमान गविष्टये अंगिरसां गवामन्वेष्ट्रे महे महते नृचक्षसे नॄणां मनुष्याणां द्रष्रेमा कर्मनेतॄणां फलं पश्यते वा इंद्राय आ पवस्व पात्रेषु दशापवित्रेण पूतो भव । ततः इंद्रस्य जठरे उदर उदरभूते द्रोणकलशे वा आ विश प्रविश ॥ ॥ ९ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, O purifying one, flow into the vessels, purified by the ten-fold filter, for Indra, the finder of the cows of the Aṅgirases, the great, the beholder of men (nṛcakṣas: the seer of men, or he who sees the fruit of the leaders of rites**NOTE**). Then enter Indra's belly, that is, the Droṇa-vessel which is like a belly.

- महे (*mahe*)—for him of great nature
- नृचक्षसे (*nṛcakṣase*)—for him who looks at the deeds of men, you for the sake of Indra

- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—of Indra
- जठरे (*jaṭhare*)—in the belly
- आ विश (*ā viśa*)—enter

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you who find the cows, who are of great nature, who look at the deeds of men, flow for the sake of Indra. Enter also Indra's belly.

##### English translation
Flow, Soma, for the mighty cattle-seeker, the beholder of men, enter Indra's belly.

#### Ṛk 16

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> म॒हाँ अ॑सि सोम॒ ज्येष्ठ॑ उ॒ग्राणा॑मिंद॒ ओजि॑ष्ठः ।  
> युध्वा॒ संछश्व॑ज्जिगेथ ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> महान् । असि । सोम । ज्येष्ठः । उग्राणाम् । इंदो इति । ओजिष्ठः ।  
> युध्वा । सन् । शश्वत् । जिगेथ ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम त्वं महान् असि यतस्त्वं देवानां प्रीणयितासि खलु। त्वं ज्येष्ठः प्रशस्यतमो भवसि । किंच हे इंदो पवमान त्वम् उग्राणाम् उद्गूर्णबलानामपि ओजिष्ठः ओजस्वितमो भवसि । त्वं युध्वा सन् शत्रुभिः सह युद्धं कुर्वन्नेव शश्वत् सर्वदा जिगेथ तांस्तेषां धनानि च जितवानसि ।' जि जये'। थलि ‘ सन्लिटोर्जेः' इत्यभ्यासादुत्तरस्य कवर्गादेशः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, you are great, for you are the pleaser of the gods; you are eldest, the most praiseworthy. Further, O Indu, O purifying one, you are the most vigorous even among the mighty, those of uplifted strength. Being a fighter, making war with enemies, you ever conquer them and have conquered their riches.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- महान् असि (*mahān asi*)—you are of great nature
- ज्येष्ठः (*jyeṣṭhaḥ*)—you are above all
- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma, who are in the form of a stream
- उग्राणां (*ugrāṇāṃ*)—among all those of great strength
- ओजिष्ठः (*ojiṣṭhaḥ*)—you of the greatest vigour
- युद्धा सन् (*yuddhā san*)**NOTE**—whenever you are fighting with enemies
- शश्वत् (*śaśvat*)—always
- जिगेथ (*jigetha*)—you gain victory itself

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you are of great nature, you are above all. O Soma, who are in the form of a stream, you of the greatest vigour among all those of great strength, gain victory itself at all times when you fight with enemies.

##### English translation
Soma, you are great, most worthy to be praised ; Indu, (you are) the most vigorous of the mighty ; engaged in battle you ever triumph.

> भूरिऽदाभ्यः । चित् । मंहीयान् ॥ १७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यः सोमः उग्रेभ्यश्चित् उद्गूर्णेभ्यो बलवद्भ्योऽपि ओजीयान् ओजस्वितमः । किंच यः शूरेभ्यश्चित् वीरेभ्योऽपि शूरतरः अत्यंतसमर्थो भवति । तथा यः सोमः भूरिदाभ्यः। ‘डुदाञ् दाने' ।' आतो मनिन् इति विच् । बहुधनानां दातृभ्योऽपि मंहीयान् दातृतमो भवति । तं त्वां वृणीमह इत्युत्तरेण संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Soma who is more vigorous even than the mighty, those of uplifted strength; who is, further, braver and exceedingly capable even than the heroes; and who is more generous even than the givers of much wealth (bhūridā): you we choose, this connects with the following verse.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)(O Soma-deva)—you who
- उग्रेभ्यश्चित् (*ugrebhyaścit*)—among all those of great strength
- ओजीयान् (*ojīyān*)—are exceedingly vigorous
- शूरेभ्यश्चित् (*śūrebhyaścit*)—among all the brave
- शूरतरः (*śūrataraḥ*)—exceedingly brave
- भूरिदाभ्यः चित् (*bhūridābhyaḥ cit*)—among all those who give much
- मंहीयान् (*maṃhīyān*)—are exceedingly generous (such you we worship)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you who among all those of great strength are exceedingly vigorous, among all the brave exceedingly brave, among all who give much exceedingly generous, such you we worship.

##### English translation
(You) who (are) mightier than the mighty, braver, more generous than generous -

#### Ṛk 18

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं सो॑म॒ सूर॒ एष॑स्तो॒कस्य॑ सा॒ता त॒नूना॑म् ।  
> वृ॒णी॒महे॑ स॒ख्याय॑ वृणी॒महे॒ युज्या॑य ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वम् । सोम । सूरः । आ । इषः । तोकस्य । साता । तनूनाम् ।  
> वृणीमहे । सख्याय । वृणीमहे । युज्याय ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम सूरः सुवीर्यः । यद्वा । सर्वस्य यागादिकर्मणि प्रेरकः त्वम् इषः अन्नानि अस्माकम् आ धेहि। उपसर्गश्रुतेर्योग्यक्रियाध्याहारः। किंच त्वं तोकस्य पुत्रस्य तनूनाम् । ‘ तन्वंति विस्तारयंति कुलमिति तन्वः पौत्राः। तेषां च साता दाता भव। ‘षणु दाने'।  जनसन' इति विट्। 'जनसन °' इत्यात्वम् । वयं तं त्वां सख्याय सखिभावाय कर्मणे वा वृणीमहे संभजामहे । तथा युज्याय । युज् सहायः । तस्य भावे कर्मणि वा ष्यञ् । संज्ञापूर्वकस्य विधेत्यरनित्वादवृद्धिः । शत्रुवधादिलक्षणसाहाय्याय च वयं वृणीमहे ॥
> अग्निहोत्रे पूर्वस्यामाहुतौ हुतायामुपस्थितेन यजमानेन प्रतिदिवसं प्रतिसंवत्सरं वानेन तृचेनाग्निरुपस्थेयः । सूत्रितं च--- आग्नेयीभिश्चाग्न आयूंषि पवस इति तिसृभिः संवत्सरे संवत्सरे ( आश्व. श्रौ. २.३-४ ) इति । चौलादिकर्मसु चतस्र आज्याहुतयो होतव्यास्तत्रैव तिस्रः । सूत्रितं च -- तेषां पुरस्ताच्चतस्र आज्याहुतीर्जुहुयादग्न आयूंषि पवस इति तिसृभिः' (आश्व. गृ. १.४.३-४) इति । आधाने पवमानेष्टावग्नेः पवमानस्य ' अग्न आयूंषि' इत्येषानुवाक्या। ‘अग्ने पवस्व' इत्येषा याज्या । सूत्रितं च----’ प्रथमायामग्निरग्निः पवमानोऽग्न आयूंषि पवसेऽग्ने पवस्व स्वपाः' ( आश्व. श्रौ. २.१ ) इति । पुनराधेये द्वितीयाज्यभागस्य ‘अग्न आयूंषि' इत्येषा वैकल्पिकानुवाक्या। सूत्रितं च’ नित्यं पूर्वमनुब्राह्मणिनोऽग्न आयूंषि पवस इत्युत्तरम्' (आश्व. श्रौ. २.८) इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, you who are a hero of good valour (or else: the impeller of all in the rites such as sacrifice), bestow on us foods (iṣaḥ); a verb of fitting meaning is supplied because of the preposition. Further, be the giver to son (toka) and to grandsons (tanūnām: those who extend the family). We choose you for friendship or for the rite of friendship, we resort to you; likewise for alliance (yujya: the state of being a helper, or the rite of helping), that is, for help consisting of the slaying of enemies and the like, we choose you.

Use of the verses: in the Agnihotra, after the first oblation has been offered, the sacrificer who has taken his place near the fire is to approach Agni with this triple verse (tṛca) every day or every year. It is also laid down in the sūtra: with the three Āgneya verses beginning agna āyūṃṣi pavase, year after year (Āśva. Śrau. 2.3-4**NOTE**). In the rites such as the tonsure four oblations of ghee are to be offered, three of them with it. The sūtra says: of these, first one should offer four ghee oblations, with the three verses beginning agna āyūṃṣi pavase (Āśva. Gṛ. 1.4.3-4**NOTE**). In the Ādhāna, in the Pavamāna offering to Agni Pavamāna, agna āyūṃṣi is the anuvākyā and agne pavasva the yājyā; the sūtra: in the first, Agni, Agni Pavamāna, agna āyūṃṣi pavase, agne pavasva svapāḥ (Āśva. Śrau. 2.1). In the Punarādheya, for the second ājyabhāga, agna āyūṃṣi is the optional anuvākyā; the sūtra: the earlier is always so for one who has studied the Brāhmaṇa, agna āyūṃṣi pavase the later (Āśva. Śrau. 2.8).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- सूरः (*sūraḥ*)—you, the impeller of all
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- इषः (*iṣaḥ*)—foods
- आ (देहि) (*ā (dehi)*)—provide to us
- तोकस्य (*tokasya*)—to our sons
- तनूनां (*tanūnāṃ*)**NOTE**—and to grandsons
- साता (*sātā*)—be the giver of food
- सख्याय (*sakhyāya*)—to gain your friendship
- वृणीमहे (*vṛṇīmahe*)**NOTE**—we worship you
- युज्याय (*yujyāya*)—to obtain your help
- वृणीमहे (*vṛṇīmahe*)**NOTE**—we worship you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you, the impeller of all, provide us foods; be the giver of food to our sons and grandsons. To obtain your friendship and your help we worship and choose you.

##### English translation
You, Soma, who are a hero, (bestow) upon (us) food, (be) the giver of sons (to us); we choose you for your friendship. (we choose you) for your alliance.
