#### Ṛk 32

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पा॒व॒मा॒नीर्यो अ॒ध्येत्यृषि॑भिः॒ संभृ॑तं॒ रस॑म् ।  
> तस्मै॒ सर॑स्वती दुहे क्षी॒रं स॒र्पिर्मधू॑द॒कम् ॥ ३२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पावमानीः । यः । अधिऽएति । ऋषिऽभिः । सम्ऽभृतम् । रसम् ।  
> तस्मै । सरस्वती । दुहे । क्षीरम् । सर्पिः । मधु । उदकम् ॥ ३२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यः ब्राह्मणः पावमानीः पवमानदेवताका ऋचः तदात्मकम् ऋषिभिः मधुच्छंदआदिभिः । संभृतं रसं वेदसारं सूक्तसंघम् अध्येति अधीते तस्मै पवमानाध्ययनं कुर्वते जनाय सरस्वती सर्वत्र सरणवती वाग्देवता क्षीरं यज्ञसाधनभूतं पयः सर्पिः तादृशं घृतं मधु मदकरम् उदकं सोमं दुहे स्वयमेव दोग्धि। एनं नरं यागादिपरं वेदशास्त्रविदं करोतीत्यर्थः । दुह प्रपूरणे । कर्मकर्तरि ‘न दुहस्नुनमां यक्चिणौ ' इति यकः प्रतिषेधः । ‘लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेषु' इति तलोपः॥ ॥१८॥ ॥ ३ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The brāhmaṇa who studies the Ṛks addressed to Pavamāna, which are of that nature, the essence of the Veda, the collection of sūktas brought together by the seers, Madhucchandas and the rest: for him, the man who makes the study of Pavamāna, Sarasvatī, the goddess of speech, who goes everywhere, herself milks milk, the means of the sacrifice, ghee of that kind, honey, the exhilarating water, Soma. The meaning is that she makes this man devoted to sacrifice and the like, a knower of the Veda and the śāstra.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—the man who
- पावमानीः (*pāvamānīḥ*)—addressed to the deity Pavamāna
- ऋषिभिः (*ṛṣibhiḥ*)—by the seers
- संस्कृतं (*saṃskṛtaṃ*)—collected **NOTE**
- रसं (*rasaṃ*)—the sūkta, which is the essence of the Vedas
- अध्येति (*adhyeti*)—recites
- तस्मै (*tasmai*)—for him
- सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*)—the goddess Sarasvatī
- क्षीरं (*kṣīraṃ*)—milk
- सर्पिः (*sarpiḥ*)—ghee
- मधु (*madhu*)—honey
- उदकं (*udakaṃ*)—Soma
- दुहे (*duhe*)—milks

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

For the man who recites these sūktas, which are addressed to the deity Pavamāna, collected by the seers, the essence of the Vedas, the goddess Sarasvatī milks milk, ghee, honey and Soma.

##### English translation
For him who reads the hymns to Pavamana, the essence (of the Veda) collected by the Rishis, Saraswati milks milk, ghee, and exilarating Soma.

### Printed p. 370

**Supplementary mantras to be recited at the end of Sūkta 67**

The total of 610 ṛks of the sixty-seven sūktas of this ninth maṇḍala are well known as the Pāvamānī ṛks. All these ṛks are in the Gāyatrī metre. We have explained many times that the ṛks in the Gāyatrī metre have a special excellence. Therefore, the fruits that come to those who study the 610 ṛks in the Gāyatrī metre addressed to the deity Pavamāna Soma, and the removal of the many kinds of sins they may have committed earlier, are bestowed by these Pāvamānī ṛks, that is, by the Veda-Puruṣa, the lord of all, as is stated in these supplementary mantras. The supplementary mantras and their main purport are explained further.

पावमानीः स्वस्त्ययनीः सुदुघा हि धृतश्चुतः । ऋषिभिः संभृतो रसो ब्राह्मणेष्वमृतं हितं (*pāvamānīḥ svastyayanīḥ sudughā hi dhṛtaścutaḥ | ṛṣibhiḥ saṃbhṛto raso brāhmaṇeṣvamṛtaṃ hitaṃ*)

These (6-0) ṛks in the Gāyatrī metre, which praise the deity called Pavamāna Soma, bring welfare to those who study them. For their satisfaction they milk ghee (the means of wealth), or water in the form of rain; that is, by granting rain they become the cause of the means of wealth. Many seers, drawing out the essence of many mantras, have gathered into these Pāvamānī mantras that sap or essence, which is nectar-like and beneficial. **NOTE**

पावमानीर्दिशंतु न इमं लोकमधो अमुं । कामान्त्समर्धयंतु नो देवीर्देवैः समाहिताः ॥ (*pāvamānīrdiśaṃtu na imaṃ lokamadho amuṃ | kāmāntsamardhayaṃtu no devīrdevaiḥ samāhitāḥ ‖*)

May these Pāvamānī ṛks, which are of the nature of deities, joined with all the other gods, procure for us the happiness that can be had in this world and the happiness that can be had in the other world, and may they fulfil all our desires.

येन देवाः पवित्रेणात्मानं पुनते सदा । तेन सहस्रधारेण पावमान्यः पुनंतु मां (*yena devāḥ pavitreṇātmānaṃ punate sadā | tena sahasradhāreṇa pāvamānyaḥ punaṃtu māṃ*)

With the streams of thousands of flowing Soma juice by which all the gods always purify themselves (that is, by drinking Soma), may these Pāvamānī ṛks purify me too.

प्राजापत्यं पवित्रं शतोद्यामं हिरण्मयं । तेन ब्रह्मविदो वयं पूतं ब्रह्म पुनीमहे ॥ (*prājāpatyaṃ pavitraṃ śatodyāmaṃ hiraṇmayaṃ | tena brahmavido vayaṃ pūtaṃ brahma punīmahe ‖*)

### Printed p. 371

Whatever Soma juice there is that belongs to Prajāpati, that is, was created by Prajāpati, that flows streaming in hundreds of streams, that is endowed with a splendour shining like gold, and that is itself pure, by that (by reciting it) we (the seers), knowers of Brahman or knowers of the mantra, purify the mantra or the food in the form of oblation.

इंद्रः पुनीती सह मा पुनातु सोमः स्वस्तावरुणः समिच्या । यमो राजा प्रमृणाभिः पुनातु मा जातवेदा मूर्जयंत्या पुनातु ॥ (*iṃdraḥ punītī saha mā punātu somaḥ svastāvaruṇaḥ samicyā | yamo rājā pramṛṇābhiḥ punātu mā jātavedā mūrjayaṃtyā punātu ‖*)

May Indra, who has become pure (or delighted) by drinking Soma, purify me as well. May the god Soma purify me by granting welfare, Varuṇa by excellent guidance, Yama, the lord, by choice things, and Agni by granting food that is full of sap.

ऋषयस्तु तपस्तेपुः सर्वे स्वर्गजिगीषवः । तपंतस्तपसोग्रेण पावमानीर्ऋचोऽब्रुवन् ॥ (*ṛṣayastu tapastepuḥ sarve svargajigīṣavaḥ | tapaṃtastapasogreṇa pāvamānīrṛco 'bruvan ‖*) (Pariśiṣṭa 18-6)

In former times, desiring to obtain heaven, all the seers performed fierce austerity, studied these Pāvamānī ṛks, and made in this manner a praise of them as the remover of sin.

यन्मे गर्भे वसतः पापमुग्रं यज्जायमानस्य च किंचिदन्यत् । जातस्य च यच्चापि च वर्धतो मे तत्पावमानीभिरहं पुनामि ॥ (*yanme garbhe vasataḥ pāpamugraṃ yajjāyamānasya ca kiṃcidanyat | jātasya ca yaccāpi ca vardhato me tatpāvamānībhirahaṃ punāmi ‖*) (Pari. 18-7) **NOTE**

The Veda-Puruṣa, the lord of all, speaks thus: whatever man, while dwelling in the womb, and later while being born, and after birth, and while growing, has committed extremely fierce sin, if he studies the Pāvamānī mantras, I destroy all such sins and make him wholly pure.

मातापित्रोर्यन्न कृतं वचो मे यत्स्थावरं जंगममा बभूव । विश्वस्य तत्पृहृषितं वचो मे तत्पावमानीभिरहं पुनामि ॥ (*mātāpitroryanna kṛtaṃ vaco me yatsthāvaraṃ jaṃgamamā babhūva | viśvasya tatpṛhṛṣitaṃ vaco me tatpāvamānībhirahaṃ punāmi ‖*) (18-8)

The sin of transgressing the word of father and mother, and whatever sin arises from speech uttered wishing harm to any being in this world, movable or immovable, such sin too I remove, and I make him wholly pure.

गोघ्नात् तस्करत्वात् स्त्रीवधाद्यच्च किल्पिषं । पापकं च चरणेभ्यस्तत्पावमानीभिरहं पुनामि ॥ (*goghnāt taskaratvāt strīvadhādyacca kilpiṣaṃ | pāpakaṃ ca caraṇebhyastatpāvamānībhirahaṃ punāmi ‖*) (Hari. 18-9) **NOTE**

Killing of a cow, theft, killing of a woman, the act of harming creatures by trampling them with the feet: the sin that may arise from these I remove and make him pure.

ब्रह्मवधात्सुरापानात्स्वर्णस्तेयाद्वृषलिगमनमैथुनसंगमात् । गुरोर्दाराधिगमनाच्च तत्पावमानीभिरहं पुनामि ॥ (*brahmavadhātsurāpānātsvarṇasteyādvṛṣaligamanamaithunasaṃgamāt | gurordārādhigamanācca tatpāvamānībhirahaṃ punāmi ‖*) (Sari. 18-10) **NOTE**

Killing of a Brāhmaṇa, drinking liquor, stealing gold, the sin of having intercourse with a woman called Vṛṣalī, who is unmarried although her younger sister is married, the sin of sexual intercourse with the wife of one's teacher: all these I remove and make him pure.

बालघ्नान्मातृपितृवधाध्भूमितस्करात्सर्ववर्णगमनमैथुनसंगमात् । पापेभ्यश्च प्रतिग्रहात्सद्यः प्रहरति सर्वदुष्कृतं तत्पामानीभिरहं पुनामि ॥ (*bālaghnānmātṛpitṛvadhādhbhūmitaskarātsarvavarṇagamanamaithunasaṃgamāt | pāpebhyaśca pratigrahātsadyaḥ praharati sarvaduṣkṛtaṃ tatpāmānībhirahaṃ punāmi ‖*) (Pari. 18-11) **NOTE**

Killing children, killing father and mother, fraudulently seizing land such as fields, consorting with women of all the low castes, accepting improper gifts, doing other evil deeds: whatever sins arise from these, I remove all those sins and make him wholly pure.

क्रयविक्रयाद्योनिदोषाद्भक्षाद्योज्यात्पतिग्रहात् । असंभोजनाच्चापि नृशंसं तत्पावमानीभिरहं पुनामि ॥ (*krayavikrayādyonidoṣādbhakṣādyojyātpatigrahāt | asaṃbhojanāccāpi nṛśaṃsaṃ tatpāvamānībhirahaṃ punāmi ‖*) (Pari. 18-12)

Buying and selling by unjust means, that is, by fraud; consorting with whatever women come one's way; eating things that must not be eaten; accepting things that are not fit to be accepted; eating without the guest who has come to the house: I remove the sins arising from these.

दुर्यष्टं दुरधीतं पापं यच्चा ज्ञानतो कृतं । अयाजिताश्च संयाज्यास्तत्पावमानीभिरहं पुनामि ॥ (*duryaṣṭaṃ duradhītaṃ pāpaṃ yaccā jñānato kṛtaṃ | ayājitāśca saṃyājyāstatpāvamānībhirahaṃ punāmi ‖*)

Performing a sacrifice otherwise than in the manner prescribed, studying the Veda without discipline, the sin done through ignorance, making those who are not entitled to sacrifice perform a sacrifice, not making those entitled to it perform it: the sins arising from such wrong deeds I remove and make him pure.

अमंत्रमन्नं यत्किंचिद्भूयते च हुताशने । संवत्सरकृतं पापं तत्पावमानीभिरहं पुनामि ॥ (*amaṃtramannaṃ yatkiṃcidbhūyate ca hutāśane | saṃvatsarakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tatpāvamānībhirahaṃ punāmi ‖*) (Pari. 18-14)

The sin arising from offering oblation in the fire without reciting the mantra prescribed, or while reciting the mantra wrongly, and whatever sins have been committed during the year, all these I remove and make him wholly pure.

ऋतस्य योनयोऽमृतस्य धाम विश्वा देवेभ्यः पुण्यगंधाः । ता न आपः प्र वहंतु पापं शुद्धा गच्छामि सुकृतामु लोकं तत्पावमानीभिरहं पुनामि ॥ (*ṛtasya yonayo 'mṛtasya dhāma viśvā devebhyaḥ puṇyagaṃdhāḥ | tā na āpaḥ pra vahaṃtu pāpaṃ śuddhā gacchāmi sukṛtāmu lokaṃ tatpāvamānībhirahaṃ punāmi ‖*) (Pari. 18-15)

May the heavenly waters, which are the chief support of truth or of the sacrifice, which dwell in eternal heaven, and which cause delight to the gods, wash away the sins mentioned above. Having made that man pure, I shall cause him to obtain the excellent world.

पावमानीः स्वस्त्ययनीयार्भिर्गच्छति नांदनं । पुण्यांश्च भक्षान्भक्षयत्यमृतत्वं च गच्छति ॥ (*pāvamānīḥ svastyayanīyārbhirgacchati nāṃdanaṃ | puṇyāṃśca bhakṣānbhakṣayatyamṛtatvaṃ ca gacchati ‖*)

These Pāvamānī ṛks bring auspiciousness to those who recite them. By the study or recitation of these ṛks a man obtains joy and merit. Eating excellent food and delicacies he is satisfied, and at the end of his life he obtains the supreme state free from death and is happy.

पावमानीः पितृन्देवान् ध्यायेद्यश्च सरस्वतीं । पित्यंस्तस्योपवर्तेत क्षीरं सर्पिर्मधूदकं ॥ (*pāvamānīḥ pitṛndevān dhyāyedyaśca sarasvatīṃ | pityaṃstasyopavarteta kṣīraṃ sarpirmadhūdakaṃ ‖*)

The man who, reciting the Pāvamānī ṛks, meditates on the Pitṛ deities and on the goddess Sarasvatī: the Pitṛ deities, staying near such a man, milk for him in abundance milk, ghee, honey and water; that is, they cause an abundance of them to arise.

पावमानं परं ब्रह्म शुक्रं ज्योतिः सनातनं । ऋषींस्तस्योपतिष्ठेत क्षीरं सर्पिर्मधूदकं ॥ (*pāvamānaṃ paraṃ brahma śukraṃ jyotiḥ sanātanaṃ | ṛṣīṃstasyopatiṣṭheta kṣīraṃ sarpirmadhūdakaṃ ‖*)

The man who meditates on the deity Pavamāna Soma, who is of the nature of Supreme Brahman, shines with extreme splendour, is of the nature of light and is without beginning or end, and on the seers who praised that god,

### Printed p. 374

and who worships him, for him there arises an abundance of milk, ghee, honey and water; that is, an abundance of manifold wealth arises.

पावमानं परं ब्रह्म ये पठंति मनीषिणः । सप्त जन्म भवेद्विप्रो धनाढ्यो वेदपारगः ॥ (*pāvamānaṃ paraṃ brahma ye paṭhaṃti manīṣiṇaḥ | sapta janma bhavedvipro dhanāḍhyo vedapāragaḥ ‖*)

The discerning men who recite and praise this Pavamāna mantra, which is of the nature of Supreme Brahman, will in the next seven births be born in the Brāhmaṇa birth itself, and be wealthy and accomplished in the study of the Veda, and be happy.

दशोत्तराण्यृचांश्चेव पावमानीः शतानि षट् । एतज्जुह्वन् जपेन्मंत्रं घोरमृत्युभयं हरेत् ॥ (*daśottarāṇyṛcāṃśceva pāvamānīḥ śatāni ṣaṭ | etajjuhvan japenmaṃtraṃ ghoramṛtyubhayaṃ haret ‖*)

If one recites these 610 ṛks in the Gāyatrī metre which praise the deity Pavamāna Soma, and offers oblation in the fire with the mantra, even such a terrible fear of death is removed.

एतत्पुण्यं पापहरं रोगमृत्युभयापहं । पठतां शृण्वतां चैव ददाति परमां गतिं ॥ (*etatpuṇyaṃ pāpaharaṃ rogamṛtyubhayāpahaṃ | paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiva dadāti paramāṃ gatiṃ ‖*)

For those who recite or listen to these Pāvamānī mantras, which bestow merit and remove sin, all disease and fear of death perish, and for them there arises the supreme state, that is, the attainment of the excellent world of heaven.

## Sūkta 68 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> चतुर्थेऽनुवाकेऽष्टादश सूक्तानि । तत्र ‘प्र देवम्' इति दशर्चं प्रथमं सूक्तं भलंदनपुत्रस्य वत्सप्रेरार्षं पवमानसोमदेवताकम् । दशमी त्रिष्टुप् शिष्टा जगत्यः । तथा चानुक्रम्यते- प्र देवं दश वत्सप्रिर्भालंदनस्त्रिष्टुबंतं ह' इति । गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that in the fourth anuvāka there are eighteen sūktas. Of these, the first is the sūkta of ten ṛks beginning प्र देवम् (*pra devam*), whose seer is Vatsapri, son of Bhalandana, and whose deity is Pavamāna Soma. The tenth ṛk is in the Triṣṭup metre and the rest are in Jagatī. He cites the Anukramaṇī: प्र देवं दश वत्सप्रिर्भालंदनस्त्रिष्टुबंतं ह (*pra devaṃ daśa vatsaprirbhālaṃdanastriṣṭubaṃtaṃ ha*). The application (viniyoga) has already been stated.

Translation.—In the fourth anuvāka of the ninth maṇḍala there are eighteen sūktas. Among them this sūkta beginning प्र देवं (*pra devaṃ*) is the first. It contains ten ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Vatsapri, the son of the seer called Bhalandana. The deity is Pavamāna Soma;

### Printed p. 375

the tenth ṛk of this sūkta is in the Triṣṭup metre. The remaining ṛks are in the Jagatī metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: प्र देवं दश वत्सप्रिर्भालंदनस्त्रिष्टुबंतं ह (*pra devaṃ daśa vatsaprirbhālaṃdanastriṣṭubaṃtaṃ ha*). The application of the sūkta has been stated earlier.

Maṇḍala 9; Anuvāka 4; Sūkta 68; Aṣṭaka 7, Adhyāya 2, Varga 19, 20. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 10. Ṛṣi: Vatsapri Bhālandana. Devatā: Pavamāna Soma. Chandas: 1–9 Jagatī; 10 Triṣṭup.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र दे॒वमच्छा॒ मधु॑मंत॒ इंद॒वोऽसि॑ष्यदंत॒ गाव॒ आ न धे॒नवः॑ ।  
> ब॒र्हि॒षदो॑ वच॒नावं॑त॒ ऊध॑भिः परि॒स्रुत॑मु॒स्रिया॑ नि॒र्णिजं॑ धिरे ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । देवम् । अच्छ । मधुऽमंतः । इंदवः । असिस्यदंत । गावः । आ । न । धेनवः ।  
> बर्हिऽसदः । वचनाऽवंतः । ऊधऽभिः । परिऽस्रुतम् । उस्रियाः । निःऽनिजम् । धिरे ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मधुमंतः मादकरससंयुक्ताः इंदवः सोमाः देवं द्योतमानं सोमात्मकमिंद्रम् अच्छ प्रति प्र असिष्यदंत प्रस्यंदंते । ग्रहादिषु प्रक्षरंति । स्यंदतेर्ण्यंतस्य लुङि चङि रूपम् । तत्र दृष्टांतः । गाव आ न धेनवः । पयस्विन्यः प्रीणयित्र्यो गावो यथा वत्सं प्रति पयांसि प्रस्रवंति तद्वत्। किंच बर्हिषदः बर्हिषि सीदंतः वचनावंतः हंभारवादिशब्दवंतः उस्रियाः । गोनामैतत् । तादृश्यो गावः ऊधभिः पयोधारकैः स्वैः स्वैरूधभिः परिस्रुतं परितः स्रवणशीलं निर्णिजं शुद्धं पयोभूतं सोमरसं धिरे दधिरे । इंद्रार्थं धारयंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains that the Soma drops (इंदवः (*iṃdavaḥ*)), endowed with intoxicating juice, flow towards the shining god, that is, Indra in the form of Soma, and drip into the cups (grahas) and the like. As an illustration he gives गाव आ न धेनवः (*gāva ā na dhenavaḥ*): just as milk-giving, satisfying cows stream their milk towards the calf, so do the Soma drops. Further, the cows (उस्रियाः (*usriyāḥ*) is a name for cows), seated on the sacred grass and lowing with sounds such as the cry of the cow, bear with their own milk-holding udders the Soma juice, which flows all around and is pure, being turned into milk, for Indra; that is, they hold it for Indra's sake.

- धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*)—milk-giving
- गावः न (*gāvaḥ na*)—as cows run lovingly to their calf
- मधुमंतः (*madhumaṃtaḥ*)—those endowed with sweet juice
- इंदवः (*iṃdavaḥ*)—the flowing Soma juices
- देवं अच्छ (*devaṃ accha*)—towards Indra, who is of divine nature
- प्र आसिष्यदंत (*pra āsiṣyadaṃta*)—flow
- बर्हिषदः (*barhiṣadaḥ*)—those seated on the seat of the assembly **NOTE**
- वचनावंतः (*vacanāvaṃtaḥ*)—those that make sound

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As milk-giving cows run lovingly to their calf, the Soma juices, endowed with sweet juice and flowing, flow towards Indra, who is of divine nature. The cows, seated on the seat of darbha grass, making sound and giving milk, bear in their udders the flowing, pure Soma juice in the form of milk.

##### English translation
The exhilarating Soma-juices flow towards the shining (Indra), as milch cow (hasten to their calves) the lowing cows sitting on the barhis grass hold in their udders the pure (juice) welling up.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स रोरु॑वद॒भि पूर्वा॑ अचिक्रददुपा॒रुहः॑ श्र॒थय॑न्स्वादते॒ हरिः॑ ।  
> ति॒रः प॒वित्रं॑ परि॒यन्नु॒रु ज्रयो॒ नि शर्या॑णि दधते दे॒व आ वर॑म् ॥ २ ॥

> तिरः । पवित्रम् । परिऽयन् । उरु । ज्रयः । नि । शर्याणि । दधते । देवः । आ । वरम् ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 377

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> रोरुवत् कलशादिकं प्रति अत्यंतं शब्दं कुर्वन् सः सोमः पूर्वाः मुख्याः स्तोतॄणां स्तुतीः अभि अचिक्रदत् अभिमुखमध्वनयत् । स्तुतयः साधीयस्य इति प्रतिध्वनिमंगीकारमकार्षीदित्यर्थः । किंच हरिः हरितवर्णः उपारुहः । रोहतेस्ताच्छीलिकः क्विप् । उपारोहणशीला ऊर्ध्वं प्रादुर्भवनशीला ओषधीः श्रथयन् अग्रे विश्लेषयन् स्वादते स्वादूकरोति । ताः फलिनीः कुर्वन स्वादुयुक्ता विदधातीत्यर्थः । तथा पवित्रम् अविवालात्मकं दशापवित्रं तिरः तिरस्कृत्य पात्राणि प्रत्यात्मनः क्षरणकाले पवित्रं व्यवधायकं कृत्वा परियन् परितो गच्छन् सोमः उरु महांतं ज्रयः वेगं करोति । ततः शर्याणि । ' शृ हिंसायाम् ' । हिंसितव्यानि यद्वा शरेण हंतव्यानि रक्षांसि नि दधते निक्षिपति न्यक्करोति । हिनस्तीति यावत् । पश्चात् देवः दीप्यमानः सोमः वरं वरणीयं धनं सोमदातृभ्यो यजमानेभ्यः आ दधते आधारयति । प्रयच्छतीत्यर्थः । दधातेः लेट्यडागमे ‘ घोर्लोपो लेटि वा ' इत्याकारलोपः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains that Soma, making a great sound towards the vessels and the like (रोरुवत् (*roruvat*)), has made the principal praises of the singers resound (अभि अचिक्रदत् (*abhi acikradat*)); that is, he has given an echo as his assent (स्तुतयः साधीयस्य (*stutayaḥ sādhīyasya*)). **NOTE** Further, Hari, the green-hued one, loosens at their tip the herbs that grow upward and sweetens them; that is, he makes them fruitful and full of sweetness. Likewise Soma, going around and crossing the ten-fold filter (दशापवित्रं (*daśāpavitraṃ*)), which is made of sheep's wool, having made the filter an intervening screen at the time of flowing into the vessels, acquires great speed. Then he casts down (destroys) the things to be injured, or the demons to be slain with an arrow. Afterwards the shining Soma bestows excellent, desirable wealth upon the sacrificers who offer Soma; that is, he gives it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सः (*saḥ*)—the well-known Soma
- रोरुवत् (*roruvat*)—making a sound
- पूर्वाः (*pūrvāḥ*)—the principal praises
- अभ्यचिक्रदत् (*abhyacikradat*)—makes them resound as an echo
- हरिः (*hariḥ*)—the green-hued Soma
- उपारुहः (*upāruhaḥ*)—the herbs that grow upward
- श्रथयन् (*śrathayan*)—separating
- स्वादते (*svādate*)—makes them tasty
- पवित्रं (*pavitraṃ*)—the ten-fold filter
- तिरः (*tiraḥ*)—crossing
- परियन् (*pariyan*)—the flowing Soma
- उरु (*uru*)—great
- ज्रयः (*jrayaḥ*)—attains speed
- नि दधते (*ni dadhate*)—destroys the demons and others
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—the shining Soma
- वरं (*varaṃ*)—excellent wealth
- आ दधते (*ā dadhate*)—provides to the sacrificers and others

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The well-known Soma, making a sound, makes the principal praises resound as an echo. The green-hued Soma, separating the herbs that grow upward, makes them tasty. The Soma that flows crossing the ten-fold filter attains great speed. He destroys the demons and others. The shining Soma provides excellent wealth to the sacrificers and others.

##### English translation
He with a noise re-echoes the principal (praises) separating the growing herbs, the green-tinted (Soma, sweetens them ; passing through the filter, (he

### Printed p. 378

exerts) great speed, he annihilates the Rakhasas, the shining (Soma) bestows wealth (upon the worshippers.)

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वि यो म॒मे य॒म्या॑ संय॒ती मदः॑ साकं॒वृधा॒ पय॑सा पिन्व॒दक्षि॑ता ।  
> म॒ही अ॑पा॒रे रज॑सी वि॒वेवि॑ददभि॒व्रज॒न्नक्षि॑तं॒ पाज॒ आ द॑दे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वि । यः । ममे । यम्या । संयती इति सम्ऽयती । मदः । साकम्ऽवृधा । पयसा । पिन्वत् । अक्षिता ।  
> मही इति । अपारे इति । रजसी इति । विऽवेविदत् । अभिऽव्रजन् । अक्षितम् । पाजः । आ । ददे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यः मदः । माद्यत्यनेनेति मदः सोमरसः । यम्या युगलभूते संयती परस्परं संगच्छमाने द्यावापृथिव्यौ वि ममे विशेषेण निर्मितवान् ततः ते साकंवृधा सहैव वर्धनशीले तथा अक्षिता अक्षीणे सामर्थ्यवत्यौ यथा भविष्यतः तथा स सोमः पयसा पयोरूपेण स्वीयरसेन पिन्वत् असिंचत् । अवर्धयदिति यावत् । किंच मही महत्यौ अत एव अपारे पर्यंतरहिते रजसी । द्यावापृथिवीनामैतत् । ते द्यावापृथिव्यौ विवेविदत् । ‘ विद ज्ञाने ' । यङ्लुकि शतरि रूपम् । अभ्यासस्वरः । इयं पृथिवीयं द्यौरिति सर्वेषां विविच्य तेजसा प्रज्ञापयन् अभिव्रजन् अभितः सर्वतो गच्छन् स सोमः अक्षितम् अक्षीणमविनश्वरं पाजः बलम् आ ददे स्वीकृतवान् । अत्यंतं बलवानभवदित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains that मदः (*madaḥ*) is the Soma juice, that by which one is intoxicated. That Soma fashioned in a special way the twin heaven and earth (यम्या युगलभूते (*yamyā yugalabhūte*)), which meet each other. Then, so that these two would grow together and be imperishable and capable, that Soma nourished them (पिन्वत् (*pinvat*)) with his own juice in the form of milk; that is, he made them grow. Further, these two, great and therefore boundless (रजसी (*rajasī*) is a name for heaven and earth), he made known (विवेविदत् (*vivevidat*)): having discriminated them for all, "this is earth, this is heaven", he made them known by his radiance. Going all around, that Soma took imperishable, indestructible strength; that is, he became exceedingly strong.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मदः (*madaḥ*)—the exhilarating
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Soma-deva
- यम्या (*yamyā*)—those that exist as a pair (as two)
- संयती (*saṃyatī*)—and are united, the heaven and earth
- वि ममे (*vi mame*)—created; that same Soma
- साकंवृधा (*sākaṃvṛdhā*)—so that both grow together

- अक्षिता (*akṣitā*)—so that they become imperishable
- पयसा (*payasā*)—with his juice
- पिन्वत् (*pinvat*)—nourished
- मही (*mahī*)—of great form
- अपारे (*apāre*)—and endless
- रजसी (*rajasī*)—heaven and earth
- विवेविदत् (*vivevidat*)—separated and established, so that all may know them
- अभिव्रजन् (*abhivrajan*)—moving around
- अक्षितं (*akṣitaṃ*)—imperishable
- पाजः (*pājaḥ*)—strength
- आ ददे (*ā dade*)—obtained

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The exhilarating Soma-deva who created the heaven and earth, which are two and yet united, nourished them with his own juice so that both would grow together and be imperishable. He separated and established the heaven and earth, great in form and endless, so that all may know them. Moving all around, he obtained imperishable strength.

##### English translation
The exhilarating (Soma) who constructed the twin united (heaven and earth) does by means of his juice maintain them growing together, imperisha-ble: he has distinguished these two great unbounded worlds. wandering everywhere, he has assumed imperishable strength. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स मा॒तरा॑ वि॒चर॑न्वा॒जय॑न्न॒पः प्र मेधि॑रः स्व॒धया॑ पिन्वते प॒दम् ।  
> अं॒शुर्यवे॑न पिपिशे य॒तो नृभिः॒ सं जा॒मिभि॒र्नस॑ते॒ रक्ष॑ते॒ शिरः॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । मातरा । विऽचरन् । वाजयन् । अपः । प्र । मेधिरः । स्वधया । पिन्वते । पदम् ।  
> अंशुः । यवेन । पिपिशे । यतः । नृऽभिः । सम् । जामिऽभिः । नसते । रक्षते । शिरः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मेधिरः । 'मेधारथाभ्यामिरनिरचौ' (पा. सू. ५.२.१०९.३) इतरन्प्रत्ययो मत्वर्थीयः । मेधावान् प्राज्ञः सः सोमः मातरा मातरौ जगतो निर्मात्र्यौ द्यावापृथिव्यौ विचरन् अंतरेणात्यंतं चरन् तथा अपः अंतरिक्षस्थितान्युदकानि वाजयन् प्रेरयन् । वजेर्ण्यंतस्य शतरि रूपम् । तादृशः स्वधया सक्तुलक्षणेनान्नेन सह पदं स्वस्थानमुत्तरवेदिरूपं प्र पिन्वते प्रकर्षेणाप्याययति । ततः नृभिः कर्मनेतृभिर्ऋत्विग्भिः यतः संयतः अंशुः सोमः यवेन पिपिशे । ‘ पिश अवयवे'। अवयवत्वेन कृतः । मिश्रित इत्यर्थः । सोमस्तु यवसक्तुभिः श्रीयते खलु। सोऽयं जामिभिः एकस्मात्पाणेरुत्पन्नाभिरंगुलीभिः सं नसते संगच्छते च । शिरः शीर्णं भूतजातं रक्षते च । स्वीयरसेन रक्षति पोषयति । नसतिर्गतिकर्मा । ‘चादिलोपे विभाषा' इति न निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains that the wise Soma, going about between the two mothers, that is, heaven and earth, the makers of the world, and driving forth the waters standing in the atmosphere, nourishes (प्र पिन्वते (*pra pinvate*)) with svadhā, that is, with food in the form of barley meal, his own place, which is the northern altar. Then the Soma, controlled by the priests, the leaders of the rite, is mixed with barley; Soma is indeed mixed with barley meal. This same Soma is joined with the fingers (जामिभिः (*jāmibhiḥ*)), those born from one hand. He also protects the शिरः (*śiraḥ*), the broken (worn) beings; he protects and nourishes them with his own juice. **NOTE**

> यूना । ह । संता । प्रथमम् । वि । जज्ञतुः । गुहा । हितम् । जनिम । नेमम् । उत्ऽयतम् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्रसंगात् सोमसूर्ययोराविर्भावमाह । दक्षेण प्रवृद्धेन मनसा सह सं जायते पृथिव्याः सम्यग्जायते । तथा ऋतस्य उदकस्यैव गर्भः गर्भस्थानीयः । यद्वा । सत्यस्य यज्ञस्य मध्ये गर्भः शब्दनीयः स्तुत्यः । स एव सोमः परः परस्तादंतरिक्षे यमा यमेन नियमेन देवैः निहितः सः । सूर्याद्धि वृष्टिर्भवति । तस्मात्सोमः सूर्यात्मकतयावस्थित इत्यर्थः । एवं यूना। ह इत्यवधारणे। युवानावेव संतौ तौ प्रथमं जननकाले वि जज्ञतुः । अयं सोमोऽयं सूर्य इति विशेषेण ज्ञायते । तयोश्चार्धं जनिम जन्म गुहा गुहायां हितं निहितं भवति । तयोः नेमम् अर्धं च उद्यतं प्रकाशितं भवति । दिवा सूर्यः प्रादुर्भवति रात्री चंद्रमा इ   ति ॥ ॥ १९ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that, by the way, he now describes the manifestation of Soma and Sūrya. Soma is born together with a developed mind (दक्षेण प्रवृद्धेन मनसा (*dakṣeṇa pravṛddhena manasā*)); that is, he is properly born from the earth. Likewise he is the embryo of water itself, one who stands in the place of an embryo. Or else: in the midst of truth, that is, of the sacrifice, he is the embryo to be praised. That same Soma, far off in the atmosphere, is placed by the gods through restraint (यमा (*yamā*)). Rain comes from the sun; therefore the meaning is that Soma stands in the form of the sun. Thus: ह (*ha*) in यूना ह (*yūnā ha*) is used for emphasis. Though both were young, at the time of birth they were distinguished: "this is Soma, this is Sūrya". Of the two, half of the birth (जनिम (*janima*)) is placed hidden in a cave, and the other half (नेमम् (*nemam*)) is manifest and lit up: by day the sun appears, by night the moon.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कविः (*kaviḥ*)—the one of far-reaching wisdom
- (सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma)
- दक्षेण (*dakṣeṇa*)—with a developed
- मनसा (*manasā*)—mind
- सं जायते (*saṃ jāyate*)—is born
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—for water
- गर्भः (*garbhaḥ*)—as its embryo
- परः (*paraḥ*)—in the excellent atmosphere
- यमा (*yamā*)—regularly
- निहितः (*nihitaḥ*)—has been placed by the gods
- यूना ह संता (*yūnā ha saṃtā*)—these two, Sūrya and the Moon (Soma), ever young
- प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*)—at the time of origin
- वि जज्ञतुः (*vi jajñatuḥ*)—have been known as different
- जनिम (*janima*)—the birth of half of them
- गुहा (*guhā*)—secretly
- हितं (*hitaṃ*)—is placed
- नेमं (*nemaṃ*)—the other half
- उद्यतं (*udyataṃ*)—is manifest, so that all can see it

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Soma of far-reaching wisdom is born together with a developed mind. As the embryo of water he is placed regularly in the excellent atmosphere by the gods (or as one of the nature of the sun), established

### Printed p. 382

he is. The ever-young Sūrya and the Moon have been known as distinct at the time of their origin. Half of the course of their birth is placed in secret. The remaining half is manifest.

##### English translation
The sage (Soma) is born with developed mind ; having his place in the womb of the water, he is deposited (by the gods) by rule from far off ; even when young these two were distinct ; the birth (of one half) was placed in secret, the (other) half was visible.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मं॒द्रस्य॑ रू॒पं वि॑विदुर्मनी॒षिणः॑ श्ये॒नो यदंधो॒ अभ॑रत्परा॒वतः॑ ।  
> तं म॑र्जयंत सु॒वृधं॑ न॒दीष्वाँ उ॒शंत॑मं॒शुं प॑रि॒यंत॑मृ॒ग्मिय॑म् ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मंद्रस्य । रूपम् । विविदुः । मनीषिणः । श्येनः । यत् । अंधः । अभरत् । पराऽवतः ।  
> तम् । मर्जयंत । सुऽवृधम् । नदीषु । आ । उशंतम् । अंशुम् । परिऽयंतम् । ऋग्मियम् ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मनीषिणः प्राज्ञा यष्टारः मंद्रस्य मदकरस्य तस्य सोमस्य रूपं विविदुः जानंति । यत् अंधः यत् सोमलक्षणमन्नं श्येनः गायत्रीरूपः पक्षी परावतः दूरात् द्युलोकात् आभरत् आजहार। 'हृग्रहोर्भश्छंदसि ' इति भकारः। तं तादृशं  सुवृधं सुष्ठु वर्धमानं सुवर्धयितारं वा अंशुं सोमं नदीषु नदमानासु वसतीवर्याख्यास्वप्सु आ मर्जयंत ऋत्विज आशोधयंति । अलंकुर्वंति वा । कीदृशम् । उशंतं देवान् कामयमानं परियंतं परितो गच्छंतम् ऋग्मियम् ऋगर्हं स्तुत्यं सोममामर्जयंतीति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains that the wise sacrificers know the form (रूपं (*rūpaṃ*)) of that exhilarating Soma: the food in the form of Soma (अंधः (*aṃdhaḥ*)) that the falcon (श्येनः (*śyenaḥ*)), a bird of the Gāyatrī form, brought from afar, from the heavenly world. The priests purify, or adorn, that Soma, who grows well or makes others grow well, in the rivers, that is, in the sounding waters called Vasatīvarī. What kind of Soma? One that desires the gods, goes around on all sides, and is worthy of praise (ऋग्मियम् (*ṛgmiyam*) means deserving of ṛk, to be praised).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम योषणः द्वाभ्यां पाणिभ्यां विभज्योत्पन्नाः दश दशसंख्याका अंगुलयः ऋषिभिः मधुच्छंदःप्रभृतिभिः सुतम् अभिषुतं हितं पात्रेषु निहितं                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              त्वां मतिभिः स्तुतिभिः धीतिभिः कर्मभिश्च अव्यः वारेभिः अविवालैः पवित्रैः मृजंति शोधयंति । उत अपि च देवहूतिभिः देवाह्वानयुक्तैः नृभिः कर्मनेतृभिर्ऋत्विग्भिः यतः ग्रहेषु संयमितः संगृहीतस्त्वं सातये दानाय वाजम् अन्नम् आ दर्षि आविदारयसि । विवृतं करोषि । स्तोतृभ्योऽन्नादिकं प्रयच्छसीति यावत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses Soma: the ten fingers, produced by the division of the two hands, purify and cleanse you, who have been pressed by seers such as Madhucchandas and placed in the vessels, with praises, hymns and rites, and with filters of sheep's hair (अविवालैः पवित्रैः (*avivālaiḥ pavitraiḥ*)). And likewise, held back in the cups (grahas) by the priests, the leaders of the rite, who call the gods, you open up food for the sake of giving (सातये (*sātaye*)): that is, you give food and the like to the singers.

- वारेभिः (*vārebhiḥ*)—with the filters having fibres
- मृजंति (*mṛjaṃti*)—purify
- उत (*uta*)—and
- देवहूतिभिः (*devahūtibhiḥ*)—who call the gods
- नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)—by the priests

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, your juice, pressed by the seers and placed in the vessels, the ten fingers born in the hands purify with praises and with rites and with the ten-fold filters that have fibres of wool. And you, collected by the priests who call the gods, supply food for the sake of giving.

##### English translation
The ten fingers cleanse you, Soma, when effused and placed in the vessels by the Rishis, with praises, religious rites, and woollen filters; and collected by the priests with oblations to the gods you bestow food (upon the worshippers) for a gift.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> परिप्रयंतं पात्राणि परितः प्रगच्छंतं वयं देवैः काम्यमानं सुसंसदं शोभनसंसदनं सोमं मनीषाः मनस ईशित्र्यः     स्तुभः स्तुतयः अभ्यनूषत अभिष्टुवंति । वय्यम् । ‘ वी गत्यादिषु' इत्यस्माद्यति 'भय्यप्रवय्ये च छंदसि' ( पा. सू. ६. १. ८३ ) इति निपातितः । अत्रानुपसर्गस्यापि निपातनं भवति । मधुमान् मदकररसवान् यः सोमः धारया स्वीयया ऊर्मिणा वसतीवर्याख्येनोदकेन सह दिवः आकाशात् द्रोणकलश आपतति: रयिषाट् शत्रुधनानामभिभविता अमर्त्यः मनुष्यधर्मरहितः स सोमः वाचम् इयर्ति प्रेरयति । तदा हि स्तोतारः स्तुवंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains that the praises (स्तुभः (*stubhaḥ*)), the मनीषाः (*manīṣāḥ*) (those that govern the mind), praise Soma, who goes all around the vessels, is desired by the gods (वय्यम् (*vayyam*)), and has a fine seat. The Soma who, endowed with intoxicating juice (मधुमान् (*madhumān*)), falls from the sky into the Droṇa vessel with his own stream, together with the water called Vasatīvarī, who overcomes the wealth of enemies (रयिषाट् (*rayiṣāṭ*)) and is free from the nature of mortals (अमर्त्यः (*amartyaḥ*)), that Soma impels speech; for then the singers praise.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The god Soma, endowed with sweet juice, who descends from the atmosphere together with his stream and the waters such as Vasatīvarī, seizes the wealth of enemies, and, free from the nature of mortals, impels speech: such a god Soma, who flows all around, is desired by the gods and has an excellent seat, meditative praises extol.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अयम् । दिवः । इयर्ति । विश्वम् । आ । रजः । सोमः । पुनानः । कलशेषु । सीदति ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयं सोमः दिवः द्युलोकात् विश्वं रजः । उदकनामैतत् । सर्वमुदकम् इयर्ति अभिप्रापयति । किंच पुनानः दशापवित्रेण पूयमानः सोमः कलशेषु द्रोणनामसु सीदति । तथा अद्रिभिः ग्रावभिः अद्भिः वसतीवर्याख्याभिः गोभिः गोविकारैः क्षीरदध्यादिभिश्च मृज्यते शोध्यते अलंक्रियते । ततः पुनानः पूतः इंदुः सोमः प्रियं प्रियतरं प्रीणनकारि वा वरिवः वरणीयं धनं विदत् स्तोतृभ्यो लंभयति । प्रयच्छतीति यावत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains that this Soma brings from the heavenly world all the water (रजः (*rajaḥ*) is a name for water). Further, Soma, being purified (पुनानः (*punānaḥ*)) with the ten-fold filter, sits in the vessels called Droṇa. Likewise he is cleansed and adorned with the pressing stones, with the waters called Vasatīvarī, and with the products of cows, such as milk and curds. Then the purified Indu, Soma, obtains dear and delightful, or gladdening, desirable wealth (वरिवः (*varivaḥ*)) and has it reach the singers; that is, he gives it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this god Soma
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—from the heavenly world
- विश्वं रजः (*viśvaṃ rajaḥ*)—all the waters
- इयर्ति (*iyarti*)—impels
- पुनानः (*punānaḥ*)—having attained purity
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- कलशेषु (*kalaśeṣu*)—in the Droṇa vessels
- सीदति (*sīdati*)—is established
- अद्रिभिः (*adribhiḥ*)—by the pressing stones
- सुतः (*sutaḥ*)—pressed
- अद्भिः (*adbhiḥ*)—with the waters
- गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)—with milk and the like

- मृज्यते (*mṛjyate*)—becomes pure
- पुनानः (*punānaḥ*)—wholly purified
- इंदुः (*iṃduḥ*)—Soma
- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—beneficial
- वरिवः (*varivaḥ*)—wealth
- विदत् (*vidat*)—provides to the singers

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This god Soma impels all the waters from the heavenly world. Having attained purity, Soma is established in the Droṇa vessels. Pressed by the pressing stones, mixed with the waters and with milk and the like, he becomes wholly pure. The purified Soma provides beneficial wealth to the singers.

##### English translation
This Soma sends from heaven all water ; being filtered he settles in the vessels ; effused with the stones he is cleansed with water and milk ; the filtered Indu bestows delightful wealth.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒वा नः॑ सोम परिषि॒च्यमा॑नो॒ वयो॒ दध॑च्चि॒त्रत॑मं पवस्व ।  
> अ॒द्वे॒षे द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी हु॑वेम॒ देवा॑ ध॒त्त र॒यिम॒स्मे सु॒वीर॑म् ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एव । नः । सोम । परिऽसिच्यमानः । वयः । दधत् । चित्रऽतमम् । पवस्व ।  
> अद्वेषे इति । द्यावापृथिवी इति । हुवेम । देवाः । धत्त । रयिम् । अस्मे इति । सुऽवीरम् ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयं प्रत्यक्षकृतः । हे सोम दधत् प्रयच्छंस्त्वं परिषिच्यमानः परितोऽद्भिर्गोभिर्वा सिच्यमानः एव चित्रतमं चित्रं नानाविधं चायनीयतमं वा वयः अन्नं नः अस्मभ्यं पवस्व प्रापय । प्रयच्छेति यावत् । किंच अद्वेषे द्वेषरहिते द्यावापृथिवी द्यावापृथिव्यौ हुवेम हविष्प्रदानार्थं वयमाह्वयेम । हे देवाः यूयं च सुवीरम् । वीरः कर्मणि समर्थः पुत्रः । तादृशपुत्रोपेतं रयिं धनम् अस्मे अस्मासु धत्त निधत्त ॥ ॥ २० ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that this ṛk is addressed directly to Soma. O Soma, giving as you are sprinkled all around (परिषिच्यमानः (*pariṣicyamānaḥ*)), that is, sprinkled with water or with milk, bestow on us the most wonderful, manifold, or most desirable food (वयः (*vayaḥ*)). Further, we invoke Heaven and Earth, free from hatred, for the offering of oblation. And you, O gods, place in us wealth together with a good son (सुवीरम् (*suvīram*): a hero, वीरः (*vīraḥ*), is a son who is capable in rites).

O god Soma, you who possess wealth, as soon as you are sprinkled by us, provide us with food of many kinds. Let us call, praying, both Heaven and Earth, who wish us no harm. O gods, establish in us wealth accompanied by excellent heroic sons.

## Sūkta 69 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> 'इषुर्न' इति दशर्चं द्वितीयं सूक्तमांगिरसस्य हिरण्यस्तूपस्यार्षं पवमानसोमदेवताकम् । नवमीदशम्यौ त्रिष्टुभौ । शिष्टा जगत्यः । तथा चानुक्रांतम् - ' इषुर्न हिरण्यस्तूपोऽंत्ये त्रिष्टुभौ ' इति । गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that the second sūkta, of ten ṛks, beginning इषुर्न (*iṣurna*), has as its seer Hiraṇyastūpa, of the Āṅgirasa family, and as its deity Pavamāna Soma. The ninth and the tenth ṛks are in the Triṣṭup metre; the rest are in Jagatī. He cites the Anukramaṇī: इषुर्न हिरण्यस्तूपोऽंत्ये त्रिष्टुभौ (*iṣurna hiraṇyastūpo 'ṃtye triṣṭubhau*). The application (viniyoga) has already been stated.

Translation.—This sūkta beginning इषुर्न (*iṣurna*) is the second sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It contains ten ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa; the deity is Pavamāna Soma; the ninth and the tenth ṛks of this sūkta are in the Triṣṭup metre. The remaining ṛks are in the Jagatī metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: इषुर्न हिरण्यस्तूपोऽन्ये त्रिष्टुभौ (*iṣurna hiraṇyastūpo 'nye triṣṭubhau*) **NOTE**. The application has been stated earlier.

### Printed p. 389

Maṇḍala 9; Anuvāka 4; Sūkta 69; Aṣṭaka 7, Adhyāya 2, Varga 21, 22. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 10. Ṛṣi: Hiraṇyastūpa. Devatā: Pavamāna Soma. Chandas: 1–8 Jagatī; 9–10 Triṣṭup.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इषु॒र्न धन्व॒न्प्रति॑ धीयते म॒तिर्व॒त्सो न मा॒तुरुप॑ स॒र्ज्यूध॑नि ।  
> उ॒रुधा॑रेव दुहे॒ अग्र॑ आय॒त्यस्य॑ व्र॒तेष्वपि॒ सोम॑ इष्यते ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इषुः । न । धन्वन् । प्रति । धीयते । मतिः । वत्सः । न । मातुः । उप । सर्जि । ऊधनि ।  
> उरुधाराऽइव । दुहे । अग्रे । आऽयती । अस्य । व्रतेषु । अपि । सोमः । इष्यते ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्मिन् पवमानरूप इंद्रे मतिः मननीयास्मदीया स्तुतिः प्रति धीयते अस्माभिर्निधीयते वा। दधाते रूपम्। तत्र दृष्टांतः । इषुर्न यथेषुः शरः धन्वन् धनुषि प्रति धीयते तद्वत् । किंच ऊधनि सर्वस्य पोषयितृत्वेनोधःस्थानीय इंद्रे सोमो मदार्थमस्माभिः उप सर्जि उपसृज्यते । कथमिव । मातुः गोः ऊधनि पयोधारके वत्सो न वत्सो यथा पयःपानार्थं सृज्यते तद्वत् । उरुधारेव बहुविधपयोधारा गौरिव अग्रे वत्सस्य पुरतः आयती गच्छंती सती पयः दुहे दुग्धे तथा सोऽयमिंद्रो वत्सभूतेभ्यः स्तोतृभ्यः पुरतो गच्छन् बहुविधान् कामान् दुग्धे। किंच अस्य एतादृशस्य व्रतेष्वपि सोम इष्यते यष्टृभिः प्रेर्यते खलु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains that in this Indra in the form of Pavamāna, our reflective praise (मतिः (*matiḥ*)) is directed and placed (प्रति धीयते (*prati dhīyate*)) by us. As an illustration he gives इषुर्न (*iṣurna*): just as an arrow is fixed on the bow. Further, in Indra, who is like an udder because he nourishes all, Soma is released by us for exhilaration (उप सर्जि (*upa sarji*)). How? As a calf is released to the udder of its mother, the cow, to drink milk. Like a cow with many streams of milk, who going before the calf yields her milk (दुहे (*duhe*)), so this Indra, going before the singers, who are like calves, yields many kinds of desired things. Further, in the sacrifices (व्रतेष्वपि (*vrateṣvapi*)) of such an Indra, Soma is indeed impelled by the sacrificers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- धन्वन् (*dhanvan*)—in the bow
- इषुः न (*iṣuḥ na*)—as an arrow is fixed
- मतिः (*matiḥ*)—our praise
- प्रति धीयते (*prati dhīyate*)—is attached to Indra
- मातुः (*mātuḥ*)—of the cow, the mother
- ऊधनि (*ūdhani*)—to the region of the udder

### Printed p. 390

- वत्सो न (*vatso na*)—as a calf is let go to drink milk
- ऊधनि (*ūdhani*)—to Indra, who nourishes all
- उपसर्जि (*upasarji*)—(for his satisfaction) Soma is released (offered)
- उरुधारा (*urudhārā*)—the cow that can pour out much milk in a stream
- अग्रे (*agre*)—before the calf
- आयती (*āyatī*)—while going
- दुहे इव (*duhe iva*)—as she yields milk in abundance (when Indra comes to the sacrificer, he pours out abundant wealth)
- अस्य (*asya*)—directed to this Indra
- व्रतेष्टपि (*vrateṣṭapi*)—in sacrifices and the like **NOTE**
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- इष्यते (*iṣyate*)—is offered

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As the arrow is fixed in the bow, our praise is attached to Indra. As the calf is let go to the region of the udder of its mother, the cow, to drink milk, so Soma is offered, for his satisfaction, to Indra, who nourishes all. As the cow that can pour out much milk in a stream yields milk in abundance while going before the calf, so Indra, when he comes to the sacrificer, pours out abundant wealth. In the sacrifices directed to this Indra, Soma is offered.

##### English translation
(Our) praise is attached (to Indra) as an arrow to the bow ; (the Soma-juice) is let loose to (Indra) the fosterer as a calf to the udder of its mother : (Indra sheds blessings) as a cow having a copious stream of milk yields it when coming into the presence (of the calf) : in Indra's sacrifices the Soma is stimulated.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उपो॑ म॒तिः पृ॒च्यते॑ सि॒च्यते॒ मधु॑ मं॒द्राज॑नी चोदते अं॒तरा॒सनि॑ ।  
> पव॑मानः संत॒निः प्र॑घ्न॒तामि॑व॒ मधु॑मांद्र॒प्सः परि॒ वार॑मर्षति ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उपो इति । मतिः । पृच्यते । सिच्यते । मधु । मंद्रऽअजनी । चोदते । अंतः । आसनि ।  
> पवमानः । सम्ऽतनिः । प्रघ्नताम्ऽइव । मधुऽमान् । द्रप्सः । परि । वारम् । अर्षति ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 391

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्मिन् पवमानरूप इंद्रे मतिः स्तुतिः उपो पृच्यते उपपृच्यते स्तोतृभिः संयोज्यते । ‘ पृची संपर्के'। तथा मधु मदकरः सोमः इंद्रार्थं सिच्यते अद्भिः यवसक्तुभिश्च सिक्तो भवति । ततश्च मंद्राजनी। अज गतिक्षेपणयोः' इत्यस्य ल्युटि ङीपि रूपम्। मदकरस्य रसस्य प्रेरयित्री सोमधारा तस्येंद्रस्य आसनि आस्ये अंतः मध्ये चोदते यष्टृभिः प्रेर्यते । आस्यशब्दस्य ‘ पद्दन्नोमास्°' इत्यादिना आसन्नित्यादेशः । किंच संतनिः ग्रहादिषु सम्यग्विस्तृतः मधुमान् मदकररसवान् पवमानः पूयमानः सोमः द्रप्सः द्रुतगमनशीलो यद्वा क्षिप्रंहननशीलः सन् वारम् अविवालमयं पवित्रं परितः अर्षति आगच्छति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । प्रघ्नतामिव । प्रकर्षेण हंतॄणां योद्धॄणां संतनिः सम्यग्विसृष्टः शरो यथा शीघ्रं प्राप्यमभितो गच्छति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains that in this Indra in the form of Pavamāna, praise (मतिः (*matiḥ*)) is joined (उपो पृच्यते (*upo pṛcyate*)) by the singers. Likewise मधु (*madhu*), the exhilarating Soma, is sprinkled (सिच्यते (*sicyate*)) for Indra with waters and with barley meal (यवसक्तुभिश्च (*yavasaktubhiśca*)). And then the Soma stream (मंद्राजनी (*maṃdrājanī*)), the impeller of the exhilarating juice, is driven by the sacrificers into the mouth (आसनि (*āsani*)) of that Indra, in the middle. Further, Soma, who is well spread out in the cups and the like (संतनिः (*saṃtaniḥ*)), rich in exhilarating juice (मधुमान् (*madhumān*)), being purified (पवमानः (*pavamānaḥ*)), swift-moving (द्रप्सः (*drapsaḥ*)) or else quickly smiting, goes around the filter made of sheep's wool (वारम् (*vāram*)). As an illustration he gives प्रघ्नतामिव (*praghnatāmiva*): as the arrow well discharged by warriors, who strike with force, goes swiftly all around to reach its object, so does Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मतिः (*matiḥ*)—the praise
- उपो पृच्यते (*upo pṛcyate*)—is joined with Indra
- मधु (*madhu*)—the exhilarating Soma
- सिच्यते (*sicyate*)—is sprinkled
- मंद्राजनी (*maṃdrājanī*)—the stream of Soma that gives delight
- आसनि अंतः (*āsani aṃtaḥ*)—in the middle of Indra's mouth
- चोदते (*codate*)—is offered
- प्रघ्नतां इव (*praghnatāṃ iva*)—as the arrow of warriors rushes swiftly forward
- संतॆनिः (*saṃtèniḥ*)—spread out in the vessels **NOTE**
- मधुमान् (*madhumān*)—tasty
- पवमानः (*pavamānaḥ*)—and purified, Soma
- द्रप्सः (*drapsaḥ*)—swift-moving
- वारं (*vāraṃ*)—the ten-fold filter
- परि अर्षति (*pari arṣati*)—goes around and reaches

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The praise is offered to Indra and is joined with him. The exhilarating Soma is sprinkled. The stream of Soma that gives delight is offered in the middle of Indra's mouth. As the arrow of warriors rushes swiftly forward, so Soma, spread out in the vessels and the like, tasty and purified, being swift-moving, goes around and reaches the ten-fold filter.

##### English translation
The praise is united (to Indra) ; the excellent (Soma) is sprinkled : (the Soma stream) emitting pleasant juice is driven into (Indra's) mouth : the filte-red **NOTE** diffused exhilarating swift-flowing (Soma) hastens to the fleece like the arrow of the combatants.

> हरिः । अक्रान् । यजतः । सम्ऽयतः । मदः । नृम्णा । शिशानः । महिषः । न । शोभते ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वधूयुः । वधूभूता वसतीवर्य एकधनासहिता आपः । तद्वान् सोमः अव्ये अवेः स्वभूते त्वचि चर्मणि परि पवते परितो वर्तते पूतो भवति वा । किंच नप्तीः नप्त्रीः । नप्तृशब्दश्चतुर्थापत्यवाची । सोमस्य नप्त्रीः । सोमो ह्योषधीनामग्रे रेतो निषिंचति । ‘प्रजापते रेतो देवा देवानां रेतो वर्षं वर्षस्य रेत ओषधयः' (ऐ. आ. २.१.३ ) इति श्रुतेः । यद्वा । नप्तृशब्दोऽपत्यवाची । तस्यापत्यानि । सोमः सुधामयैः स्वकिरणैरोषधीर्वर्धयति । तस्मादपत्यभूताः। अदितेः। पृथिवीनामैतत् । अदीनायाः पृथिव्या उत्पन्ना ओषधीः ऋतं सत्यरूपं यज्ञं यते गच्छते यजमानाय श्रथ्नीते अग्रभागे फलिनीः कर्तुं विश्लेषयति । किंच हरिः हरितवर्णः यजतः सर्वैर्यष्टव्यः अत एव संयतः ग्रहादिषु संगृहीतः मदः। माद्यत्यनेनेति मदः सोमः । तादृशः अक्रान् क्रामति । पात्रेष्ववतिष्ठते । यद्वा । शत्रूनतिक्रामति । क्रमेर्लुङि तिपि ‘बहुलं छंदसि' इति इडागमाभावाद्वृद्धौ कृतायां सिज्लोपे सति हल्ङ्यादिना तिपो लोपे ‘मो नो धातोः' इति नत्वे कृते रूपम् । अत एव सोमः नृम्णा स्वबलानि शिशानः तीक्ष्णीकुर्वन् । अथवा शत्रुबलानि तनूकुर्वन् । महिषो न । महन्नामैतत् । महानिव सर्वत्र व्याप्त इव शोभते स्वतेजसा सर्वत्र दीप्यते । यद्वा । नः संप्रत्यर्थे । इदानीमेवंगुणयुक्तो महान् सोमः शोभत इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains that वधूयुः (*vadhūyuḥ*) refers to the waters, in the form of brides, called Vasatīvarī, together with the Ekadhanā waters. Soma, who has them, is purified, or moves around, on the sheepskin (अव्ये (*avye*)), that is, on the hide (त्वचि (*tvaci*)) that belongs to the sheep. Further, नप्तीः (*naptīḥ*) means granddaughters, the Soma's granddaughters; the word नप्तृशब्दश्चतुर्थापत्यवाची (*naptṛśabdaścaturthāpatyavācī*). For Soma first sheds seed into the plants; he cites the śruti ‘प्रजापते रेतो देवा देवानां रेतो वर्षं वर्षस्य रेत ओषधयः' (*‘prajāpate reto devā devānāṃ reto varṣaṃ varṣasya reta oṣadhayaḥ '*) (Ai. Ā. 2.1.3) **GLOSS**. Or else, the word नप्तृ (*naptṛ*) denotes offspring: Soma makes the plants grow with his nectar-filled rays, and therefore they are his offspring. अदितेः (*aditeḥ*) is a name of the earth: the plants, born of the earth that is never poor, go to the sacrifice (यते (*yate*)) of truthful nature (ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)) for the sacrificer, and Soma loosens them (श्रथ्नीते (*śrathnīte*)) in order to make them bear fruit at the front end. Further, हरिः (*hariḥ*) is green-coloured; यजतः (*yajataḥ*) is to be worshipped by all; and therefore संयतः (*saṃyataḥ*) is held in the cups and the like; मदः (*madaḥ*) is Soma, because one is exhilarated by him. Such a Soma अक्रान् (*akrān*) steps forth, that is, stays in the vessels; or else he overcomes the enemies. Therefore Soma, sharpening (शिशानः (*śiśānaḥ*)) his own powers (नृम्णा (*nṛmṇā*)), or else weakening the powers of the enemies, shines like the great one (महिषो न (*mahiṣo na*); महिष (*mahiṣa*) is a name for the great), as if pervading everywhere, blazing everywhere with his own splendour. Or else, नः (*naḥ*) is used in the sense of "now": now the great Soma, endowed with such qualities, shines.

- वधूयुः (*vadhūyuḥ*)—Soma, who desires the bride in the form of Vasatīvarī
- अव्ये (*avye*)—of the sheep
- त्वचि (*tvaci*)—on the hide
- परि पवते (*pari pavate*)—becomes purified
- ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)—the sacrifice of truthful nature
- यते (*yate*)—for the benefit of the sacrificer who performs it
- नप्रीतिः (*naprītiḥ*)—his own daughters **NOTE**
- अदितेः (*aditeḥ*)—the plants born on the earth
- श्रद्धीते (*śraddhīte*)—he separates, as if to let the fruits go **NOTE**
- हरिः (*hariḥ*)—of green colour
- यजतः (*yajataḥ*)—worthy of worship
- संयतः (*saṃyataḥ*)—collected
- मदः (*madaḥ*)—the exhilarating Soma
- अक्रान् (*akrān*)—he occupies the vessels

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma, who desires the bride in the form of Vasatīvarī, becomes purified on the hide of the sheep. For the benefit of the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice of truthful nature, he separates the plants, his own daughters, born on the earth, as if to let the fruits go. Soma, green in colour, worthy of worship, collected and exhilarating, occupies the vessels. Sharpening his own powers, he shines like a great one.

##### English translation
(Soma) seeking his spouse is filtered in the sheepskin ; he separates his grand-daughters on the earth for the sacrificer : green-tinted, adorable, colle- cted **NOTE** (in the ladles) exhilarating, he overcomes (his foes) ; sharpening his vigour he shines like one of might.

### Printed p. 394

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उक्षा रेतसः सेक्ता वृषभः पुरतः मिमाति शब्दायते । 'माङ् माने शब्दे च ' । तं वृषभं धेनवः गावः प्रति यंति अनुगच्छंति । तथा देवस्य द्योतमानस्य निष्कृतं संस्कृतं स्थानं देवीः देव्यः उप यंति उपगच्छंति । अनेनार्धेन सोमस्तुतिश्चाभिधीयते । सोमः सन् द्रोणकलशाभिगमनकाले शब्दं करोति। तमनु धेनवः प्रीणयित्र्यः स्तुतयः पारियंति देवस्य स्थानं स्तुतयोऽभिगच्छंति । तथा सोऽयं सोमः अर्जुनं श्वेतवर्णम् अव्ययम् अविमयमविस्वभूतं वारं वालं पवित्रम् अत्यक्रमीत् अतिक्रामति । अतिक्रम्य पात्राणि गच्छतीत्यर्थः । किंच सोमः अत्कं न आत्मीयं कवचमिव निक्तम् उज्ज्वलं श्रयणद्रव्यं परि अव्यत परितः संवृणोति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains that the bull (उक्षा (*ukṣā*)), the sprinkler of seed, lows (मिमाति (*mimāti*)) in front; the cows follow that bull (प्रति यंति (*prati yaṃti*)). Likewise the goddesses go up to the refined place (निष्कृतं (*niṣkṛtaṃ*)) of the shining god. By this half-verse the praise of Soma is also stated: Soma makes a sound at the time of going to the Droṇa vessel; after him the pleasing praises, the cows (धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*)), go to the place of the god. Likewise this Soma crosses over (अत्यक्रमीत् (*atyakramīt*)) the white (अर्जुनं (*arjunaṃ*)) filter (वारं (*vāraṃ*)) made of sheep's wool (अव्ययम् (*avyayam*)); having crossed it, he goes to the vessels. Further, Soma covers himself all around (परि अव्यत (*pari avyata*)) with the shining admixture (श्रयणद्रव्यं (*śrayaṇadravyaṃ*)), as with his own armour (अत्कं न (*atkaṃ na*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उक्षा (*ukṣā*)—the bull
- मिमाति (*mimāti*)—makes a sound
- धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*)—the cows
- प्रति यंति (*prati yaṃti*)—follow around it
- देवस्य (*devasya*)—of Soma, who is the deity
- निष्कृतं (*niṣkṛtaṃ*)—the well-refined place
- देवीः (*devīḥ*)—the shining praises
- उपयंति (*upayaṃti*)—approach
- अव्ययं (*avyayaṃ*)—of wool
- अर्जुनं (*arjunaṃ*)—white
- वारं (*vāraṃ*)—the threads of the ten-fold filter
- अत्यक्रमित् (*atyakramit*)—having crossed over, Soma enters the vessels **NOTE**
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- अत्कं न (*atkaṃ na*)—as one puts on armour
- निकतं (*nikataṃ*)—the shining admixture **NOTE**
- परि अव्यत (*pari avyata*)—he takes to himself

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As cows follow around the bull when it makes a sound, the shining praises approach the well-refined place of Soma, who is the deity. Having crossed the white threads of the ten-fold filter of wool, Soma enters the vessels. As one puts on armour, Soma takes to himself the shining admixture.

##### English translation
The bull lows, the cows flock around him : the divine (praises) gather round the station of the radiant (Soma) : Soma passes through the white sheep-skin ; he clothes himself with it as it were with a burnished armour.

### Printed p. 395

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अमृ॑क्तेन॒ रुश॑ता॒ वास॑सा॒ हरि॒रम॑र्त्यो निर्णिजा॒नः परि॑ व्यत ।  
> दि॒वस्पृ॒ष्ठं ब॒र्हणा॑ नि॒र्णिजे॑ कृतोप॒स्तर॑णं च॒म्वो॑र्नभ॒स्मय॑म् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अमृक्तेन । रुशता । वाससा । हरिः । अमर्त्यः । निःऽनिजानः । परि । व्यत ।  
> दिवः । पृष्ठम् । बर्हणा । निःऽनिजे । कृत । उपऽस्तरणम् । चम्वोः । नभस्मयम् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अमर्त्यः मनुष्यधर्मरहितः हरिः हरितवर्णः सोमः निर्णिजानः उदकेन शोध्यमानः सन् अमृक्तेन । ‘मृजी शौचालंकारयोः' । अनिर्णिक्तेनापि रुशता स्वतः शुक्लवर्णेन पयोरूपेण वाससा परि व्यत परित आच्छादयति । सोमे परिपूते गव्येन पयसा मिश्रीकुर्वंति खलु । तदुच्यते । ततः सोऽयं सोमः दिवः द्युलोकस्य पृष्ठं पृष्ठभागे तिष्ठंतमादित्यं बर्हणा बर्हणाय पापानामुद्यमनकारिणे पापनाशिने निर्निजे निर्नेजनाय परिपवनाय कृत द्युलोकेऽकार्षीत् । स हि स्वदीप्त्या सर्वं निर्णेक्ति । कृत । कृणोतेर्लुङि ‘ह्रस्वात्' इति सिचो लोपः । तदेवाह । चम्वोः । द्यावापृथिवीनामैतत् । चमंति भक्षयंत्यत्र देवा मनुष्या इति । तयोः उपस्तरणम् आच्छादनशीलं नभस्मयम् आदित्यमयमादित्यस्य स्वभूतं तेजश्च सर्वेषां निर्णेजनाय अकार्षीत् ॥ ॥ २१ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains that Soma, free from human qualities (अमर्त्यः (*amartyaḥ*)), of green hue (हरिः (*hariḥ*)), while being cleansed with water (निर्णिजानः (*nirṇijānaḥ*)), covers himself all around (परि व्यत (*pari vyata*)) with a garment (वाससा (*vāsasā*)) in the form of milk, which is uncleansed (अमृक्तेन (*amṛktena*)), shining (रुशता (*ruśatā*)), and naturally white. For when Soma has been purified, they mix it with cow's milk; that is what is said. Then this Soma made (कृत (*kṛta*)), in the heavenly world, the Āditya who stands on the back (पृष्ठं (*pṛṣṭhaṃ*)) of the heavenly world (दिवः (*divaḥ*)) for destruction (बर्हणा (*barhaṇā*)), that is, for the one who uproots sins, the destroyer of sin, and for cleansing (निर्निजे (*nirnije*)), for purification; for the Āditya cleanses everything by his own radiance. That is what he says: चम्वोः (*camvoḥ*) is a name of Heaven and Earth, because gods and men eat in them (चमंति भक्षयंत्यत्र देवा मनुष्या इति (*camaṃti bhakṣayaṃtyatra devā manuṣyā iti*)). The covering (उपस्तरणम् (*upastaraṇam*)) of these two, which has the nature of covering, made of the Āditya (नभस्मयम् (*nabhasmayam*)), that is, the Āditya's own brilliance, he made for the cleansing of all.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अमर्त्यः (*amartyaḥ*)—free from the nature of death
- हरिः (*hariḥ*)—of green colour; Soma
- निर्णिजानः (*nirṇijānaḥ*)—though he has attained purity
- अमृक्तेन (*amṛktena*)—that has not been refined
- रुशता (*ruśatā*)—and is white
- वाससा (*vāsasā*)—with a garment in the form of milk
- परिव्यत (*parivyata*)—he is covered
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the atmosphere
- पृष्ठं (*pṛṣṭhaṃ*)—the Āditya who is on the back
- बर्हणा (*barhaṇā*)—for the destruction of the world's sins
- निर्निजे (*nirnije*)—and for the purification of the world
- कृत (*kṛta*)—he created
- चन्नोः (*cannoḥ*)—both Heaven and Earth **NOTE**
- उपस्तरणं (*upastaraṇaṃ*)—that covers (surrounds)
- नभस्मयं (*nabhasmayaṃ*)—he created the brilliance of the Āditya

### Printed p. 396

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma, free from the nature of death and of green colour, though he has attained purity, is covered with a garment in the form of milk, which is not refined and is white. He created the Āditya, who is on the back of the atmosphere, for the destruction of the world's sins and for the purification of the world. He also created the brilliance of the Āditya, which covers both Heaven and Earth.

##### English translation
The immortal green-tinted Soma when purified is arranged in an uncleansed shining vestment; he has created (Aditya) who stands on the back of the sky for the destruction (of sin) and purification, (and has created) Aditya's brilliance, the cover of the two worlds.

> तंतुम् । ततम् । परि । सर्गासः । आशवः । न । इंद्रात् । ऋते । पवते । धाम । किम् । चन ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सूर्यस्य रश्मयः सर्वस्य प्रेरकस्य सुवीर्यस्य वादित्यस्य रश्मयः सर्वतो व्यापकाः किरणाः इव द्रावयित्नवः सर्वत्रद्रवणशीलाः मत्सरासः मदकराः प्रसुपः शत्रूणां प्रस्वापका हंतारः आशवः ग्रहेषु चमसेषु च व्याप्ताः सर्गासः सृज्यमानाः सोमाः ततं विस्तृतं तंतुं तंतुभिः कृतं वस्त्रं साकं सह युगपत् परि ईरते परितो गच्छंति । ते सोमाः इंद्रादृते इंद्रं वर्जयित्वा अन्यत् किं चन धाम देवशरीरं लक्षीकृत्य न पवते न गच्छति। एकवचनं छांदसम् । न गच्छंति । किंत्विंद्रस्यैव धाम प्रति गच्छंति । इंद्रस्य धाम्नो यष्टव्यत्वं च ' अयाळिंद्रस्य प्रिया धामानि ' (वा. सं. २१.४७ ) इति मंत्रवर्णादवगम्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains that the Soma-juices (सर्गासः (*sargāsaḥ*), those being let flow), which are ever-running (द्रावयित्नवः (*drāvayitnavaḥ*)), exhilarating (मत्सरासः (*matsarāsaḥ*)), lulling the enemies to sleep, that is, slaying them (प्रसुपः (*prasupaḥ*)), and pervading the cups and the ladles (आशवः (*āśavaḥ*); ग्रहेषु चमसेषु च (*graheṣu camaseṣu ca*)), go (परि ईरते (*pari īrate*)) all around, together and at once, the extended (ततं (*tataṃ*)) cloth made of threads (तंतुं (*taṃtuṃ*)), like the rays (रश्मयः (*raśmayaḥ*)) of Sūrya, who is the impeller of all, or of good vigour, that is, the Āditya, rays that spread in every direction. Those Soma-juices, except Indra (इंद्रादृते (*iṃdrādṛte*)), do not go aiming at any other abode (धाम (*dhāma*)), that is, the body of a god; the singular is Vedic usage. They go only to Indra's abode. That Indra's abode is to be worshipped is known from the Vedic text अयाळिंद्रस्य प्रिया धामानि (*ayāḷiṃdrasya priyā dhāmāni*) (Vā. Saṃ. 21.47) **GLOSS**.

- द्रावयित्सवः (*drāvayitsavaḥ*)—those of spreading nature **NOTE**
- मत्सरासः (*matsarāsaḥ*)—the exhilarating
- प्रसुपः (*prasupaḥ*)—the destroyers of enemies
- आशवः (*āśavaḥ*)—the swift-going
- सर्गासः (*sargāsaḥ*)—the Soma-juices offered for the sacrifice
- ततं (*tataṃ*)—extended
- तंतुं (*taṃtuṃ*)—on the cloth made of thread
- सूरस्य रश्मय इव (*sūrasya raśmaya iva*)—like the rays of the sun **NOTE**
- साकं (*sākaṃ*)—together
- परि (*pari*)—all around
- ईरते (*īrate*)—they spread
- इंद्रादृते (*iṃdrādṛte*)—except Indra
- किं चन धाम (*kiṃ cana dhāma*)—to any other region
- न पवते (*na pavate*)—Soma does not enter

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Soma-juices, which are of spreading nature, exhilarating, destroyers of enemies, swift-going and offered for the sacrifice, spread together all around over the extended cloth made of thread, like the rays of the sun. Apart from Indra, this Soma does not enter any other region.

##### English translation
The rushing exhilarating foe-slaying Soma-juices when let loose flow together round the extended cloth like the son's rays **NOTE** : they flow to no other person except, Indra.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सिंधो॑रिव प्रव॒णे नि॒म्न आ॒शवो॒ वृष॑च्युता॒ मदा॑सो गा॒तुमा॑शत ।  
> शं नो॑ निवे॒शे द्वि॒पदे॒ चतु॑ष्पदे॒ऽस्मे वाजाः॑ सोम तिष्ठंतु कृ॒ष्टयः॑ ॥ ७ ॥

### Printed p. 398

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सिंधोःऽइव । प्रवणे । निम्ने । आशवः । वृषऽच्युताः । मदासः । गातुम् । आशत ।  
> शम् । नः । निऽवेशे । द्विऽपदे । चतुःऽपदे । अस्मे इति । वाजाः । सोम । तिष्ठंतु । कृष्टयः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वृषच्युताः । वृष हिंसासंक्लेशनदानेष्वपि । वृषभिः सोमस्य दातृभिर्ऋत्विग्भिश्युनदताः परिस्रुताः मदासः मदकारिणः सोमाः स्तुतिभिः प्राप्तव्य इंद्रे गातुं गमनम् आशत प्राप्नुवंति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । सिंधोरिव प्रवणे । प्रगच्छंत्युदकानि यत्रेति तत्प्रवणम् । तस्मिन् निम्ने स्थले सिंधोर्नद्याः आशवः व्याप्ता आपो यथा गच्छंति तद्वत् । अथ प्रत्यक्षः। हे सोम नः अस्माकं निवेशे स्वगृहं प्रति प्रवेशने निर्गमने वा द्विपदे पुत्रादिकाय चतुष्पदे गवादिकाय पशवे शं सुखं कुरु । किंच हे सोम अस्मे अस्मासु वाजाः अन्नानि कृष्टयः पुत्रादिकाः प्रजाश्च तिष्ठंतु । अन्नादिकं देहीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains that वृषच्युताः (*vṛṣacyutāḥ*) are the exhilarating (मदासः (*madāsaḥ*)) Soma-juices poured forth (परिस्रुताः (*parisrutāḥ*)) by the bulls, that is, by the priests who give Soma **NOTE**. They find the way (गातुं गमनम् आशत (*gātuṃ gamanam āśata*)) to Indra, who is to be reached by praises. As an illustration he gives सिंधोरिव प्रवणे (*siṃdhoriva pravaṇe*): प्रवण (*pravaṇa*) is the place to which waters flow; as the pervading (आशवः (*āśavaḥ*)) waters of a river go to that low ground, so the juices go. Now he addresses Soma directly: O Soma, make happiness (शं (*śaṃ*)) for our two-footed creatures, sons and the like, and our four-footed creatures, cows and the like, at our entering (निवेशे (*niveśe*)) our own house or going out of it. Further, O Soma, let food (वाजाः (*vājāḥ*)) and offspring (कृष्टयः (*kṛṣṭayaḥ*)), sons and the like, abide in us (अस्मे (*asme*)); that is, give us food and the like.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आशवः (*āśavaḥ*)—swift-going
- सिंधोः (*siṃdhoḥ*)—the streams of the river
- प्रवणे (*pravaṇe*)—that are the support of the water
- निम्मे इव (*nimme iva*)—as they flow to low-lying regions **NOTE**
- वृषच्युताः (*vṛṣacyutāḥ*)—offered by the priests
- मदासः (*madāsaḥ*)—and exhilarating, the Soma-juices
- गातुं (*gātuṃ*)—to Indra, who is their place of support
- अशत (*aśata*)—they go and reach **NOTE**
- सोम (*soma*)—O god Soma
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- निवेशे (*niveśe*)—entering the house
- द्विपदे (*dvipade*)—to sons and the like
- चतुष्पदे (*catuṣpade*)—and to cattle
- शं (*śaṃ*)—bring happiness
- अस्मे (*asme*)—in us
- वाजाः (*vājāḥ*)—food
- कृष्टयः (*kṛṣṭayaḥ*)—and offspring such as sons
- तिष्ठंतु (*tiṣṭhaṃtu*)—let them be established

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As the swift streams of a river flow to the low-lying regions that are the support of the water, the exhilarating Soma-juices offered by the priests go and reach Indra, who is their place of support. O god Soma, bring happiness to the sons and the like, and to the cattle, that enter our house. Let food and offspring such as sons be established in us.

##### English translation
The exhilarating (Soma-juices) poured forth by the sprinklers effect their way to Indra as in a waterfall of a river the pervading (waters find their

### Printed p. 399

way) to dry ground ; bless on our return our two-footed and four-footed things ; may food and offspring ever abide with us.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ नः॑ पवस्व॒ वसु॑म॒द्धिर॑ण्यव॒दश्वा॑व॒द्गोम॒द्यव॑मत्सु॒वीर्य॑म् ।  
> यू॒यं हि सो॑म पि॒तरो॒ मम॒ स्थन॑ दि॒वो मू॒र्धानः॒ प्रस्थि॑ता वय॒स्कृतः॑ ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । नः । पवस्व । वसुऽमत् । हिरण्यऽवत् । अश्वऽवत् । गोऽमत् । यवऽमत् । सुऽवीर्यम् ।  
> यूयम् । हि । सोम । पितरः । मम । स्थन । दिवः । मूर्धानः । प्रऽस्थिताः । वयःऽकृतः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम त्वं वसुमत् वसुयुक्तं हिरण्यवत् कनकादिसहितम् अश्ववत् गोमत् गवाश्वसहितं यवमत् । यवो नाम धान्यविशेषः। धान्यविशिष्टं सुवीर्यं शोभनवीर्योपेतं धनं नः अस्मभ्यम् आ पवस्व आप्रापय । प्रयच्छेति यावत् । किंच हे सोम यतस्त्वं मम पितॄणामंगिरसामपि पितासि ततो यूयम् एव मम पितरः स्थन भवथ । पितृबहुत्वमत्र सोमस्याभिधीयते । कीदृशाः । दिवः द्युलोकस्य मूर्धानः मूर्धवदुच्छ्रिताः । कर्मभिः स्वर्गादिकमलभंतेत्यर्थः । प्रस्थिताः सर्वदा कर्मकरणार्थं स्थिताः वयस्कृतः हवीरूपस्यान्नस्य कर्तारः । तादृशा मम पितरस्त्वं भवसि । ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses Soma: bestow (आ पवस्व (*ā pavasva*)), that is, give, to us wealth that is endowed with treasures (वसुमत् (*vasumat*)), with gold and the like (हिरण्यवत् (*hiraṇyavat*)), with horses (अश्ववत् (*aśvavat*)), with cows (गोमत् (*gomat*)) and with barley (यवमत् (*yavamat*); यवो नाम धान्यविशेषः (*yavo nāma dhānyaviśeṣaḥ*), barley is a particular grain, so, endowed with grain), and endowed with good vigour (सुवीर्यं (*suvīryaṃ*)). Further, O Soma, since you are the father even of my fathers, the Aṅgirases, you yourselves are my fathers (स्थन (*sthana*), you are); the plurality of fathers is here said of Soma. What are they like? They are heads (मूर्धानः (*mūrdhānaḥ*)) of the heavenly world (दिवः (*divaḥ*)), raised like a head; by rites they obtain heaven and the like. They are प्रस्थिताः (*prasthitāḥ*), always standing ready to perform rites, and वयस्कृतः (*vayaskṛtaḥ*), makers of the food in the form of oblation. Such are my fathers; such you are.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

**NOTE**

- वसुमत् (*vasumat*)—(O god Soma) endowed with wealth
- हिरण्यवत् (*hiraṇyavat*)—filled with gold
- अश्ववत् (*aśvavat*)—endowed with horses
- गोमत् (*gomat*)—accompanied by cows
- यवमत् (*yavamat*)—endowed with barley grain
- सुवीरं (*suvīraṃ*)—the wealth endowed with excellent vigour **NOTE**
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- आपवस्व (*āpavasva*)—provide
- सोम (*soma*)—O god Soma
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the heavenly world

### Printed p. 400

- मूर्धानः (*mūrdhānaḥ*)—those who are like the head
- प्रस्थिताः (*prasthitāḥ*)—engaged in rites
- वयस्सतः (*vayassataḥ*)—those who offer oblation **NOTE**
- मम पितरः (*mama pitaraḥ*)—in the form of our fathers
- यूयं हि स्थान (*yūyaṃ hi sthāna*)—you yourself are **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O god Soma, provide us with wealth that is endowed with riches, filled with gold, endowed with horses, accompanied by cows, endowed with barley grain, and endowed with excellent vigour. O god Soma, you yourself are, in the form of our fathers, those who are like the head of the heavenly world, engaged in rites, offerers of oblation.

##### English translation
Pour upon us (wealth), comprising treasure, gold, horses, cattle, barley, and excellent male offspring; you Soma, are my progenitors, the chiefs of heaven, placed (for sacrifices), the offerers of oblation.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒ते सोमाः॒ पव॑मानास॒ इंद्रं॒ रथा॑ इव॒ प्र य॑युः सा॒तिमच्छ॑ ।  
> सु॒ताः प॒वित्र॒मति॑ यं॒त्यव्यं॑ हि॒त्वी व॒व्रिं ह॒रितो॑ वृ॒ष्टिमच्छ॑ ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एते । सोमाः । पवमानासः । इंद्रम् । रथाःऽइव । प्र । ययुः । सातिम् । अच्छ ।  
> सुताः । पवित्रम् । अति । यंति । अव्यम् । हित्वी । वव्रिम् । हरितः । वृष्टिम् । अच्छ ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पवमानासः पवित्रेण पूयमानाः एते अस्मदीयाः सोमाः सातिम् । ‘षण संभक्तौ । कर्मणि क्तिन् । सर्वैः संभजनीयम् इंद्रम् अच्छ प्र ययुः प्रकर्षेण गच्छंति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । रथाइव । इंद्रस्य रथा यथा सातिम् । ‘षो अंतकर्मणि' । ऊतियूति' इत्यादिना निपातितः । सीयते म्रियतेऽस्मिन्निति सातिः संग्रामः । तमच्छ तं प्रति प्रगच्छंति तद्वत् । किंच सुताः ग्रावभिरभिषुताः सोमाः अव्यम् अविवालभवं पवित्रम् अति यंति अतीत्य गच्छंति । तेऽमी हरितः हरितवर्णा अश्वाः । यद्वा । हरितस्त आदित्यवाहनरूपा अश्वा भूत्वा । वव्रिम् । वृणोति शरीरमिति वव्रिर्जरा । ‘ आदृगमहन' इति किप्रत्ययः । सर्वांगव्यापिनीं जरां हित्वी हित्वा तरुणाः संतः वृष्टिमच्छ वृष्टिं गमयितुं गच्छंति । हित्वी। ‘जहातेश्च क्त्वि' (पा. सू. ७.४. ४३ ) इति ह्यादेशः । ‘ स्नात्व्यादयश्च' इति छंदसि निपातितम् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains that these Soma-juices of ours, being purified with the filter (पवमानासः (*pavamānāsaḥ*)), go forth (प्र ययुः (*pra yayuḥ*)) with force towards Indra, who is to be shared by all (सातिम् (*sātim*)). As an illustration he gives रथाइव (*rathāiva*): as the chariots of Indra go towards the battle (सातिम् (*sātim*): the place where one is killed, a battle). Further, the Soma-juices, pressed (सुताः (*sutāḥ*)) with the stones, go beyond (अति यंति (*ati yaṃti*)) the filter (अव्यम् (*avyam*)) made of sheep's wool. They are the green-coloured horses (हरितः (*haritaḥ*)); or else, having become horses that carry the Āditya, they leave behind old age (वव्रिम् (*vavrim*) means old age, because it covers the body), which pervades all the limbs, and, having become young, go to bring about the rain (वृष्टिमच्छ (*vṛṣṭimaccha*)).
